name: Telur Masak Kicap Gaya Makcik Kantin
ingredients: Cooking oil, enough to submerge the eggs
1 ladle of the oil used to fry the eggs
1/4 cup sweet soy sauce (or as needed for the gravy)
Red and green bird's eye chillies, roughly sliced (about 6)
A little Chinese celery, roughly chopped (or spring onion)
instructions: 1. Crack an egg into a small bowl. Heat plenty of oil in a wok until very hot and slightly smoking. Fry the eggs one at a time; spoon hot oil over the top if needed and do not flip, so the yolks remain runny. Remove when the edges are crisp and drain. 2. Heat one ladle of the egg-frying oil in the wok. Sauté shallots, garlic and ginger until softened and fragrant. 3. Add blended chilli and fry until cooked and crisp. 4. Add the tomato and stir. 5. Add chilli sauce and oyster sauce. Stir in sweet soy sauce and tamarind water, then simmer. 6. Add sugar, a pinch of salt and white pepper if desired. Taste and adjust. Add onion rings and stir for about 15 seconds so they soften but remain crisp. 7. Arrange the fried eggs in the gravy just before serving and spoon gravy over them. Garnish with sliced chillies and Chinese celery. Serve hot with rice.

name: Kari Ayam Pecah Minyak & Kuah Merah
ingredients: A little water to mix the spice paste
Extra water for the first and second additions, as needed
instructions: 1. Prepare the cinnamon, star anise, cloves, cardamom and curry leaves. Thinly slice half an onion. 2. Mix the curry powder, chilli powder and optional blended chilli with a little water to make a paste. 3. Roughly chop the shallots, garlic and ginger, then blend with a little water. Cut the chicken and quarter the potatoes. 4. Heat the oil in a heavy-bottomed wok. Fry the whole spices, curry leaves and sliced onion until softened and lightly golden. 5. Add the blended ingredients and cook until the moisture evaporates and the mixture turns lightly golden. 6. Add the spice paste and fry until the oil separates. Add water in two stages, frying until the oil separates after each addition. 7. Add chicken and stir for 4-5 minutes. Add potatoes, cover and cook for 5-10 minutes. 8. Add tamarind water, salt and coconut milk. Add hot water as needed and simmer uncovered over medium-low heat until the chicken and potatoes are cooked and red oil rises to the surface. 9. Taste and adjust seasoning. Turn off the heat while the gravy is still moderately loose and rest for 10-15 minutes to thicken slightly. Serve hot.

name: Sambal Sotong Lembut Tak Liat (Pekat Bersalut)
ingredients: 1 large shallot, roughly sliced for frying
A little thick tamarind water, to taste
1 tsp salt for cleaning the squid
15-20 dried chillies, boiled until soft and deseeded
instructions: 1. Boil the dried chillies until soft and remove the seeds. Blend with the small shallots, large shallot, garlic and ginger, using only a little water. 2. Clean the squid by removing the innards, ink sac and digestive tract. Remove the skin if desired, and remove the beak. Cut the squid tubes into thick rings about 1 inch wide. 3. Rub the squid with 1 tsp salt for 30-60 seconds, rinse until the foam disappears, then drain thoroughly. 4. Heat the oil. Fry the bruised lemongrass and roughly sliced shallot until fragrant and softened. 5. Add the blended paste and cook over medium heat until thick and the oil separates. Add a little water if needed. 6. Add oyster sauce, tamarind water, palm sugar and sweet soy sauce. Cook until the sambal is thick and season with salt. 7. Pour hot water over the drained squid and leave for 1 minute only. Drain immediately. 8. Add the squid to the thick sambal and toss quickly to coat. Add onion rings, stir just until slightly softened, then turn off the heat.

name: Nasi Lemak Rice Cooker Tak Keras Bila Sejuk
instructions: 1. Measure 3 cups of rice. Wash and rinse several times until the water is fairly clear. 2. Drain the rice in a strainer so excess washing water is removed. 3. Put the rice into the rice cooker inner pot. 4. Pour in 1 cup coconut milk and 3.2 cups water. 5. Add ginger, knotted pandan leaves, salt and sugar. 6. Add cooking oil and stir gently to combine. 7. Select the White Rice setting and start the cooker. 8. When the rice is cooked, fluff it gently from the bottom upwards. Serve with sambal, boiled eggs, anchovies and cucumber.

name: Sambal Tumis Udang Petai Pekat & Wangi
ingredients: 1 onion, sliced into rings for garnish
A little water or oil for blending
A pinch of salt for the prawns
instructions: 1. Clean the prawns, remove the sharp tips and the dark vein, then season with a pinch of salt. 2. Blend the large shallot, garlic, dried chillies and ginger with a little water or oil. 3. Heat a little oil and briefly fry the prawns until half-cooked. Remove and set aside. 4. Briefly fry the petai in the same oil, then remove. 5. Add cooking oil and sauté the sliced onion until soft and lightly golden. 6. Add the blended paste and cook over medium heat until the chilli is fully cooked and the oil separates. 7. Add tomato and cook until it softens into the sambal. 8. Season with palm sugar, oyster sauce, seasoning powder and salt. Cook until thick and dark red. 9. Return the prawns and petai to the wok and add the onion rings. Toss until combined and the onion softens slightly. Turn off the heat and serve.

name: Sup Ayam Pekat Rempah Sendiri
ingredients: 1 tbsp fennel seeds or ground fennel
instructions: 1. Cut the carrot into large pieces. Separate the stems and leaves of the Chinese celery, and slice the spring onion. 2. Roughly slice the onion, garlic and ginger. 3. Combine the coriander, fennel, cumin and black pepper. Blend the spice mixture with the onion, garlic and ginger, adding water until smooth. 4. Heat a little oil in a pot. Fry the cinnamon, star anise, cardamom and cloves. 5. Add the blended mixture, then add the chicken and stir until it tightens slightly. 6. Add water and the celery stems. Simmer briefly. 7. Add carrot and simmer until tender. 8. Add potatoes, chicken stock cube, white pepper, salt, tomato and half the celery leaves. Turn off the heat when cooked. 9. Squeeze in a little lime juice and garnish with spring onion and fried shallots.

name: Ayam Masak Merah Raya Special
ingredients: 1 large onion, sliced for frying and garnish
instructions: 1. Roughly slice the onion for frying. Roughly chop the shallots, onion, garlic and ginger. Boil and deseed the dried chillies. Roughly chop the tomatoes and blend the shallots, onion, garlic, ginger and chillies until smooth. Bruise the lemongrass. 2. Coat the chicken with salt and turmeric. Fry until half-cooked, then remove and set aside. 3. Fry the lemongrass until fragrant. Add sliced onion, the whole spices and pandan leaf; sauté until fragrant. 4. Add the blended paste and cook until the oil rises. Add tomato and stir. 5. Add chilli sauce, oyster sauce and seasoning powder. When the gravy thickens and darkens, add palm sugar. 6. After about 10 minutes, add the fried chicken and coat well with the gravy. Cover briefly and cook until the chicken is fully cooked through. 7. Add green peas and cook until tender. Garnish with sliced onion and Chinese celery. Turn off the heat when the onion softens.

name: Bihun Goreng Kicap
instructions: 1. Crush and finely slice the garlic. Halve the fish balls. Wash the mustard greens, separate the stems and leaves, and roughly chop them. Roughly chop the cabbage and chicken. Slice spring onion and red chilli for garnish; slice bird's eye chilli if using. 2. Soak the vermicelli for about 15 minutes until soft, then drain. 3. Heat oil and sauté the garlic. When golden, add blended chilli and fry until cooked. 4. Add chicken and cook until half-done. Add oyster sauce, fish balls, light and sweet soy sauces; stir well. 5. Add the chicken stock cube, white pepper, mustard stems and sesame oil. Add the vermicelli and combine. 6. Add a little water gradually until the vermicelli is soft. Adjust the colour with more caramel and sweet soy sauce if needed; season with salt. 7. Add cabbage and cook until it wilts, then add mustard leaves and cook just until wilted. Garnish with red chilli and spring onion. Serve with sliced bird's eye chilli and light soy sauce if desired.

name: Rendang Ayam Dendang Perantau
instructions: 1. Blend the fresh ingredients until smooth. Dry-roast the coriander, cumin and fennel seeds, then grind them finely. 2. Heat the oil and sauté the whole spice mix with the blended ingredients until darker and the oil separates. 3. Add the chicken, ground roasted spices, tamarind pieces and thin coconut milk. 4. Cook until the chicken is tender and the liquid has reduced. 5. Add thick coconut milk, kerisik, kaffir lime leaves with the centre ribs removed, salt and palm sugar. 6. Continue cooking until the rendang gravy is fairly dry. 7. Sprinkle in finely sliced turmeric leaves and serve.

name: Set Ayam Goreng Kunyit
ingredients: A small bowl of sliced chicken meat
instructions: 1. Cut the chicken meat into small pieces. Marinate with salt, turmeric, white pepper, curry powder, optional coriander powder and cornflour. 2. Slice the Holland onion and carrot, roughly slice the red chilli, cut the long beans lengthwise and roughly chop the garlic. 3. Heat oil and fry the chicken until lightly golden and half-cooked, stirring regularly. Add garlic; when golden, add the vegetables and stir just until wilted. Remove. 4. For the soup, roughly slice shallots, garlic and ginger, then blend coarsely. Peel and cut carrot and potato into large pieces. Slice Chinese celery and spring onion. 5. Heat a pot with a little oil and sauté the blended ingredients until fragrant and lightly golden. Add the soup spice sachet and chicken bones. Add water, cover and simmer until boiling. Add potato and carrot, then chicken stock cube, black pepper, white pepper and salt. Cook until tender and garnish with Chinese celery and spring onion. 6. For the sambal belacan, roughly slice red chillies, bird's eye chillies and tomato. Blend with toasted belacan without adding water. Season with salt, sugar and calamansi juice.

name: Kuey Teow Goreng Dan Cili Potong Kicap
instructions: 1. Blend the garlic, shallots and dried anchovies until fine. 2. Heat oil and sauté the blended ingredients until lightly golden. 3. Add blended chilli and fry until crisp and the oil separates, then add sliced fish cake. 4. Add chilli sauce, oyster sauce, caramel soy sauce, optional fish sauce, prawns and white pepper. Stir briefly. 5. Add the kuey teow and toss to coat. Push the noodles aside, crack in the egg and let it set briefly before scrambling and mixing through. 6. Add bean sprouts gradually and the Chinese chives. Remove from heat and serve with sliced bird's eye chillies mixed with sweet soy sauce and lime juice.

name: Asam Pedas Ikan Pari
instructions: 1. Blend the fresh turmeric, ginger, garlic, shallots and belacan until smooth; set aside. 2. Heat oil and sauté fenugreek, lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves, followed by the blended paste. 3. Add blended chilli and cook until the oil separates. Add a little water and cook until the oil separates again; repeat 3-4 times so the chilli mixture is thoroughly cooked. 4. Add tamarind concentrate and water to make the gravy. 5. Add the stingray and cook until the gravy boils. 6. Add okra, tomato and Vietnamese coriander; cook until the vegetables are tender. 7. Season with salt and sugar to taste.

name: Mee Goreng Basah
ingredients: 4 cloves garlic, crushed and roughly chopped
instructions: 1. Bring water to a boil, blanch the yellow noodles and drain. 2. Heat a little oil and sauté the garlic until golden. 3. Add blended chilli and fry until crisp. 4. Add fish cake, chilli sauce, sweet soy sauce, oyster sauce, prawns, squid, white pepper, tomato, a little prawn-shell stock and mustard stems. 5. Add the yellow noodles, mustard leaves and bean sprouts. Add more chilli sauce or soy sauce if desired. 6. Garnish with fried shallots, spring onion, red chilli and calamansi or lime.

name: Sotong Goreng Kunyit
ingredients: 1 onion, sliced into rings or as desired
instructions: 1. Toss the squid with salt and turmeric powder, then fry briefly. 2. Sauté the onion using 2-3 tbsp of the oil used to fry the squid. 3. Add capsicum and onion and toss briefly. 4. Return the squid to the wok. 5. Season with salt and white pepper, then add the tomato. 6. Toss until evenly combined and serve.

name: Ayam Goreng Madu
instructions: 1. Marinate the chicken with the blended turmeric, ginger, shallots, garlic and lemongrass, sweet soy sauce, honey and a little salt for 1 hour. 2. Fry until the chicken is cooked and golden brown. 3. Drain, then toss once more with honey before serving.

name: Crispy Air-Fried Ayam Goreng Kunyit
instructions: 1. Toss chicken pieces with turmeric powder, curry powder, minced garlic, salt and 1 tbsp cooking oil. Marinate for 15 minutes. 2. Preheat air fryer to 180°C. Place marinated chicken in the basket in a single layer. 3. Air fry at 180°C for 10 minutes, shaking halfway through. 4. Add sliced onion, long beans, carrot and red chilli into the basket and air fry another 5 minutes at 190°C until golden and crisp. 5. Serve hot with steamed rice and sambal belacan.

name: Ikan Bakar Garing (Crispy Pan-Grilled Fish)
ingredients: Indian mackerel (ikan kembung), rubbed with turmeric and salt
A pinch of black or white pepper powder
Garlic (pounded until smooth, for fish rub)
Ginger (pounded until smooth, for fish rub)
Bird's eye chilies (pounded until smooth, for fish rub)
Salt (pounded with aromatics, for fish rub)
Sugar (pounded with aromatics, for fish rub)
A little seasoning powder (for fish rub)
Turmeric (pounded until smooth, for fish rub)
instructions: 1. Fry the salt- and turmeric-rubbed mackerel in a frying pan over the stove until half-cooked and slightly crispy. Remove and set aside on a plate. 2. For the fish topping paste, combine the pounded garlic, ginger, bird's eye chilies, salt, sugar, seasoning powder, and turmeric in a small bowl with sweet soy sauce and black or white pepper powder. 3. Add a little cooking oil and stir well. 4. Coat both sides of the half-cooked fish evenly with this paste. 5. Grill the fish in a frying pan over the stove or in an air fryer. 6. Alternatively, if using an oven, bake for about 10 to 15 minutes. 7. Transfer to a plate and serve.

name: Daging Bakar Harimau Menangis (Crying Tiger Grilled Beef)
ingredients: Beef tenderloin, washed, scored, and drained
Black pepper sauce (or freshly ground black pepper)
5-6 large red chilies, sliced, briefly fried, and blended
4-5 cloves garlic, roasted until golden, crushed, and diced
Chili sauce and oyster sauce (for dipping sauce)
Granulated sugar, lime juice, fish sauce, and tamarind water (for dipping sauce)
3/4 tbsp uncooked rice, dry-toasted until golden and ground or pounded
instructions: 1. Toss the scored beef with the chili sauce, oyster sauce, black pepper sauce, honey, fish sauce, and cooking oil in a mixing bowl and marinate; the longer, the better. 2. Air-fry the beef at 200°C for 5 to 10 minutes. 3. Once cooked, let the beef rest and cool slightly, then slice thinly on a chopping board. 4. For the dipping sauce, combine the blended red chilies, diced garlic, chili sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar, granulated sugar, lime juice, fish sauce, tamarind water, and cornstarch in a frying pan over the stove, excluding the toasted rice powder. 5. Add a little water and simmer until thickened, adjusting sour, sweet, and salty flavors to taste. 6. Stir in the toasted rice powder and cook briefly. Let cool, transfer to a small bowl, and sprinkle with dried chili powder. 7. Slice shallots and chop fresh coriander leaves, then scatter over the dish as garnish before serving.

name: Ikan Kerisi Bakar Petai Tempoyak (Grilled Threadfin Bream with Petai and Tempoyak)
instructions: 1. Pound the bird's eye chilies using a mortar and pestle according to your desired spiciness. 2. Transfer to a small bowl and mix thoroughly with turmeric, tempoyak, a little sugar, sliced lemongrass, and finely shredded turmeric leaf. 3. Fold in the stink beans and spread the mixture evenly over cleaned threadfin bream (ikan kerisi). 4. Cook in an air fryer at 160°C for 20 minutes.

name: Nasi Minyak Kampung (Traditional Ghee Rice)
ingredients: 4 cups water (1 cup used to blend fried shallots)
Salt and seasoning powder, to taste
instructions: 1. Blend the large onion, garlic, and ginger until smooth. 2. Turn on the rice cooker and melt the margarine inside the pot. 3. Saute the cinnamon stick, star anise, and cardamom pods until fragrant. 4. Add the blended onion, garlic, and ginger paste and saute. 5. Add the spiced soup sachet, raisins, salt, and seasoning powder. 6. Stir in the fried shallots blended with 1 cup of water. 7. Add the basmati rice, pandan leaves, and finally the remaining 3 cups of water. 8. Close the rice cooker lid and cook until done. 9. Once cooked, gently fluff the rice with a spoon to avoid breaking the grains.

name: Roti Daging Cheese (Cheesy Beef Buns)
instructions: 1. Place the minced beef in a frying pan over the stove and dry-fry without oil until crispy. 2. Add the mutton meat from the canned Adabi mutton soup into the pan. 3. Stir-fry together with the minced beef. 4. Add the oregano flakes and parsley flakes. 5. Add the chili sauce and salt. 6. Stir until the chili sauce, salt, oregano, and parsley are evenly combined. 7. Once everything is well mixed and cooked, turn off the stove. 8. Grease a baking pan with margarine evenly. 9. Slice the buns in half on a chopping board. 10. Spread margarine onto both sides of the buns. 11. Spoon the cooked meat onto the buns, then top with mayonnaise and cheese. 12. Place the buns in the oven using top and bottom heat. 13. Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes. 14. Remove from the oven, transfer to a plate, and serve.

name: Tart Nenas (Melt-in-the-Mouth Pineapple Tarts)
ingredients: A little yellow food coloring (for egg wash)
instructions: 1. In a mixing bowl, combine the butter, sweetened condensed milk, ghee, 1 egg yolk, vanilla essence, and yellow food coloring, and mix until smooth. 2. Add the wheat flour, cornstarch, and custard powder, and knead until a uniform dough forms. 3. Shape the dough and fill each piece with pineapple jam. 4. In a small bowl, mix the egg yolk and yellow food coloring, then brush it over the top of the tarts. 5. Bake in the oven at 160°C for about 25 minutes, depending on your oven.

name: Nasi Lemak (Coconut Milk Steamed Rice)
ingredients: 3 pandan leaves, knotted and slightly bruised
1 portion tamarind pulp (size of 3 ping-pong balls)
instructions: 1. Rinse the rice and drain well, then place it in a rice cooker. 2. Measure 50 ml of the thick coconut milk and dilute with water, stirring in 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp sugar. 3. Pour the diluted coconut milk over the rice and add enough water so the total liquid is about 6 cups, then add the crushed ginger, lemongrass, and knotted pandan leaves. 4. Switch on the rice cooker and cook until it reaches the warming stage. 5. Pour in the remaining 150 ml of thick coconut milk, stir, close the lid, and finish cooking; fluff the rice before serving. 6. Blend the soaked, deseeded dried chilies into a paste, and separately blend the shallots and garlic. 7. Rinse the dried anchovies in cold water and dry thoroughly, then fry in hot oil in a wok over low heat until light brown and crisp; strain and reserve a portion as a side dish. 8. Soak the tamarind pulp in 3 cups water for 15 minutes, squeeze to extract flavor, and strain to keep the tamarind juice. 9. Heat oil in the wok over the stove, fry the shrimp paste until aromatic, then add the chili paste and blended shallots and garlic and fry until fragrant. 10. Stir in the red onion rings, fried anchovies, tamarind juice, 1 tsp salt, and 3 tbsp sugar, and simmer over low heat until the sambal thickens. 11. Rinse and drain the raw peanuts, dry-toast in a clean hot wok over low heat for 5 minutes while stirring, then add a drop or two of oil and toss until browned and coated. 12. Place the eggs in a pot of water over the stove, bring to a boil, cover, turn off the heat, and let sit for 15 minutes; peel while warm and halve once cooled. 13. Peel and slice the cucumber thickly, then serve the hot coconut rice on plates with the sambal, crispy anchovies, peanuts, hard-boiled eggs, and cucumber slices.

name: Kuih Bahulu (Traditional Malay Sponge Cakes)
ingredients: 1 tsp rose essence or orange cordial
instructions: 1. Lightly beat the 4 grade A eggs in a mixing bowl with a whisk. 2. Add the sugar and whisk until fluffy and doubled in volume. 3. Add the rose essence or orange cordial and whisk until pale white. 4. Sift the wheat flour through a strainer gradually into the egg mixture and fold gently with a spatula until smooth. 5. Grease the baking molds with oil and preheat them in the oven for about 10 minutes. 6. Pour the batter into the hot molds and bake at 200°C with top and bottom heat for 10 to 12 minutes.

name: Nasi Daging Air Asam (Spiced Beef Rice with Tamarind Dip)
ingredients: 3 cups basmati rice, washed, soaked for 30 minutes, and drained
1 tbsp soup spice powder, mixed with a little water into a paste
3 tbsp kurma spice powder, mixed with a little water into a paste
Cinnamon stick, star anise, cloves, and cardamom pods
5 green bird's eye chilies (for tamarind kerisik dip)
4 green bird's eye chilies, diced (for topping)
1 ladle beef broth (for tamarind kerisik dip)
instructions: 1. Boil the beef in a pot over the stove until tender, and reserve the beef broth. 2. Heat a wok over the stove, add margarine and cooking oil, and saute the large onion, pounded garlic and ginger, cinnamon, star anise, cloves, and cardamom until golden. 3. Stir in the kurma spice paste and soup spice paste; once the oil separates, add the evaporated milk and knotted pandan leaves, stirring until the milk is absorbed. 4. Fold in the drained basmati rice until evenly coated. 5. Switch on the rice cooker and transfer the spiced rice mixture into the rice cooker pot. 6. Pour in the reserved beef broth matching the rice ratio (3 cups broth for 3 cups rice) and season with salt to taste. 7. Simmer briefly, place the boiled beef on top of the rice, cover with the lid, and let cook until done. 8. For the tamarind kerisik dip, pound the green bird's eye chilies, red chili, 1/2 yellow onion, belacan, and 1 tomato in a mortar and pestle until smooth, then add tamarind water, beef broth, and squeeze in the lime juice. 9. Stir in the kerisik, salt, and palm sugar to taste. 10. Combine the pounded dip in a small bowl with the diced yellow onion, diced tomato, and diced green bird's eye chilies. 11. Garnish the beef rice with chopped Chinese celery, spring onions, and fried shallots on a plate before serving with the dip.

name: Nasi Goreng Kampung (Village-Style Fried Rice)
ingredients: 60 g water spinach (kangkung), cut into sections
100 g medium shrimp, peeled with tails intact
3 bowls cooked long-grain rice, cooled (from 2 cups uncooked rice)
3 red chilies, deseeded and cut into sections
3 cloves garlic, peeled and finely minced
2 tbsp dried shrimp, soaked and drained
instructions: 1. Place the 3 bowls of cooled cooked rice into a mixing bowl and gently loosen any clumps with wet hands. 2. Cut the water spinach into sections, dice the long beans, peel the shrimp with tails intact, and crush the bird's eye chilies. 3. Soak the dried shrimp until softened and drain thoroughly in a strainer. 4. Deseed the red chilies and peel and chop the garlic and shallots into large pieces. 5. Blend the red chilies, garlic, shallots, dried shrimp, and toasted shrimp paste for about 3 seconds into a coarse spice paste, and set aside. 6. Heat a wok over the stove until smoking hot, then add the vegetable oil. 7. Fry the spice paste until lightly browned and fragrant. 8. Add the water spinach, long beans, peeled shrimp, and crushed bird's eye chilies, and stir-fry briefly to combine. 9. Add the loosened cooked rice and toss well to distribute all ingredients evenly. 10. Season with salt and fish sauce and continue stir-frying for about 5 minutes until hot and fragrant. 11. Transfer to a plate and serve hot, garnished with crispy fried shallots and prawn crackers on the side.

name: Stir-Fried Sambal Long Beans
ingredients: Salt and chicken stock, to taste
instructions: 1. Wash, rinse, and drain the long beans, then cut them into 2-inch lengths on a chopping board. 2. Soak the dried shrimp until soft, drain, and chop coarsely. 3. Blend the red chilies, dried chilies, shallots, garlic, and piece of shrimp paste together into a sambal paste. 4. Heat vegetable oil in a wok over the stove, add the coarsely chopped dried shrimp, and stir-fry until golden brown. 5. Add the sambal paste and stir-fry until aromatic. 6. Add the cut long beans and hot water, mixing well to coat with the sambal. 7. Season with salt and chicken stock to taste. 8. Cover and simmer over low heat until the water evaporates and the long beans are tender and well coated in sambal. 9. Transfer to a plate and serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Soto Daging (Malay Beef Soto Soup)
ingredients: 2 roots Chinese celery and spring onion
instructions: 1. Bring the water to a boil in a pot over the stove and add all the ingredients except the salt, simmering until the beef is tender. 2. Once the beef is tender, season with salt and seasoning powder if desired. 3. Ladle into bowls and garnish the soto soup with chopped Chinese celery and crispy fried shallots.

name: Laksa Johor
ingredients: Torch ginger flower (bunga kantan, for garnish)
instructions: 1. Boil half a wolf herring (ikan parang) or Spanish mackerel in a pot over the stove with ginger and garlic. 2. Debone the fish and blend the fish flesh with some of the boiling broth until smooth. 3. Blend the fish bones separately with broth and pass through a strainer, reserving the strained liquid for the gravy. 4. Heat oil in a wok or pot over the stove and saute the blended onion, shallots, garlic, lemongrass, and dried chilies until fragrant. 5. Stir in the fish curry powder mixed with a little water into a paste. 6. Add the blended fish flesh and dried shrimp, stir well, and bring to a boil. 7. Add the kerisik and coconut milk and bring back to a simmer. 8. Season with salt, sugar, and 1 dried tamarind slice (asam keping). 9. Simmer over low heat so the flavors meld, then serve over spaghetti topped with the fresh herbs, vegetables, sambal belacan, and calamansi lime.

name: Kuih Cara Manis (Sweet Pandan Kuih)
ingredients: 1 cup evaporated milk or coconut milk
A few drops of green food coloring
instructions: 1. Blend all the ingredients in a blender or whisk them together in a mixing bowl until smooth and lump-free. 2. Heat a lightly oiled pan or kuih cara mold over the stove, brush with a little oil, and pour in the batter. 3. Spoon a little sugar into the center of each kuih, cover with a lid, and cook for 5 minutes until set. 4. Lift out onto a plate and serve.

name: Bihun Goreng Daging Lada Hitam (Black Pepper Beef Fried Vermicelli)
instructions: 1. Bring water to a boil in a wok over the stove. 2. Blanch the rice vermicelli in the hot water until softened, then drain using a strainer. 3. Heat oil in the wok over the stove. 4. Once hot, add the sliced onion, blended garlic, and blended ginger and saute until fragrant. 5. Add the sliced beef and seafood sauce, cooking until the beef is tender. 6. Add the black pepper powder and salt. 7. Add the carrot, bell pepper, and bird's eye chilies, tossing well. 8. Add the blanched rice vermicelli and stir-fry until evenly coated. 9. Fold in the bean sprouts and toss briefly. 10. Transfer to serving bowls and serve hot.

name: Rendang Minang
instructions: 1. Heat a wok over the stove and add the blended shallots, garlic, dried chilies, ginger, and galangal along with the beef, turmeric leaf, Indonesian bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves; no oil is needed for sauteing. 2. Once the mixture begins to bubble, pour in the coconut milk (using 1 kg of coconut milk for every 1 kg of beef), and season with salt and seasoning powder. 3. Simmer and stir until the gravy thickens, reduces, and coats the tender beef, then transfer to a plate and serve.

name: Ayam Ungkep (Braised Spiced Chicken)
ingredients: 1/4 chicken, cut into small pieces (rubbed with salt and turmeric and rested 10 minutes)
2 red chilies (or 6 bird's eye chilies for extra heat)
1/2 inch fresh ginger and 1/2 inch fresh turmeric
1 tsp each fennel seeds, cumin seeds, and coriander seeds
A little tamarind water (or dried tamarind slice)
instructions: 1. Heat oil in a wok over medium heat on the stove and saute the fennel, cumin, coriander seeds, and bruised lemongrass. 2. Blend the shallots, garlic, chilies, ginger, and turmeric, add to the wok with a splash of water, and fry until slightly crisp and fragrant, then add the tamarind water and chicken and stir well. 3. Simmer until the chicken is tender and the gravy thickens, then add the chicken stock cube, salt, sugar, and kaffir lime leaves (plus coconut milk if using). Cook until aromatic, turn off the stove, and serve.

name: Sawi Masak Lemak Putih (Mustard Greens in Coconut Milk)
ingredients: 2 bunches white mustard greens (sawi putih), separated and chopped
A little carrot, cut into matchsticks
250 ml water, to mix with coconut milk
instructions: 1. Pour the coconut milk and water into a pot over the stove. 2. Add the carrot matchsticks, coarsely pounded dried shrimp, sliced shallots, garlic, soft tofu, and salt into the pot, leaving out the mustard greens and chilies. 3. Cook over low heat, stirring steadily. 4. When the coconut milk comes to a gentle boil, add the chopped mustard greens and stir until wilted. 5. Ladle into a serving bowl and top with the sliced chilies. 6. Serve hot.

name: Pisang Goreng Crispy (Crispy Banana Fritters)
ingredients: 4 tbsp food-grade slaked lime water (air kapur)
instructions: 1. Combine all the dry ingredients in a mixing bowl. 2. Gradually pour in the 2 cups of water along with the egg, slaked lime water, and butter until the batter is slightly thin and smooth rather than overly thick. 3. Coat sliced bananas or sweet potatoes in the batter. 4. Heat plenty of oil in a wok over the stove until very hot; drizzle a little batter into the hot oil to form crispy crumbs before adding the coated bananas, then deep-fry until golden brown and crispy. Drain and serve on a plate.

name: Daging Goreng Thai (Thai-Style Fried Beef)
ingredients: 4 tbsp coriander seeds, pounded or ground
2 tbsp palm sugar or somtam sugar (or white sugar)
2 tbsp uncooked rice, dry-toasted and finely ground
2 tbsp fish sauce or squid sauce
Fresh coriander leaves and 3 shallots, finely chopped
instructions: 1. Combine the beef in a mixing bowl with the ground coriander seeds, ground black pepper, oyster sauce, and salt, excluding the butter and garlic. 2. Marinate for 30 minutes to 2 hours. 3. For the dipping sauce, stir the Thai chili flakes, palm sugar, ground toasted rice, lime juice, tamarind water, fish sauce, chopped coriander, and chopped shallots together in a small bowl until well dissolved. 4. Heat butter in a wok or frying pan over the stove, saute the garlic until fragrant, and fry the marinated beef until cooked through and browned; serve hot on a plate with the dipping sauce.

name: Lempeng Oat (Savory Oat Pancakes)
instructions: 1. Combine all the ingredients except the coconut oil in a mixing bowl and whisk until evenly mixed. 2. Heat the coconut oil in a frying pan over the stove and pan-fry spoonfuls of the batter into thin pancakes on both sides until golden and cooked through. 3. Transfer to a plate and serve.

name: Masak Lemak Padang Ikan Tenggiri (Padang-Style Coconut Spanish Mackerel)
instructions: 1. Rub the Spanish mackerel pieces with turmeric powder and salt, then pan-fry in a frying pan over the stove until cooked through; set aside on a plate. 2. Heat oil in the wok or frying pan over the stove and saute the sliced galangal, lemongrass, and Indonesian bay leaf briefly. 3. Blend the ginger, 2 cm galangal, fresh turmeric, shallots, garlic, candlenuts, and red chilies, then add to the pan and fry until the oil separates. 4. Pour in the water and coconut milk and bring to a boil. 5. Add the tomato and the fried Spanish mackerel. 6. Season with salt and seasoning powder, simmer briefly, then turn off the stove. 7. Serve hot.

name: Asam Pedas Ikan Bawal (Sour and Spicy Pomfret Stew)
instructions: 1. Soak the dried chilies, uncooked rice, and black peppercorns in a bowl of hot water until softened and plumped. 2. Blend the soaked ingredients together with the lemongrass, ginger, fresh turmeric, shrimp paste, shallots, and garlic until smooth. 3. Pour the blended paste directly into a pot over the stove, adding a little water if too thick, followed by the tamarind water. 4. Once the gravy comes to a boil, add the golden pomfret and bamboo shoots, season with salt to taste, and simmer until the fish is cooked through.

name: Telur Bistik Daging (Savory Beef Omelette)
ingredients: Spicy sweet soy sauce (kicap manis pedas)
instructions: 1. Beat the eggs in a small bowl and fry in a frying pan over the stove with generous oil until crispy as an omelette, then transfer to a plate. 2. Pour off excess oil from the pan and saute the chopped onion and chili until golden. 3. Add the beef burger patties and break them apart while frying until cooked through (or use minced beef). 4. Stir in the chili sauce, spicy sweet soy sauce, oyster sauce, and a pinch of pepper powder. 5. Add a splash of water, simmer briefly into a glossy sauce, and spoon over the crispy omelette.

name: Lamb Shank Sup Tulang Merah (Red Bone Marrow Lamb Shank Soup)
ingredients: Whole spices (cinnamon stick, star anise, cloves, and cardamom)
Bone soup spice sachet (sup bunjut tulang)
A few drops of red food coloring (optional)
instructions: 1. Heat oil in a pot over the stove and saute the sliced garlic, shallots, ginger, and whole spices until fragrant. 2. Once the oil separates, pour in water and add the lamb shanks. 3. Drop in the bone soup spice sachet and simmer until the lamb begins to tenderize. 4. Stir in the dried chili paste, tomato puree, red food coloring if using, and coriander roots and leaves. 5. Season with salt and palm sugar to taste, simmer until the lamb shanks are tender, and garnish with extra chopped coriander leaves before serving.

name: Singgang Daging (Spiced Clear Beef Broth)
ingredients: 1/2 kg beef, thinly sliced or cut into small pieces
1 inch ginger, cut into thin strips
3 dried chilies, coarsely pounded with coriander seeds
Seasoning powder and fermented fish sauce (budu), optional
instructions: 1. Place the bruised galangal, ginger strips, coarsely pounded coriander seeds and dried chilies, sliced garlic, sliced shallots, and palm sugar into a pot with the beef without water and toss well. 2. Cook over low heat on the stove without added water for a few minutes so the beef releases its juices and absorbs the spices. 3. Pour in enough water to cover the beef. 4. Simmer until the beef starts to soften. 5. Add salt and the dried tamarind slices, and continue simmering until the beef is completely tender. 6. Add seasoning powder and fermented fish sauce (budu) if desired. 7. Turn off the stove and serve hot in bowls.

name: Cucur Udang (Crispy Prawn Fritters)
instructions: 1. Combine all the ingredients in a mixing bowl and stir into a smooth, even batter. 2. Heat oil in a wok or frying pan over the stove and spoon thin, flat portions of batter into the hot oil, frying until golden brown and crispy on both sides. Drain and serve on a plate.

name: Sambal Belacan Tomato (Tomato Shrimp Paste Chili Dip)
instructions: 1. Heat cooking oil in a frying pan over the stove. 2. Fry the chilies, tomato, shallots, and shrimp paste until lightly charred and softened. 3. Transfer to a blender and pulse coarsely, then season with sugar, salt, and seasoning powder. 4. Spoon into a small bowl and serve.

name: Mee Rebus Tulang (Beef Bone Gravy Noodles)
ingredients: Dried shrimp, dry-toasted and finely ground
Boiled sweet potatoes and potatoes, blended smooth (potatoes half the amount of sweet potatoes)
instructions: 1. Heat oil in a pot over the stove and saute the sliced shallots and garlic until fragrant, then add the ground toasted dried shrimp. 2. Once aromatic, add the dried chili paste and fry until the oil separates. 3. Pour in the beef broth along with the beef meat and bones. 4. When boiling, stir in the blended sweet potatoes and potatoes, followed by chili sauce, sugar, and salt to taste (and beef stock cube if using). 5. If the gravy is not thick enough, blend 3 to 4 peeled raw potatoes until smooth and simmer in the gravy until thickened to your preference, then serve over yellow noodles.

name: Mee Bandung (Rich Beef and Seafood Noodle Soup)
instructions: 1. Blend the boiled dried shrimp, dried shrimp boiling water, dried chilies, shallots, garlic, sugar, salt, and Marie biscuits into a paste, then fry in a pan over the stove to cook the paste. 2. Boil the beef or beef bones in a pot over the stove until tender, keeping the broth for the gravy. 3. Heat oil in a pot and add the prepared chili-shrimp paste. 4. Saute until the oil separates, then add the boiled beef or beef bones. 5. Stir briefly to coat, then pour in all the reserved beef broth and a little extra water. 6. Let simmer with the beef, and add fried and blended potatoes to thicken the gravy. 7. Add the fresh prawns, fish cake, and fish balls, then crack the eggs directly into the simmering broth. 8. Cook briefly until the eggs and seafood are done, then fold in the mustard greens at the end. 9. Ladle over noodles in bowls and garnish with crispy fried shallots.

name: Gulai Tempoyak Ikan Termenung (Fermented Durian Mackerel Curry)
instructions: 1. Blend the bird's eye chilies, onion, and fresh turmeric, then transfer into a wok or deep pan over the stove along with the bruised lemongrass. 2. Blend the tempoyak with water until smooth and pour into the wok. 3. Bring to a boil, then add the mackerel (and cucumber slices if desired), seasoning with salt and sugar to taste until the fish is cooked through. Serve on a plate.

name: Lontong Goreng (Stir-Fried Compressed Rice Cakes)
ingredients: 9 dried chilies, deseeded and soaked in hot water (or chili paste)
10 small packets compressed rice cakes (nasi impit), diced
1 block fresh tofu, fried and diced
7 long beans, finely chopped, and a handful of bean sprouts
instructions: 1. Blend the garlic, shallots, soaked dried chilies, dried shrimp, and dried anchovies, then saute in oil in a wok over the stove until fragrant. 2. Stir in the minced beef or chicken, chili sauce, oyster sauce, and sweet soy sauce. 3. Crack in the eggs, let them set slightly, then scramble and mix evenly. 4. Add the chopped long beans. 5. Pour in a splash of water and add the dark soy sauce. 6. Stir until the sauce thickens, then fold in the diced compressed rice cakes, fried tofu, and bean sprouts until evenly coated. 7. Season with salt and sugar to taste and stir-fry until dry and well combined. 8. Turn off the stove and serve on a plate.

name: Kerabu Bayam Brazil dan Taugeh (Brazilian Spinach and Bean Sprout Salad)
instructions: 1. Boil the sardines in a pot over the stove, flake the fish meat, and blend it together with the shallots, garlic, dried chili, and coconut milk. 2. Transfer the blended mixture into a frying pan over the stove and cook while stirring until thickened and fragrant. 3. Remove from heat and allow the dressing to cool completely. 4. Place Brazilian spinach and bean sprouts into a mixing bowl and spoon the cooled dressing over the greens. 5. Season with a pinch of salt, fresh lime juice, and sliced chilies. 6. Toss thoroughly to coat and serve.

name: Masak Lemak Ikan Jenahak (Golden Snapper in Turmeric Coconut Gravy)
instructions: 1. Place the cleaned golden snapper steaks into a pot. 2. Add the pounded shallot, fresh turmeric, green chilies, chili paste, torn turmeric leaf, and bruised lemongrass into the pot. 3. Cook over low heat on the stove until the fish absorbs the aromatic spices. 4. Pour in the water and coconut milk, add the dried tamarind slice, and ladle-stir the gravy continuously to prevent the coconut milk from splitting. 5. Once simmering nicely and the fish is cooked through, turn off the stove and season with salt and sugar to taste. 6. Serve hot.

name: Char Kway Teow Special
instructions: 1. Heat cooking oil in a very hot wok over high heat. 2. Sauté minced garlic and chilli paste for 10 seconds until aromatic. 3. Toss in prawns and stir-fry until they turn pink. 4. Add the kuey teow, light soy sauce and dark soy sauce, tossing briskly to get smoky wok hei. 5. Push noodles aside, crack in the eggs and scramble lightly before folding through. 6. Add bean sprouts and Chinese chives, toss for 15 seconds and serve immediately.

name: Cantonese Steamed Fish
ingredients: 1 whole sea bass or snapper, cleaned
instructions: 1. Score both sides of the fish and place it on a heatproof plate with half the julienned ginger. 2. Bring water to a rolling boil in a pot fitted with a steaming rack. 3. Steam the fish covered for 8-10 minutes until the flesh flakes easily. 4. Mix light soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar and hot water in a small bowl. 5. Discard the fishy steaming liquid, pour the soy sauce mixture over the fish and top with remaining ginger, spring onion and coriander. 6. Heat cooking oil until smoking and drizzle over the aromatics before serving.

name: Siew Yoke (Chinese Roast Pork Belly)
instructions: 1. Using a sharp knife, scrape away any impurities and hair on the pork skin at a 90-degree angle without cutting into the meat. 2. Rinse thoroughly, drain, and pat dry with paper towels. 3. Prick the skin all over with the tip of a sharp knife or roasting needles, making pinpricks rather than slits. 4. Flip the pork belly skin-side down and score the meat side with shallow cuts about 1 cm deep and 1.5 cm apart along its length. 5. Mix the fermented red beancurd, sugar, five spice powder, white pepper, and rice wine in a small bowl, then rub the marinade all over the meat and into the cuts without touching the skin. 6. Flip skin-side up onto a rack, wipe the skin dry again with paper towels, and rub salt evenly into the skin. 7. Place a tray underneath and chill uncovered in the refrigerator overnight to dry out the skin. 8. Remove from the refrigerator 1 hour before roasting to bring to room temperature, then brush off excess salt and pat the skin dry. 9. Preheat the oven to 200 C with fan and both upper and lower heating elements on, and place a foil-lined drip tray beneath the middle roasting rack. 10. Roast for 20 minutes, then remove, brush vinegar onto the skin, switch the oven to grill mode, and grill for 20 minutes. Repeat brushing with vinegar and grilling twice more, monitoring closely until the skin is crackled and blistered (about 1 hour 20 minutes total). 11. Remove from the oven and rest for at least 10 minutes, scraping off any charred spots on the skin with a serrated knife. 12. Chop the roast pork belly into bite-sized pieces and serve.

name: Steamed Egg with Preserved Radish
ingredients: 1 bowl warm water (equal volume to eggs)
20 g sweet preserved radish (rinsed, squeezed dry, and chopped)
10 g salty preserved radish (rinsed, squeezed dry, and chopped)
100 g minced meat (mixed with a little cornflour)
instructions: 1. Crack the eggs into a bowl and measure an equal volume of warm water in another bowl. 2. Whisk the eggs with salt and warm water until well combined, then strain through a fine strainer into a deep, wide heatproof plate. 3. Cover the plate tightly with heatproof cling wrap and place it into a covered pot with boiling water on the stove. 4. Steam over low heat for 10 to 15 minutes until the egg custard is set, then remove the cling wrap. 5. Meanwhile, rinse, drain, and squeeze dry the sweet and salty preserved radishes, chop the garlic, and dice the spring onion. 6. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok or frying pan over medium heat and saute the chopped garlic and preserved radishes until fragrant. 7. Add the minced meat and stir-fry until just cooked, then stir in the chicken stock granules, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and dark soy sauce. 8. Mix the cornflour with 1 tbsp water and stir into the pan, frying until the topping is dry. 9. Spoon the preserved radish and meat topping over the steamed egg custard, garnish with diced spring onions, and serve hot.

name: Steamed White Sugar Cake (Bak Tong Gou)
ingredients: 1/2 tsp cooking oil (plus extra for greasing)
instructions: 1. Dissolve the instant yeast in 1 tbsp lukewarm water in a small bowl and set aside for 10 minutes until foamy. 2. Place the sifted rice flour in a mixing bowl, add 280 g room-temperature water, and whisk until smooth and thick. 3. In a saucepan over medium heat, heat the sugar, 340 g water, and knotted pandan leaves until the sugar dissolves completely. 4. Discard the pandan leaves and slowly pour the hot sugar syrup into the rice flour batter while whisking constantly to prevent lumps. 5. Allow the batter to cool until lukewarm (about 30 C), then stir in the foamy yeast mixture until well combined. 6. Cover with plastic wrap and leave to proof in a warm place for 2 hours until large bubbles form on the surface. 7. Stir in 1/2 tsp cooking oil, grease a 10-inch round heatproof pan or plate, pour in the batter, and rest for 20 minutes until small bubbles appear. 8. Place the pan in a covered pot with rapidly boiling water on the stove and steam over high heat for 30 minutes. 9. Remove and cool completely before running a spatula around the edges, unmoulding, and slicing to serve.

name: Black Sesame Glutinous Rice Balls (Tang Yuan)
ingredients: 1/4 cup black sesame seeds (toasted and coarsely ground)
150 g old ginger (peeled and lightly crushed)
instructions: 1. Peel and thickly slice the old ginger, then lightly crush it. Bring 5 cups of water to a boil in a pot on the stove, add the ginger and knotted pandan leaves, cover, and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes. 2. Add 1 cup sugar and the sweet osmanthus, boil over medium heat for 5 minutes, then simmer for 10 minutes until slightly reduced. Remove the ginger and pandan leaves and set the syrup aside. 3. Lightly toast the black sesame seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until aromatic, then coarsely grind them with a mortar and pestle. 4. Mix the ground sesame seeds with 1/4 cup sugar and coconut oil in a small bowl to form a paste, then chill in the refrigerator. 5. Place the glutinous rice flour in a mixing bowl, stir in the boiling water with a spatula to partially cook the flour, then gradually add cold water and knead into a smooth, non-sticky dough. 6. Divide the dough into 20 g balls, flatten each piece, place 1 tsp chilled sesame paste in the center, wrap, and roll into smooth balls. 7. Boil a pot of water on the stove, gently drop in the rice balls in batches, and cook for 3 to 5 minutes until they float to the surface. 8. Lift the cooked rice balls out with a strainer, plunge into cold water for 1 minute for a chewier texture, then transfer to the warm ginger syrup and serve hot or cold.

name: Salted Egg Yolk Fried Chicken
ingredients: 500 g whole chicken legs (2 legs, cut into bite-sized pieces)
instructions: 1. Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces. Place the salted egg yolks in a small bowl and steam in a covered pot on the stove for 5 to 7 minutes, then cool and mash with a spoon. 2. Dice the bird's eye chillies and strip the curry leaves from their stalks. 3. In a mixing bowl, combine the chicken pieces with the salt, 1/4 tsp white pepper, sesame oil, water, all-purpose flour, and cornflour. Cover and marinate for at least 1 hour or overnight. 4. Heat 1 cup cooking oil in a wok or frying pan for deep-frying, then fry the marinated chicken in batches until golden brown and cooked through. Drain on a paper-lined plate. 5. Heat 1 tbsp cooking oil in a clean wok or pan, add the mashed salted egg yolks, curry leaves, and diced chillies, and stir-fry until fragrant. 6. Reduce the heat, pour in the evaporated milk, sugar, and remaining 1/4 tsp white pepper, and bring to a gentle boil. 7. Add the fried chicken and toss until evenly coated in the thickened salted egg sauce. Garnish with extra chopped chillies and serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Claypot Bean Curd
ingredients: 4 blocks semi-firm bean curd (cut into cubes)
100 g roasted pork (sliced into bite-sized pieces)
100 ml cooking oil (for frying, plus 1 tbsp)
instructions: 1. Soak the dried shiitake mushrooms until soft, drain well, and slice. Mince the garlic, slice the ginger, cut the onion into wedges, slice the carrot, and trim the snow peas. 2. Slice the roasted pork into 2 cm pieces. Shell and devein the prawns, then lightly season them with a pinch of salt and sugar. Cut the bean curd into cubes. 3. Heat 100 ml oil in a wok or frying pan over high heat and deep-fry the bean curd cubes in batches until golden brown, then drain in a strainer lined with kitchen paper. 4. Mix the oyster sauce, light soy sauce, salt, white pepper, and 150 ml water in a small bowl. Mix the cornflour with 2 tbsp water in another small bowl. 5. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pot or claypot on the stove and saute the garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant. 6. Add the prawns, roasted pork, and mushrooms and stir-fry briefly, then add the carrots and snow peas and cook for 5 minutes. 7. Pour in the sauce mixture, add the fried bean curd gently without breaking the cubes, and bring to a boil for 2 minutes. 8. Stir in the cornflour slurry until the gravy thickens, cover, remove from heat, and serve hot.

name: Mapo Tofu
ingredients: 450 g soft white tofu (1 box, cubed)
2 tbsp doubanjiang (spicy fermented broad bean and chilli paste)
instructions: 1. Marinate the minced meat with sesame oil and salt in a mixing bowl. Cut the soft tofu into cubes, chop the spring onions and garlic, and mix the cornstarch with 3 tbsp water in a small bowl. 2. Boil water in a saucepan on the stove, gently blanch the tofu cubes for 1 minute, drain through a strainer, and set aside. 3. Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or frying pan over medium heat and stir-fry the marinated meat until just cooked, then remove and set aside. 4. In the same pan, fry the doubanjiang until aromatic, then add the white parts of the spring onion, garlic, fermented black beans, and ground Sichuan peppercorn and stir-fry until fragrant. 5. Pour in 400 ml water and bring to a boil, then gently slide in the blanched tofu, soy sauce, and cooked meat without mashing the tofu. 6. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 5 to 10 minutes. 7. Swirl in the cornstarch slurry in batches while gently stirring until the sauce thickens, top with green spring onions, and serve hot over steamed rice.

name: Steamed Bean Curd with Shallot Oil
instructions: 1. Place the soft bean curd on a heatproof plate. Soak and drain the dried prawns, thinly slice the shallots, and chop the spring onion. 2. In a small bowl, mix together the oyster sauce, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, chicken stock granules, and water. 3. Place the plate of bean curd into a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam over high heat for 5 minutes, then carefully drain off excess liquid from the plate. 4. Heat the cooking oil in a wok or frying pan over medium heat and fry the sliced shallots until golden brown and crispy, then spoon the shallots and oil over the steamed bean curd. 5. In the same pan, fry the soaked dried prawns until golden brown and set aside. 6. Pour the seasoning sauce mixture into the pan and bring to a boil, then pour the hot sauce over the bean curd. 7. Garnish with fried dried prawns and chopped spring onions, and serve immediately.

name: Steamed Pumpkin Savoury Cake
ingredients: 30 g dried shrimp (soaked, drained, and chopped)
20 g dried shiitake mushrooms (3 to 4 pieces, soaked, drained, and chopped)
1 tbsp shallot oil (plus extra oil for frying shallots and greasing)
instructions: 1. Oil and line a 6-inch round or square baking pan with parchment paper. Cut the peeled pumpkin into cubes, steam in a covered pot on the stove until tender, and mash with a spoon. 2. Thinly slice the shallots and deep-fry in oil in a wok or frying pan until crisp and golden brown, reserving 1 tbsp of the shallot oil. 3. Chop the soaked mushrooms and soaked dried shrimp, then stir-fry them in 1 tbsp shallot oil until aromatic and transfer to a small bowl. 4. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the sifted self-raising flour, salt, instant yeast, and baking powder. 5. Fold in the mashed pumpkin and water with a spatula until smooth, then stir in the fried shallots, mushrooms, and dried shrimp. 6. Pour the batter into the lined pan, tap gently to remove air pockets, smooth the top, cover with cling wrap, and proof for about 60 minutes until doubled in size. 7. Place the pan in a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam over high heat for 30 minutes. Cool before slicing and serving.

name: Purple Sweet Potato Steamed Cake (Huat Kueh)
ingredients: 50 g purple sweet potato (steamed and mashed)
instructions: 1. Peel and dice the purple sweet potato, steam in a covered pot on the stove for 20 minutes until soft, then mash smoothly with a spoon and set aside. 2. In a mixing bowl, combine the sieved flour, salt, sugar, and yeast, then whisk in the milk, water, and vegetable oil until smooth. 3. Transfer 100 g of the plain batter into a small bowl, and mix the mashed purple sweet potato into the remaining batter until smooth. 4. Cover both batters with cling wrap and leave to proof for 1 hour. 5. Line 7.5 cm heatproof cups with paper liners. Spoon the plain batter into the cups first, top with the purple sweet potato batter, and smooth the tops. 6. Bring water to a rapid boil in a pot on the stove, place the cups inside, cover, and steam over high heat for 15 minutes. 7. Remove and let cool slightly before serving.

name: Steamed Pork Ribs with Pickled Plum
ingredients: 400 g pork soft ribs (cut into 1-inch pieces)
1 stalk coriander leaves (cut into long pieces)
instructions: 1. Mince the garlic, chop the spring onion and coriander, and dice the red chillies. 2. Rub the pork ribs briefly with salt, rinse thoroughly in a strainer to remove impurities, pat dry with paper towels, and cut into 1-inch bite-sized pieces. 3. In a mixing bowl, toss the ribs with light soy sauce, mashed pickled plums, plum sauce, plum liquid, fermented bean paste, sugar, and minced garlic. 4. Dissolve the cornstarch in 1 tbsp water in a small bowl and mix into the ribs until absorbed, then coat with sesame oil and cooking oil. Cover and marinate for 15 to 30 minutes. 5. Arrange the marinated ribs in a single layer on a deep heatproof plate, keeping pieces slightly separated. 6. Place the plate into a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam over high heat for 12 minutes, then turn off the heat and keep covered for 3 minutes more. 7. Check that the ribs are tender, garnish with chopped spring onions, chillies, and coriander, and serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Bitter Gourd Omelette
ingredients: 1 tsp cooking oil (plus 2 tbsp for frying)
1 tsp salt (for rubbing bitter gourd, plus a pinch)
instructions: 1. Halve the bitter gourd lengthwise, scrape out the pith and seeds with a spoon, slice thinly at an angle, rub with 1 tsp salt, and rest for 5 minutes. 2. Rinse the bitter gourd several times to remove excess salt and drain well. 3. Crack the eggs into a mixing bowl, add the light soy sauce, chicken stock granules, and ground white pepper, and whisk until combined. 4. Heat 1 tsp cooking oil in a wok or frying pan, saute the chopped garlic until fragrant, add the bitter gourd with a pinch of salt, and stir-fry until tender. 5. Transfer the cooked bitter gourd into the beaten egg mixture and stir to combine. 6. Heat 2 tbsp cooking oil in the pan, pour in the egg and bitter gourd mixture, and spread evenly. Once the edges set, reduce to medium heat without pressing the omelette. 7. When the underside is firm and golden, flip and cook the other side until set. Slide onto a plate and serve hot with rice or porridge.

name: Steamed Caramel Cupcakes
instructions: 1. Melt the sugar in a saucepan over low heat until it turns golden brown caramel, then carefully stir in the water and margarine until thickened. Remove from heat and let cool. 2. Sieve the all-purpose flour, baking powder, baking soda, and custard powder together into a mixing bowl. 3. In another bowl, whisk the eggs, fresh milk, and vanilla essence until combined. 4. Mix the cooled caramel into the egg mixture, then fold in the dry flour mixture in 3 alternating batches until a smooth batter forms. 5. Strain the batter through a strainer into a pouring bowl, then fill silicone cupcake moulds about three-quarters full. 6. Place the moulds in a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam over high heat for 15 to 20 minutes. 7. Remove, let cool slightly, unmould, and serve.

name: Steamed Shiitake Mushroom Beancurd
instructions: 1. Soak the dried shiitake mushrooms in cold water for about 1 hour until soft, drain, squeeze dry, chop roughly, and blend in a blender until finely minced. 2. Peel and mince the ginger. Heat the vegetable oil and sesame oil in a wok or frying pan over medium heat and saute the ginger until aromatic. 3. Add the blended mushrooms and stir-fry until fragrant, then stir in the vegetarian oyster sauce, vegetarian shacha sauce, sugar, soy sauce, white pepper, and Zhejiang vinegar. Cook over low heat for 2 minutes. 4. Place the soft bean curd on a heatproof plate and spoon the mushroom sauce evenly on top. 5. Place the plate into a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam over medium heat for 10 minutes. 6. Garnish with carrot strips and Chinese parsley, and serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Steamed Ginger Milk Pudding
ingredients: 2 tbsp ginger juice (from 50 g old ginger)
instructions: 1. Scrape the skin off the old ginger with a spoon, grate finely with a grater, and press the pulp through a fine strainer into a small bowl to extract 2 tbsp ginger juice. 2. Separate the egg whites into a mixing bowl, add the sugar and salt, and whisk gently until dissolved. 3. Slowly whisk in the fresh milk, then pass the mixture through a strainer to remove air bubbles and stir in the ginger juice. 4. Divide the mixture evenly into heatproof small bowls, skim off any surface bubbles, and cover each bowl tightly with heatproof cling wrap. 5. Place the bowls on a heatproof rack inside a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam over medium-low heat for 15 minutes until set. 6. Serve warm, or cool to room temperature and chill in the refrigerator before serving.

name: Ginger Sauce Steamed Fish
ingredients: 3 stalks spring onion (2 to line plate, 1 shredded for garnish)
instructions: 1. Rinse the fish with cold water, pat dry, score small slits on both sides, and lay it on a heatproof plate lined with 2 stalks of spring onion. 2. Place the plate into a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam over high heat for 10 to 15 minutes until cooked through. 3. Meanwhile, grate the fresh ginger. Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or frying pan and stir-fry the grated ginger until fragrant. 4. Add the salt, sugar, oyster sauce, cooking wine, sesame oil, chicken stock granules, and water, and bring to a boil. 5. Stir in the cornstarch slurry until the ginger sauce thickens, then transfer to a small bowl. 6. Remove the steamed fish, discard the steaming liquid and bottom spring onions, and spoon the ginger sauce over the fish. 7. Drizzle with fried garlic oil, garnish with shredded spring onion, coriander, and red chilli strips, and serve hot.

name: Homestyle Marmite Chicken
ingredients: 500 g whole chicken legs (2 legs, cut into large bite-sized pieces)
instructions: 1. Wash and drain the chicken pieces well, then marinate with salt for at least 30 minutes. 2. In a mixing bowl, lightly beat the egg white, toss the chicken pieces in it, and coat evenly with potato starch. 3. Heat deep-frying oil in a wok or frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the chicken in batches for 10 to 15 minutes until golden brown and cooked through. Lift out with a strainer and drain on a paper-lined plate. 4. In a small bowl, stir together the Marmite, soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar, and dark soy sauce until the Marmite dissolves. 5. Heat the water in a clean wok or pan over medium-high heat, pour in the Marmite sauce mixture, and cook until bubbling and slightly thickened. 6. Quickly add the fried chicken and toss over high heat until the sauce reduces and coats every piece evenly. Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Lotus Root Stir Fry
ingredients: 250 g young lotus root (peeled and thinly sliced)
40 g dried black fungus (soaked and trimmed)
instructions: 1. Soak the dried black fungus in cold water for 20 minutes until expanded, then drain and trim off tough stems. 2. Peel and thinly slice the lotus root, carrot, celery, and water chestnuts, and trim the strings from the snow peas. 3. Toast the macadamia nuts in a dry wok or frying pan until lightly golden and set aside in a small bowl. 4. Heat cooking oil in the wok over medium heat and saute the minced garlic until fragrant. 5. Add the lotus root, snow peas, and carrot, and stir-fry for about 3 minutes. 6. Pour in the chicken broth, add the celery, water chestnuts, and black fungus, and cook for another 5 minutes. 7. Season with soy sauce and oyster sauce, stir-fry briefly until bubbling, fold in the toasted macadamia nuts, transfer to a plate, and serve immediately.

name: Chinese Steamed Chicken
instructions: 1. Rub the salt evenly over both sides of the cleaned half chicken and let it rest for 30 minutes on a heatproof plate. 2. Place the plate into a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam over high heat for 20 to 30 minutes until cooked through and tender. 3. Remove the chicken, let cool slightly, and chop into bite-sized pieces on a chopping board, then arrange on a serving plate. 4. Meanwhile, heat the vegetable oil in a wok or frying pan over medium heat and fry the minced garlic and chopped ginger until fragrant and golden brown. 5. Transfer the browned garlic, ginger, and fragrant oil into a small bowl and stir in the soy sauce. 6. Drizzle the aromatic sauce evenly over the chopped chicken, garnish with chopped green onions and red chilli slices, and serve with steamed rice.

name: Homemade Savory Turnip Pau
ingredients: Prepared savory turnip filling (optional, as desired)
instructions: 1. Place the pau flour, sugar, baking powder, and instant yeast into a mixing bowl and stir to combine. 2. Gradually add enough water to form a soft dough and knead for 5 minutes until combined. 3. Add the shortening and continue kneading for 8 to 10 minutes until the dough is smooth, soft, and elastic. 4. Divide the dough into 50 g portions, roll each into a ball, and flatten into a round disc. 5. Spoon savory turnip filling into the center of each disc, gather and pleat the edges to seal into a bun, and place each bun onto a square of parchment paper. 6. Leave the buns to proof for 20 to 30 minutes until doubled in size. 7. Arrange the buns on a heatproof perforated plate inside a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam over high heat for 15 minutes. 8. Turn off the heat and wait 3 minutes before uncovering to prevent the skins from wrinkling, then serve warm.

name: Homestyle Chinese Egg Dumplings
ingredients: 1/4 tsp salt (plus a pinch for eggs)
instructions: 1. In a mixing bowl, combine the minced meat with sesame oil, white pepper, salt, cornstarch, and Chinese cooking wine. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 3 hours. 2. Heat a little oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat and stir-fry the minced garlic and marinated meat until cooked through, then transfer to a small bowl. 3. Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt in a bowl. 4. Lightly oil the same frying pan over low heat, pour 2 tbsp beaten egg into the center, and swirl with the back of a spoon into a 3-inch circle. 5. Before the top fully sets, place 1/2 tbsp cooked meat slightly off-center, fold half of the egg sheet over with a spatula to form a half-moon purse, and press the edges to seal. 6. Cook gently on both sides until set, transfer to a plate, and repeat with the remaining egg and filling.

name: Stir-Fried Fish with Bitter Gourd
ingredients: 350 g fresh whole fish (cut into large chunks)
instructions: 1. Halve the bitter gourd lengthwise, scrape out the seeds with a spoon, and slice thinly. Blanch in a pot of salted boiling water for 2 minutes to reduce bitterness, then drain and set aside. 2. Season the fish chunks with a pinch of salt and pepper, then coat evenly with cornflour. 3. Heat oil in a wok or frying pan and fry the fish chunks until lightly browned, then drain onto a plate. 4. Mix the sesame oil, dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, sugar, black pepper, and Chinese cooking wine in a small bowl. 5. In a clean pan with a little oil, stir-fry the garlic, ginger, shallots, onion wedges, fermented black beans, and bird's eye chillies until fragrant. 6. Add the blanched bitter gourd and stir-fry over high heat for 2 minutes, then pour in the seasoning mixture and 50 ml hot water. 7. Return the fried fish chunks to the pan, toss gently for 1 minute to coat in the sauce, and serve warm with rice.

name: Malaysian Style Braised Chicken with Bitter Gourd
ingredients: 500 g chicken (2 whole legs, skin removed and cut into bite-sized pieces)
1 tbsp fermented black beans (rinsed and drained)
1 tsp cornstarch (mixed with 1 tbsp water for thickening)
2 tbsp light soy sauce (divided: 1 tbsp marinade, 1 tbsp sauce)
1/2 tsp white pepper (divided: 1/4 tsp marinade, 1/4 tsp sauce)
instructions: 1. Clean and drain the skinless chicken pieces, then marinate in a mixing bowl with 1 tbsp light soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, 1/4 tsp white pepper, and 1/2 tbsp cornstarch for 30 minutes. 2. Halve the bitter gourd lengthwise, scrape out the seeds, cut into 3-inch by 3/4-inch strips, rub with salt, blanch in a pot of boiling water for 1 minute, rinse in cold water, and drain in a strainer. 3. Mix 1 tbsp light soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, salt, 1/4 tsp white pepper, and 1 cup water in a small bowl. 4. Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a wok or frying pan, saute half the garlic and ginger until fragrant, and stir-fry the chicken over medium-high heat for 3 minutes until half-cooked, then remove. 5. Add a little more oil to the wok, fry the remaining garlic and ginger until lightly browned, then add the yellow bean paste and fermented black beans and stir-fry until aromatic. 6. Add the bitter gourd and chicken back in, pour in the sauce mixture, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender. 7. Stir in the cornstarch slurry until the gravy thickens and serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Steamed Minced Pork with Salted Fish
ingredients: 2 dried shiitake mushrooms (soaked until soft and finely chopped)
1 thumb-sized piece salted fish (rinsed, pan-fried, and diced)
1 tsp Chinese cooking wine (Hua Tiao Chiew)
instructions: 1. Pan-fry the rinsed salted fish briefly in a small frying pan and cut into small pieces. 2. In a mixing bowl, combine the minced pork with soy sauce, cooking wine, sesame oil, sugar, salt, white pepper, and cornstarch, then gradually stir in the water until absorbed. 3. Mix in the chopped shiitake mushrooms, water chestnuts, grated ginger, and half the salted fish, stirring vigorously in one direction until the mixture becomes a sticky paste. 4. Spread and press the pork mixture evenly into a heatproof plate about 1 cm thick, leaving a small border around the edge, and chill for 1 hour if time permits. 5. Top with the remaining salted fish and shredded ginger, and drizzle with garlic or shallot oil. 6. Place the plate into a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam over high heat for 10 minutes until cooked through. 7. Garnish with chopped spring onions and serve hot.

name: Steamed Beancurd with Preserved Radish
instructions: 1. Place the block of white bean curd on a deep heatproof plate. 2. Soak the chopped preserved radish to reduce saltiness, drain well, and marinate the minced meat in a small bowl with salt, sesame oil, and cornflour for 30 minutes. 3. Heat the cooking oil in a wok or frying pan and saute the chopped shallots until fragrant. 4. Add the preserved radish and stir-fry until aromatic, then add the minced meat and fry until separated and cooked through. 5. Stir in the oyster sauce, sugar, and ground white pepper until well combined, then spoon the topping over the bean curd. 6. Place the plate into a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam over high heat for 10 minutes. 7. Top with diced spring onion and sliced red chilli, and serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Steamed Purple Rice Cake
ingredients: 150 g purple sweet potato (peeled and diced)
1 tsp cooking oil (plus extra for greasing)
instructions: 1. Peel and cut the purple sweet potato into small cubes, place in a saucepan with the knotted pandan leaves and 600 ml water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes. 2. Strain 400 ml of the hot purple liquid through a strainer into a bowl and stir in 80 g sugar until completely dissolved. 3. Sift the rice flour into a large mixing bowl, pour in the hot purple sugar liquid, and whisk until smooth and lump-free. Let the batter cool completely to room temperature. 4. In a small bowl, dissolve 1/2 tbsp sugar and the yeast in 30 ml lukewarm water and rest for 10 minutes until foamy. 5. Lightly grease a heatproof cake pan or deep plate with oil. Stir the foamy yeast into the cooled batter, cover with cling wrap, and proof for 2 hours. 6. Stir the proofed batter to release air bubbles, mix in 1 tsp cooking oil, and pour into the greased pan. 7. Place the pan in a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam over high heat for 30 minutes until a skewer inserted comes out clean. Cool completely before slicing.

name: Purple Sweet Potato Steamed Flower Buns
ingredients: 200 g all-purpose flour (sieved, for white dough)
2 g instant yeast (1 tsp, for white dough)
80 g purple sweet potato (steamed and mashed)
150 g all-purpose flour (sieved, for purple dough)
2 g instant yeast (1 tsp, for purple dough)
instructions: 1. Peel and dice the purple sweet potato, steam in a covered pot on the stove for 15 minutes until tender, and mash smoothly while hot. 2. For the white dough, combine 200 g flour, 2 g yeast, and sugar in a mixing bowl, gradually stir in 110 g milk, and knead in 6 g softened butter until smooth and soft. Wrap and chill while preparing the purple dough. 3. For the purple dough, mix 150 g flour, mashed purple sweet potato, 2 g yeast, and condensed milk, gradually stir in 60 g milk, and knead in 4 g softened butter until smooth. 4. Divide the purple dough into 10 equal balls (about 30 g each) and cover. Divide the chilled white dough into 10 equal balls (about 35 g each). 5. Flatten each white ball into a round wrapper, place a purple ball in the center, pinch to seal tightly, shape taller with your palms, and score a shallow cross across the top with a floured knife. 6. Proof the buns for 30 minutes until light, then arrange on a perforated plate inside a covered pot with cold water on the stove. Bring to a boil and steam for 10 to 12 minutes. 7. Turn off the heat and wait 5 minutes before uncovering, then serve hot.

name: Braised Black Pomfret with Tofu
ingredients: 3 blocks semi-soft tofu (cut into large cubes)
instructions: 1. Clean and pat dry the black pomfret, rub lightly with salt, marinate for 15 minutes, and dust with a little cornstarch. 2. Heat oil in a wok or frying pan and deep-fry the pomfret until golden brown, then drain onto a plate. Pan-fry the tofu cubes in the pan until golden brown and set aside. 3. Heat 2 tsp oil in a clean pan over medium heat and stir-fry the minced garlic and julienned ginger until golden and fragrant. 4. Add the spring onions and fermented bean paste and stir-fry briefly, then pour in the water, soy sauce, and sugar. 5. Bring the sauce to a boil, gently add the fried pomfret and tofu, cover, and simmer for 2 minutes. 6. Thicken the sauce with the cornstarch water, garnish with spring onions and sliced red chillies, and serve hot.

name: Chinese Steamed Tofu with Dried Shrimp
ingredients: 1/4 cup dried shrimp (soaked for 10 minutes and drained)
1 stalk green onion (cut into thin strips)
instructions: 1. Place the silken tofu on a heatproof plate inside a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam over high heat for 8 minutes. 2. Meanwhile, fry the sliced shallots in oil in a wok or frying pan over low heat until golden brown and crisp, taking care not to burn them, then set aside with the oil. 3. Heat 1 tbsp oil in the pan, fry the soaked dried shrimp until fragrant, then add 3 tbsp water, light soy sauce, and dark soy sauce. Remove from heat. 4. Drain any excess water from the steamed tofu plate, spoon the fried shallots, shallot oil, and dried shrimp mixture over the tofu, garnish with green onion and red chilli strips, and serve hot.

name: Crispy Homemade Seafood Tofu
ingredients: 8 tbsp cornstarch (3 tbsp for batter, 5 tbsp for coating)
instructions: 1. Chop the fish and prawns into smooth pastes, finely dice the carrot, spring onion, and coriander, and place the egg tofu into a large mixing bowl. 2. Add the fish paste, prawn paste, carrot, spring onion, coriander, eggs, salt, sugar, fish sauce, Shaoxing wine, and white pepper, and mash smoothly with a spoon until well combined. 3. Fold in 3 tbsp cornstarch and sesame oil until the mixture is smooth and cohesive. 4. Line a heatproof tray or plate with parchment paper, spread the mixture evenly, and smooth the top with a spatula. 5. Place into a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam over medium-high heat for 20 minutes until firm and cooked through, then cool completely for at least 1 hour. 6. Cut the cooled seafood tofu into bite-sized pieces, coat evenly with the remaining 5 tbsp cornstarch, and rest for 10 minutes. 7. Deep-fry in hot oil in a wok or frying pan over medium heat in batches until golden and crispy, raising the heat briefly at the end to drain excess oil. Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

name: Chinese Steamed Egg
instructions: 1. Crack the eggs into a mixing bowl and lightly whisk, then slowly stir in the warm water, salt, ground white pepper, and chicken stock granules. 2. Strain the egg mixture through a fine strainer into a shallow heatproof bowl and cover tightly with heatproof cling wrap. 3. Place the bowl into a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam over low heat for 10 minutes until just set. 4. Meanwhile, fry minced garlic in oil in a small pan until golden brown, and chop the spring onions. 5. Uncover the steamed egg custard, top with light soy sauce, fried garlic with oil, and chopped spring onions, and serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Steamed Minced Meat with Three Colour Eggs
ingredients: 1 tbsp fried garlic oil or sesame oil
instructions: 1. In a mixing bowl, lightly whisk the 3 eggs with the salted egg white, salt, pepper, and chicken stock granules, then stir in the warm water. 2. Stir in the minced meat, salted egg yolk chunks, and century egg chunks, and pour into an 8- to 9-inch heatproof plate. 3. Place the plate into a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam over medium-low heat for about 10 minutes until the custard is just set and firm. 4. Remove from the pot, drizzle with fried garlic oil or sesame oil and light soy sauce, garnish with chopped spring onions, and serve immediately.

name: Vegetarian Kam Heong Sauce
ingredients: 30 g vegetarian dried shrimp (soaked until soft and drained)
instructions: 1. Soak the vegetarian dried shrimp until soft, then drain well. Blend the candlenuts in a blender, dice the bird's eye chillies, and wash and drain the curry leaves. 2. Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or frying pan over medium heat and fry the curry leaves until crisp and fragrant, then lift out the leaves with a strainer, leaving the aromatic oil in the pan. 3. Add the soaked vegetarian dried shrimp, blended candlenuts, and diced bird's eye chillies to the oil and stir-fry until aromatic. 4. Stir in the curry powder, sugar, light soy sauce, vegetarian oyster sauce, and dark soy sauce, and cook over low heat for 2 minutes until well blended. 5. Cool and store in a clean container in the refrigerator, or use immediately as a stir-fry sauce.

name: Steamed Hoisin Ribs
ingredients: 500 g pork spare ribs (cut into bite-sized pieces)
15 g ginger (peeled and cut into strips)
instructions: 1. Cut the spare ribs into bite-sized pieces, toss with 1 tbsp cornstarch, rinse under running water for 1 to 2 minutes in a strainer, and pat dry with paper towels. 2. In a mixing bowl, massage the ribs with hoisin sauce, fermented bean paste, Shaoxing wine, and 1 tsp cornstarch for 1 minute until evenly coated. Cover and marinate for 1 hour. 3. Peel and julienne the ginger, and chop the spring onion and red chilli. 4. Arrange the marinated ribs on a foil-lined heatproof plate and top with shredded ginger and chopped red chilli. 5. Place the plate into a covered pot with rapidly boiling water on the stove and steam over high heat for about 30 minutes until tender. 6. Garnish with chopped spring onions, extra ginger strips, and chillies, and serve hot.

name: Bitter Gourd Pork Ribs Soup
ingredients: 1 medium carrot (peeled and cut into 1-inch rings)
instructions: 1. Blanch the pork ribs in a pot of boiling water for 5 minutes to remove impurities, then drain with a strainer and rinse clean. 2. Halve the bitter gourd lengthwise, scoop out the seeds with a spoon, rub lightly with salt, and rinse to reduce bitterness. Cut into large chunks, reserving one chunk to slice thinly. 3. Bring 2000 ml water to a boil in a large pot on the stove, then add the blanched pork ribs, red dates, carrots, and large bitter gourd chunks. 4. Once boiling again, reduce heat to low and simmer for 45 to 60 minutes. 5. Ten minutes before turning off the heat, add the soaked wolfberries and thin bitter gourd slices, season with salt to taste, and serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Crispy Stuffed Fried Tofu Puff
ingredients: 30 g dried scallops (soaked for 30 minutes and shredded)
1 tbsp cornstarch (plus 1 tbsp mixed with 1 tbsp water)
instructions: 1. Make a small slit in each tofu puff and gently turn the skin inside out. 2. Soak the dried scallops for 30 minutes until soft, drain (reserving 1/2 cup soaking liquid), and shred finely. 3. In a large mixing bowl, combine the minced pork, fish paste, shredded scallops, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, Chinese rice wine, white pepper, 1 tbsp cornstarch, sesame oil, salt, and chicken stock granules. Stir vigorously in one direction until sticky and cohesive. 4. Stuff a generous spoonful of filling into each tofu puff, smoothing the surface with the back of a spoon and pressing the edges to seal. 5. Heat oil in a wok or frying pan over medium heat and deep-fry the stuffed tofu puffs for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy. 6. Lift out with a strainer, drain on paper towels, and serve hot with sweet chilli sauce.

name: Beancurd in Thick Soup (Tofu Kan)
ingredients: 1 box soft bean curd (cut into thin strips)
