4 dried shiitake mushrooms (rehydrated and thinly sliced)
2 to 4 tbsp cornstarch (mixed with 4 to 6 tbsp water)
instructions: 1. Rehydrate the dried shiitake mushrooms and dried scallops, slice the shiitake and button mushrooms thinly, shred the scallops, dice the prawns, and cut the soft bean curd into thin strips. 2. Mix the concentrated chicken stock, oyster sauce, light soy sauce, salt, sugar, and ground white pepper in a small bowl. Mix the cornstarch and water in another small bowl. 3. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pot on the stove, add the shiitake mushrooms, button mushrooms, and shredded scallops, and stir-fry until fragrant. 4. Pour in 1.5 litres water and the seasoning mixture, cover, and bring to a boil. 5. Add the diced prawns and gently slide in the bean curd strips, cooking until the prawns are done. 6. Slowly stir in the cornstarch slurry in batches until the soup thickens, then finish with cooking wine and sesame oil. Garnish with chopped coriander and serve hot.

name: Butter Prawns with Egg Floss
ingredients: 2 cups cooking oil (for deep-frying, plus 1/2 cup for egg floss)
instructions: 1. Trim the sharp spine, whiskers, legs, and tail tips off the prawns, devein them, rinse, pat dry, season with salt in a mixing bowl, and coat evenly with cornflour. 2. Heat 2 cups cooking oil in a wok or frying pan over medium heat, fry the prawns for 2 to 3 minutes per side until cooked and golden, drain in a strainer, then double-fry briefly for extra crispiness. 3. Lightly beat the egg yolks with a whisk and strain through a fine strainer into a small bowl. Chop the garlic and dice the bird's eye chillies. 4. In a clean wok over medium-low heat, heat 1/2 cup cooking oil and melt the butter completely. 5. Pour the egg yolks from high up in a thin, steady stream while stirring vigorously in one direction with a spoon or spatula until fine golden egg strands form. 6. Reduce to low heat and fry until the mixture foams, then add the chopped garlic, curry leaves, bird's eye chillies, sugar, chicken stock granules, and fried prawns. Toss quickly and remove from heat. 7. Pour through a strainer to drain excess oil, transfer to a serving plate, and serve immediately.

name: Steamed Garlic Prawns
ingredients: 250 g medium prawns (10 prawns, butterflied and deveined)
50 g glass noodles (soaked in warm water and drained)
60 g garlic (1 bulb, peeled and chopped)
instructions: 1. Trim the prawns, slit the backs lengthwise to devein and butterfly without cutting all the way through, rinse, and pat dry. 2. Soak the glass noodles in warm water for 10 minutes and drain. Peel and chop the garlic, and dice the spring onion. 3. Heat 1 tbsp cooking oil in a wok or frying pan, lightly fry half the chopped garlic without browning, then stir in the oyster sauce and sugar until dissolved. Turn off the heat and mix in the light soy sauce, Chinese cooking wine, water, and white pepper. 4. In the same pan, heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil and fry the remaining garlic until crisp and golden brown, transferring it to a small bowl. 5. Arrange the soaked glass noodles on a deep heatproof plate, place the butterflied prawns neatly on top, and spoon the garlic sauce onto each prawn. 6. Place the plate into a covered pot with rapidly boiling water on the stove and steam over high heat for 5 to 8 minutes. 7. Top with crispy fried garlic and diced spring onions, and serve immediately.

name: Braised Tofu and Fried Beancurd Skin
ingredients: 60 g dried beancurd stick (soaked until soft and cut into 4 cm pieces)
2 stalks spring onion (cut into long strips)
1 block firm tofu (cut into 1 cm thick slices)
instructions: 1. Soak the dried beancurd sticks in water until soft and white, drain, and cut into 4 cm pieces. Slice the tofu 1 cm thick, halve and rinse the shimeiji mushrooms, mince the garlic and ginger, and cut the spring onions into strips. 2. Mix the cornstarch with 2 tbsp water in a small bowl. 3. Heat oil in a frying pan over medium-low heat and pan-fry the tofu slices in a single layer for about 5 minutes until golden and crisp on both sides, then transfer to a plate. 4. Blanch the shimeiji mushrooms in boiling water in a pot for 1 minute, drain through a strainer, and set aside. 5. Heat a little oil in a wok over low heat, saute the minced garlic and ginger until fragrant, and stir in the light soy sauce. 6. Add the fried tofu, enough water to partially cover, oyster sauce, salt, sugar, white pepper, chicken stock granules, and dark soy sauce, and simmer gently over medium-low heat for 2 minutes. 7. Add the beancurd sticks and blanched mushrooms, simmer for 1 to 2 minutes, stir in the cornstarch slurry until thickened, toss in the spring onions for 1 minute, and serve hot.

name: Steamed Eggplants
instructions: 1. Place the vegetable oil, sesame oil, and minced garlic in a small microwave-safe bowl and microwave on high for 1 minute 30 seconds, then stir in the soy sauce and mirin. 2. Peel the eggplants, quarter them lengthwise, and cut into 2-inch pieces. 3. Arrange the eggplant pieces on a heatproof plate inside a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam for 10 minutes until tender, then drain excess water. 4. Pour the garlic soy sauce over the steamed eggplants, garnish with sliced green onions and optional toppings, and serve immediately.

name: Minced Pork and Dried Scallop Porridge (Congee)
ingredients: 3/4 tsp ground black pepper (divided: 1/4 tsp marinade, 1/2 tsp porridge)
30 g ginger (2 inches, peeled and julienned)
1 fried dough cruller (yu char kway, thinly sliced)
instructions: 1. Rinse and soak the dried scallops in a small bowl of water for 30 minutes until softened. 2. In a mixing bowl, combine the minced pork with 1/4 tsp ground pepper and soy sauce, and set aside to marinate. 3. Combine the vegetable oil, sesame oil, and minced garlic in a microwave-safe small bowl and microwave on high for 1 minute 30 seconds to make garlic oil. 4. In a large pot, rinse and drain the rice 3 to 4 times until clear, then add 2.4 litres (10 cups) water and the soaked scallops. 5. Bring to a boil on the stove, partially cover with a tilted lid, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 15 minutes. 6. Stir in the marinated minced pork, breaking it up into small pieces, then season with salt and the remaining 1/2 tsp pepper and simmer for another 15 minutes, adding 120 ml water if too thick. 7. Ladle into bowls, garnish with garlic oil, sliced green onions, julienned ginger, and sliced yu char kway, and serve hot.

name: Leng Ngau Tong (Lotus Root Soup)
ingredients: 2.4 litres water (10 cups, plus water for blanching)
450 g pork neck bones or bone-in pork ribs (1 lb)
10 red dates (rinsed and soaked for 15 minutes)
450 g lotus root (1 lb, peeled and sliced 1/8 to 1/4 inch thick)
instructions: 1. Wipe the dried cuttlefish with a damp towel, place it on a baking rack, and broil in the oven for 4 to 5 minutes per side until fragrant. 2. Bring a large pot half-filled with water to a boil on the stove, blanch the pork neck bones or ribs for 4 to 5 minutes, remove with a strainer or tongs, and rinse in cold water. 3. Discard the blanching water, fill the pot with 2.4 litres fresh water, and bring to a boil. 4. Add the blanched pork bones, broiled cuttlefish, soaked red dates, and sliced lotus root, return to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours, skimming any surface scum. 5. Season with salt to taste, turn off the heat, and ladle into bowls to serve warm.

name: Steamed Glutinous Rice with Chicken (Loh Mai Kai)
ingredients: 200 g glutinous rice (soaked 6 hours or overnight)
4 dried shiitake mushrooms (soaked, soaking water reserved)
200 g boneless chicken thigh (cut into bite-sized pieces)
1/2 Chinese sausage (casing removed and diagonally sliced)
3/4 tsp salt (divided: 1/4 tsp chicken, 1/2 tsp rice)
1 1/2 tsp sugar (divided: 1/2 tsp chicken, 1 tsp rice)
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp light soy sauce (divided: 1 tsp chicken, 1 tbsp rice)
1 1/2 tsp sesame oil (divided: 1 tsp chicken, 1/2 tsp rice)
3/4 tsp ground white pepper (divided: 1/2 tsp chicken, 1/4 tsp rice)
1 tsp dark soy sauce (divided: 1/2 tsp chicken, 1/2 tsp rice)
instructions: 1. Soak the dried mushrooms for 2 hours and dried scallops for 1 hour, reserving both soaking liquids. Soak the Chinese sausage for 10 minutes, peel off the casing, and slice diagonally. 2. Drain the overnight-soaked glutinous rice and toss in a mixing bowl with 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tbsp light soy sauce, 1/2 tsp dark soy sauce, 1/2 tsp sesame oil, and 1/4 tsp white pepper. 3. Pound peeled ginger in a mortar and pestle to extract 1 tbsp ginger juice. Marinate the chicken pieces in a bowl with 1/4 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp sugar, 1 tsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, oyster sauce, ginger juice, 1/2 tsp white pepper, Chinese cooking wine, 1/2 tsp dark soy sauce, and cornflour for 3 hours. 4. Heat cooking oil in a wok or frying pan and fry the sliced shallots until golden brown, then remove and keep the fragrant oil. 5. Using a little shallot oil, stir-fry the garlic, mushrooms, and Chinese sausage, add the mushroom water, and cook until dry, then set aside. Stir-fry the seasoned glutinous rice in a little shallot oil until fragrant. 6. Divide the marinated chicken, mushrooms, Chinese sausage, and scallops into 4 small heatproof bowls, pack the fried glutinous rice on top, and spoon 4 tbsp of mushroom and scallop soaking liquid over each bowl. 7. Place the bowls into a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam over medium heat for 40 minutes. Run a knife around each bowl, invert onto small plates, and serve hot.

name: Steamed Yam Cake (Kuih Keladi)
ingredients: 500 g yam (peeled and cut into 1 cm cubes)
100 g dried shrimp (soaked, drained, and chopped)
100 g dried shiitake mushrooms (soaked, squeezed dry, and diced)
50 g preserved turnip (tai tau choy, soaked and diced)
50 g wheat starch (tang mein flour, sifted)
2 tbsp cooking oil (plus extra for greasing)
instructions: 1. Peel and cube the yam, soak and chop the dried shrimp, dried mushrooms, and preserved turnip, mince the shallots and garlic, and cube the meat. 2. Heat 2 tbsp cooking oil in a wok or frying pan over medium-high heat, saute the shallots and garlic until fragrant, then fry the dried shrimp, mushrooms, and preserved turnip until aromatic. 3. Add the cubed meat and fry until just cooked, add the yam cubes and fry until lightly browned, then stir in the salt, white pepper, chicken stock granules, and five spice powder. 4. In a large mixing bowl, whisk the rice flour, wheat starch, all-purpose flour, tapioca flour, and 1500 ml water until smooth. 5. Strain the batter slowly into the wok through a strainer over low heat, stirring continuously with a spatula until the batter begins to thicken, then turn off the heat. 6. Pour the mixture into a greased 14-inch round heatproof tray, smooth the top, place into a covered pot with boiling water on the stove, and steam over high heat for 45 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. 7. Cool before sprinkling with fried shallots, chopped spring onions, chopped red chillies, and toasted sesame seeds, then slice and serve with chilli sauce.

name: Kung Pao Chicken
ingredients: 300 g boneless, skinless chicken breast or thigh (cubed)
8 dried chillies (soaked, deseeded, and cut into 2 cm pieces)
2 stalks spring onion (white part diced, green part cut into 3 cm lengths)
instructions: 1. Place the chicken cubes in a mixing bowl with salt, egg white, white pepper, sesame oil, 1 tbsp cornflour, and 1 tbsp water, and marinate for 30 minutes. 2. Slice the garlic and ginger, cut the spring onions, and soak, deseed, and cut the dried chillies. 3. In a small bowl, whisk together the sugar, black vinegar, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, 1 tsp cornflour, and 2 tbsp water for the sauce. 4. Dry-toast the cashew nuts in a hot wok or frying pan for 3 minutes until golden brown and set aside. 5. Heat 1 tbsp cooking oil in the wok and stir-fry the marinated chicken until about 80 percent cooked, then remove to a plate. 6. Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil, stir-fry the ginger, garlic, and white spring onions briefly, then add the dried chillies and fry until fragrant and darkened. 7. Return the chicken and add the toasted cashews, pour in the sauce, and stir continuously until thickened and glossy. Toss in the green spring onions and serve hot with steamed white rice.

name: Teochew Sticky Rice Dumplings (Zong Zi)
ingredients: 68 bamboo leaves (plus hemp or grass tying strands)
1 kg pork belly (skin-on, cut into large pieces)
200 g small dried shiitake mushrooms (soaked overnight)
200 g dried prawns (soaked in warm water)
500 g shallots (sliced, fried, and oil reserved)
5 tbsp dark soy sauce (3 tbsp pork, 2 tbsp rice)
2 tbsp sesame oil (1 tbsp pork, 1 tbsp mushrooms)
4 tbsp Chinese five spice powder (2 tbsp pork, 2 tbsp rice)
3 1/2 tbsp white pepper (2 tbsp pork, 1 1/2 tbsp rice)
4 tbsp sugar (3 tbsp pork, 1 tbsp mushrooms)
Homemade red bean paste balls (optional, as desired)
instructions: 1. Boil the bamboo leaves in a large pot of water for 5 minutes until pliable, cool, wipe clean, and soak overnight with the tying strands. 2. Marinate the pork belly overnight in the refrigerator with oyster sauce, soy sauce, 3 tbsp dark soy sauce, 1 tbsp sesame oil, cinnamon sticks, star anise, 2 tbsp five spice powder, 2 tbsp white pepper, 3 tbsp sugar, and 1 tbsp optional MSG. 3. Soak the dried mushrooms overnight, then drain and season with 1 tbsp sesame oil and 1 tbsp sugar. Boil the soaked chestnuts briefly and clean off the inner skins. 4. Wash and soak the glutinous rice for 1 hour, drain in a strainer, and season with salt, 1 1/2 tbsp white pepper, soy sauce, 2 tbsp dark soy sauce, 2 tbsp five spice powder, and 1 tbsp optional MSG. 5. Fry the sliced shallots in oil until golden, reserving the shallot oil. In a large wok with shallot oil, separately stir-fry the dried prawns, mushrooms, chestnuts, and Chinese sausages, setting each aside. 6. Saute the chopped garlic in shallot oil, stir-fry the marinated pork belly with Chinese cooking wine, transfer to a tray, and sprinkle with half the fried shallots. Lightly stir-fry the seasoned glutinous rice in shallot oil over low heat and mix with the remaining fried shallots. 7. Overlap 2 bamboo leaves, fold into a cone, layer in 1 tbsp glutinous rice, one piece each of mushroom, chestnut, pork belly, salted egg yolk, Chinese sausage, red bean paste if using, and dried prawns, top with 2 tbsp rice, fold tightly, and tie securely with a strand. 8. Submerge the dumplings in a large pot of salted boiling water on the stove, cover, and boil over medium heat for about 3 hours until cooked through, then hang to air-dry for 1 hour before serving hot.

name: Teochew Peach Kuih with Yam Bean Filling
ingredients: 125 g tapioca flour (sifted, plus extra for dusting)
2 tsp salt (1 tsp dough, 1 tsp filling)
600 ml boiling water (tinted with 1 to 2 drops red food colouring)
500 g yam bean (jicama, peeled and shredded)
1/4 cup dried prawns (soaked, drained, and chopped)
5 dried shiitake mushrooms (soaked, drained, and diced)
instructions: 1. Peel and shred the yam bean and carrot, thinly slice the shallots, chop the soaked dried prawns, dice the soaked mushrooms, and cut or mince the meat. 2. Heat 3 tbsp cooking oil in a wok or frying pan over medium-low heat, saute the shallots until fragrant, then fry the dried prawns until crisp and golden. 3. Add the diced mushrooms and meat and stir-fry until the meat is cooked, then stir in the sugar, 1 tsp salt, white pepper, chicken stock granules, oyster sauce, light soy sauce, and fish sauce. 4. Add the shredded yam bean and carrot and stir-fry until softened, then transfer the filling to cool. 5. Boil 600 ml water in a saucepan and stir in 1 to 2 drops of red food colouring. 6. In a large mixing bowl, sift together the rice flour, glutinous rice flour, tapioca flour, and 1 tsp salt, gradually pour in the hot red water while stirring with a spatula until a dough forms, then cover and rest for 10 to 20 minutes. 7. Knead in the shallot oil until smooth and elastic, divide into 30 to 50 g portions, flatten each, fill with 2 tbsp yam bean filling, seal, dust with tapioca flour, press into a peach kuih mould, and unmould onto oiled banana leaf pieces. 8. Place into a covered pot with boiling water on the stove and steam over high heat for 10 minutes, brush with shallot oil while hot, and serve warm or pan-fried until golden.

name: Nasi Beriani
ingredients: Red onion, cut into large pieces
instructions: 1. Soak the basmati rice for 30 minutes. 2. Sauté the red onion and four-spice mix in ghee until fragrant. 3. Add the chicken and stir to coat. 4. Add the biriani rice seasoning. 5. Add the carrot and tomato. 6. After the rice has soaked for 30 minutes, transfer the sautéed mixture into the rice cooker. 7. Cook the rice as usual. 8. Once cooked, add coriander leaves to enhance the aroma. 9. Leave for 5 minutes, then gently stir the rice. 10. To make the cucumber pickle, combine the cucumber, carrot, onion, tomato and red chilli. Sprinkle over the sugar. 11. Add lemon juice or vinegar and mix well. 12. Serve the biriani with the pickle.

name: Kentang Varuval
instructions: 1. Fry the boiled potatoes in a little oil. Remove and set aside. 2. Add a little more oil to the pan and sauté the cinnamon and star anise until fragrant. 3. Add the red onion, garlic, ginger, dried chillies and curry leaves. Sauté until fragrant. 4. Add the chilli powder, chicken curry powder and garam masala. Season with salt and cook until the oil separates. 5. Add the fried potatoes and toss with the spices for 5 minutes. 6. Serve.

name: Tosai
instructions: 1. Wash the rice thoroughly and soak it together with the urad dal for 8 hours. 2. Take a handful of freshly cooked rice and add it to the soaked mixture. 3. Transfer the soaked rice and urad dal, along with their soaking water, into a blender. 4. Blend until smooth, with no visible rice grains. 5. Add water if necessary. The batter should be neither too thick nor too runny. 6. Transfer the blended batter into a container and cover it. 7. Leave it overnight until the batter rises to about twice its original volume. 8. Pour the batter in a circular shape onto a flat griddle and cook until the surface becomes slightly golden brown. 9. Serve.

name: Parpu Telur
ingredients: Split lentils or dhal, washed and boiled
Salt and seasoning powder, to taste
instructions: 1. Boil the split lentils (dhal) in water. 2. Add the blended onion, ginger and turmeric mixture, then continue boiling until the lentils are tender. 3. Once the lentils are soft, add the potatoes. 4. When the potatoes are tender, add the coconut milk, salt, seasoning powder and eggs. Alternatively, crack the eggs directly into the simmering gravy. 5. In a separate pan, sauté the sliced onion, garlic, dried chillies and curry leaves until golden. 6. Pour the tempering into the dhal mixture and combine. 7. Serve.

name: Gulab Jamun
ingredients: 2 tbsp ghee, for forming the dough balls
Ghee or cooking oil, for frying
instructions: 1. Combine the khoya, wheat flour, baking powder and ghee. Knead and press the mixture until no lumps remain. Shape into small balls and set aside. 2. Heat the ghee or oil over medium heat; it should not be too hot or too cool. 3. Fry the balls until evenly brown. Remove and set aside. 4. To make the syrup, combine the sugar, water, cardamom, optional rose water and saffron, and lemon or lime juice. Cook until the syrup becomes thick and sticky. Allow it to cool until warm. 5. Place the warm fried balls into the warm syrup. 6. Leave them to soak for 2-5 hours, or until the syrup has penetrated the balls. 7. Serve.

name: Kheema Kambing
ingredients: 1 large glass sour milk (1 glass of milk curdled with 4 calamansi limes)
Onion and ginger, finely blended without water or thinly sliced
instructions: 1. Season the minced meat with the fennel powder, chilli powder, paprika, turmeric powder, black pepper and yogurt. 2. Heat oil or ghee in a pan and sauté the cardamom, cloves and bay leaves. 3. Add the finely blended or sliced onion and ginger. Stir until golden brown. 4. Add the masala spice and stir carefully so it does not burn. Add a little water and cook until the oil separates. 5. Add the seasoned minced meat and stir until evenly combined and the meat changes colour. 6. Once the mixture has dried slightly and the oil separates, add the sour milk. 7. Simmer until the gravy thickens. Season with salt and seasoning powder. 8. Add chopped coriander leaves. 9. Serve.

name: Rasam
ingredients: Tamarind water mixed with 1/2 tbsp turmeric powder (use a golf-ball-sized amount of tamarind)
instructions: 1. Heat a little oil in a pot and add the mustard seeds. 2. Add the curry leaves and dried chillies. 3. Add the optional asafoetida powder. 4. Add the coarsely crushed garlic and small onion. 5. Add the tomatoes and a little water to help them cook. 6. Add the coriander roots and the remaining coarsely crushed ingredients. 7. Pour in the tamarind water and add more water until the sourness is balanced. Cook over low heat. 8. If the rasam is too sour, add more water; if it is not sour enough, add more tamarind water. 9. After 2 minutes, add coriander leaves and salt to taste. Stir and let it cook gently. 10. When small bubbles begin to appear around the edges, stir once and let it continue heating. 11. When it begins to boil, turn off the heat. 12. Serve.

name: Tikka Masala
ingredients: 100 ml heavy cream (cooking cream may be used instead)
instructions: 1. Use half of the powdered spices, salt and yogurt to marinate the chicken. 2. Mix the marinade thoroughly with the chicken and refrigerate for 2-3 hours. 3. Heat oil in a pan and sear the chicken until lightly browned. Remove and set aside. 4. In the same pan, sauté the onion, garlic and ginger until softened and fragrant. 5. Add the remaining powdered spices and cook until the spices are thoroughly cooked. 6. Add the tomato paste or purée, starting with a little and adjusting to suit the desired level of acidity. 7. Add water and simmer. 8. Stir in the heavy cream or cooking cream. 9. Return the chicken to the pan and simmer for 10 minutes. 10. Season with salt and sugar. 11. Sprinkle coriander leaves over the dish. 12. Serve.

name: Kheer
ingredients: 1/2 cup rice, washed and soaked for 25 minutes
instructions: 1. Wash and soak the rice for 25 minutes, then drain. 2. Heat 1 tbsp ghee and fry the rice for 1 minute. 3. Add the milk, palm sugar, cardamom and carrot. 4. Cook, stirring frequently to prevent the mixture from sticking. 5. Add more milk if the liquid reduces too much. 6. Check the rice and sugar; the cooking time is approximately 20-25 minutes. 7. For the garnish, fry the saffron, almonds and cashew nuts in ghee, then sprinkle them over the kheer.

name: Bubur Kuthiraivali
instructions: 1. Heat the ghee in a pot and sauté the whole spices until fragrant. 2. Add the chopped shallots and ginger-garlic paste. Sauté until the raw smell disappears. 3. Add the vegetables and cook briefly. 4. Pour in water and bring to a boil for 3 minutes. 5. Add the kuthiraivali millet and cook for 10 minutes. 6. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. 7. Continue cooking until the millet becomes soft. 8. Turn off the heat and garnish with sliced coriander and curry leaves.

name: Golgapa / Pani Puri
ingredients: 500 ml boiled, filtered or mineral water at room temperature
Bird's eye chillies, sliced, to taste
instructions: 1. Mash the cooked potatoes and mix with the diced onion. 2. Add the chopped coriander leaves. 3. Season with black pepper and salt, then mix well. 4. Add the nylon sev and combine. 5. In a separate bowl, combine the mint paste, coriander paste, pani puri masala, jal jeera and tamarind sauce. 6. Add the water and sliced bird's eye chillies according to your preferred heat level. 7. Add the lemon juice and a little sugar. Stir well. 8. Chill the sauce in the refrigerator, then sprinkle boondi over it. 9. Prepare the pani puri papad according to its package instructions. Make a small hole in the centre of each puri. 10. Fill each puri with the potato mixture and sauce. 11. Serve immediately.

name: Gula-Gula Kelapa
ingredients: 500 g granulated sugar (250 g per coconut)
Cocoa powder or brown food colouring
instructions: 1. Dry-roast the grated coconut over low heat for 10 minutes. 2. Over medium heat, add the condensed milk and cocoa powder to the pan with the grated coconut. Stir until combined. 3. Continue stirring until the sugar dissolves, approximately 30 minutes. 4. Add butter or margarine and continue stirring. 5. The candy is ready when the mixture reaches a consistency that can hold together like a ball. 6. Grease a tray with butter or margarine. 7. Transfer the mixture to the tray while it is still hot. 8. Using the back of a greased spoon, press and spread the mixture evenly in the tray. 9. Cut into pieces while it is still hot. 10. Allow to cool and serve.

name: Beef Murtabak Cheese
ingredients: Black pepper and white pepper to taste
instructions: 1. Dry-cook the minced beef in a frying pan until all liquid evaporates. 2. Add the ginger. 3. Add a little cooking oil, minced garlic, 1/3 of the diced yellow onions, and meat curry powder, adding a bit more oil if too dry. 4. Pour in 1 cup of water so the mixture becomes moist and bubbles. 5. Once the water reduces, add another 1/3 of the yellow onions. 6. Season with salt, sugar, black pepper, and white pepper along with the stock cubes. 7. Add the fried potatoes, finely mashed. 8. Stir everything together until well combined. 9. Add a splash of water if needed and mix well. 10. Cook and stir until dry, about 45 minutes, to ensure the beef is thoroughly cooked. 11. In a mixing bowl, beat the eggs with the remaining yellow onions, stir in a little of the beef mixture, and scoop 1 heaped tablespoon onto a spring roll wrapper already lined with a slice of cheese; fold into a parcel. 12. Pan-fry in a frying pan until golden brown on both sides.

name: Ayam Kurma
ingredients: Yellow onion, half cut into wedges and half thinly sliced
instructions: 1. Heat cooking oil in a wok or pot, then sauté the thinly sliced shallots, yellow onion, garlic, star anise, cinnamon stick, and cardamom pods until fragrant. 2. Mix kurma spice powder with a little water in a small bowl into a paste and add it to the pan. 3. Sauté until crisp and oil separates three times by adding a splash of water each time it dries out, taking care not to burn the spices. 4. Add the chicken and stir until coated with the spice paste, adding a little water if needed. 5. Pour in enough water to simmer. 6. Add potatoes if using; when half cooked, add the yellow onion wedges and bring to a brief boil. 7. Stir in evaporated milk, salt, sugar, and tamarind juice to taste along with optional tomatoes, large chilies, and boiled eggs; simmer briefly until cooked through, then turn off the stove.

name: Wholemeal Bread Murtabak
instructions: 1. Blend the wholemeal bread in a blender until finely ground. 2. Add the shallots, garlic, egg, chili, and a little water into the blender and blend until smooth. 3. Add the BBQ seasoning and blend again until well combined. 4. Pour the batter onto a dry frying pan without oil and cook until both sides are browned and cooked through. 5. Serve warm.

name: Mamak Spanish Mackerel Curry (Ikan Tenggiri)
ingredients: 200 g thin coconut milk (or evaporated milk)
A little cooking oil for sautéing
Tomatoes, green or red large chilies
instructions: 1. Heat oil in a wok or pot and sauté the mixed fenugreek spices, cinnamon sticks, star anise, ginger, onions, and garlic until fragrant. 2. Once softened and golden, stir in the fish curry powder mixed into a paste and the chili powder. 3. Cook until the oil separates and the gravy turns deep red, then pour in the thin coconut milk or evaporated milk. 4. Add the curry leaves, tamarind paste, salt, and sugar. 5. Once boiling, gently add the Spanish mackerel and stir slowly. 6. In a separate pot, boil water and blanch the round eggplants, then drain with a strainer. 7. Add the okra, blanched round eggplants, tomatoes, and large chilies to the curry and simmer until tender. 8. Serve hot.

name: Mamak-Style Pomfret Fish Curry
ingredients: 2 small packets curry powder (mixed with a little water to form a paste)
Bird's eye chilies or large green chilies
instructions: 1. Heat a generous amount of cooking oil in a wok or pan, then sauté the shallots, garlic, mixed fenugreek spices, and curry leaves until fragrant. 2. Add the curry paste and cook until the oil separates, stirring occasionally so the spices do not clump. 3. Pour in the tamarind juice. 4. Bring to a boil, then add the pomfret fish and cook until tender. 5. Season with salt or seasoning powder to taste. 6. Add the bird's eye chilies and okra, and stir in the tomatoes last before serving.

name: Mutton Kurma (Kurma Kambing)
ingredients: 5-6 tbsp kurma spice paste (kurma powder mixed with water, for blending)
Four-spice mix (cinnamon, star anise, cardamom, cloves)
Bird's eye chilies or green chilies
instructions: 1. Blend the shallots, garlic, half large onion, ginger, and kurma spice paste in a blender until smooth. 2. Heat cooking oil and ghee in a pot, then sauté the thinly sliced large onion, four-spice mix, and pandan leaf until golden. 3. Pour in the blended paste and cook until the oil separates, repeating 2 to 3 times if desired. 4. Add the mutton and cook until half tender, then add the potatoes and carrots. 5. Once the meat is tender, stir in the coconut milk, salt, quartered onion, and quartered tomato, and bring to a boil. 6. Turn off the stove and garnish with chilies and crispy fried shallots.

name: Mamak Fish Head Curry (Jenahak)
ingredients: 3 tbsp Adabi fish curry powder (mixed with a little water)
instructions: 1. Sauté the shallots, garlic, ginger, curry leaves, and mixed fenugreek spices in a pot until fragrant, then add the fish curry paste and sauté until crisp and oil separates. 2. Pour in enough water, stir evenly, and bring to a boil. 3. Add the snapper fish head and okra, and season with salt and sugar. 4. Stir in the tamarind juice and quartered tomatoes and simmer until cooked through. 5. Remove from the stove and serve hot.

name: Red Snapper Masala Curry
instructions: 1. Heat oil in a wok or frying pan and sauté the sliced onion, garlic, mixed fenugreek spices, and curry leaves until slightly crisp and fragrant. 2. Add the diced tomato and sauté briefly until softened. 3. In a small bowl, mix the curry powder, garam masala, turmeric powder, and chili powder with water until smooth. 4. Add the spice paste and pounded ginger-garlic paste to the pan and stir until the spices cook through. 5. Pour in water to your desired gravy consistency. 6. Stir in the tamarind juice. 7. Gently add the fried red snapper along with extra coconut milk or yogurt if a richer gravy is desired. 8. Simmer until boiling and season with salt and sugar to taste. 9. Serve warm.

name: Homemade Chicken Tandoori
ingredients: 4 chicken whole legs (washed, skin removed, and scored)
2 tsp ginger-garlic paste (from 5 cloves garlic and 3 cm ginger, finely blended)
instructions: 1. In a mixing bowl, combine the thick yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, garam masala, coriander powder, black pepper powder, turmeric powder, lime or lemon juice, salt, and red food coloring into a thick paste without adding water. 2. Rub the marinade thoroughly over the scored chicken legs, coat with 2 tablespoons of cooking oil, and marinate for at least 4 hours or overnight. 3. Arrange sliced carrots or celery on a baking tray to keep the chicken from sticking and allow air circulation beneath the meat. 4. Place the chicken on top and bake in a preheated oven at 230°C for 25 to 30 minutes. 5. After the first 20 minutes, check the chicken and brush a little oil over the surface; continue baking until cooked through, optionally broiling briefly at the end for slight charring. 6. Remove from the oven and serve warm.

name: Roti Canai
ingredients: 1 cup ice water (mixed with 2 tbsp sweetened condensed milk and a pinch of salt)
instructions: 1. Mix the sweetened condensed milk and salt into the ice water in a small bowl. 2. Pour the milk mixture into a mixing bowl with the wheat flour and margarine. 3. Mix and knead until a smooth dough forms. 4. Divide and shape the dough into round balls, then coat lightly with a little extra margarine. 5. Let the dough balls rest for 2 to 3 hours. 6. Stretch and fold each ball thin, then cook on a hot oiled frying pan until golden brown and flaky on both sides.

name: Mee Goreng Mamak
ingredients: 2 pieces firm tofu (cut into small cubes)
instructions: 1. Blend the 8 cloves garlic, small onion, dried anchovies, dried shrimp, and dried chilies in a blender into a smooth paste. 2. Heat cooking oil in a wok, add the crushed garlic, and sauté until fragrant. 3. Add the sliced large onion and fry until browned. 4. Add the tofu cubes and halved fish balls and fry until golden. 5. Stir in the blended paste and sliced tomato, mixing well, and cook until the oil separates. 6. Pour in 2 cups of water and bring to a boil. 7. Add the eggs, let them set briefly, then stir gently. 8. Add the yellow noodles, mustard greens, oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, and salt to taste, tossing until the noodles are cooked and the liquid reduces. 9. Stir in the crispy fried shallots, sliced green chilies, and coarsely ground peanuts until evenly mixed, then serve hot.

name: Homemade Garam Masala
ingredients: 12 g cinnamon sticks (broken into small pieces)
instructions: 1. Clean all whole spices to remove any dust or debris. 2. Heat a dry frying pan over low heat without oil to toast the spices in stages. 3. Start with the coriander seeds, fennel seeds, and black peppercorns, dry-roasting until fragrant. 4. Add the cinnamon sticks, star anise, and bay leaves and continue toasting until the aroma deepens. 5. Lightly toast the cardamom pods briefly so they do not burn. 6. Warm the nutmeg briefly just to release its aroma. 7. Transfer the toasted spices to a plate and let them cool completely. 8. Grind all the cooled spices in a blender until a fine powder forms. 9. Sift through a strainer and re-blend any coarse bits until fine, then store in an airtight container.

name: Prawn Biryani (Nasi Briyani Udang)
ingredients: 2 cups basmathi rice (washed and soaked for 30 minutes)
Four-spice mix (cinnamon, star anise, cardamom, cloves)
Raisins and cashew nuts, as needed
instructions: 1. Heat the ghee and cooking oil in a pot, then sauté the four-spice mix with the sliced shallots, garlic, and ginger until golden. 2. Mix the biryani spice powder with a little water in a small bowl into a paste, add to the pot, and cook until the oil separates. 3. Add the bruised lemongrass, bay leaves, bird's eye chilies, red chili, raisins, cashew nuts, and prawns; when the prawns are nearly cooked, season with salt to taste. 4. Transfer the sautéed prawn mixture into a rice cooker with the drained basmathi rice and 2.5 cups of water, and cook until done. 5. Once cooked, drizzle a little yellow food coloring over the rice, cover briefly without stirring, then fluff and serve warm.

name: Crispy Garam Masala Kale Chips
instructions: 1. Rinse and drain the kale, remove the center stems and tough ribs, tear into large pieces, and pat completely dry with paper towels. 2. Preheat the oven to 165°C (325°F). 3. Place the thoroughly dried kale in a mixing bowl, drizzle with olive oil, add salt and garam masala without oversalting, and toss to coat evenly. 4. Arrange the leaves in a single layer on a baking pan and bake for 30 minutes or until crisp. 5. Remove from the oven and allow to cool before serving.

name: Indian-Style Beef Rendang
ingredients: Four-spice mix (cinnamon, star anise, cardamom, cloves)
Beef (cut into pieces and boiled, reserving the broth)
instructions: 1. Boil the cut beef in a pot until tender and reserve the broth. 2. Dry-blend the dried chilies, cumin seeds, and fennel seeds in a blender and toast in a dry frying pan; separately blend the large onion, garlic, and ginger into a paste. 3. Heat oil in a wok or frying pan and sauté the finely sliced shallots, garlic, ginger, four-spice mix, and curry leaves until fragrant. 4. Add the toasted spice blend and stir briefly, then add the blended onion-garlic-ginger paste, sweet soy sauce, tamarind juice, salt, and sugar. 5. Pour in the boiled beef together with its reserved broth. 6. Simmer until the gravy thickens and coats the beef, then serve warm.

name: Puffy Wheat Flour Roti Puri
instructions: 1. Combine the wheat flour, cooking oil, sugar, yeast, and salt in a mixing bowl and rub together until crumbly. 2. Gradually add the hot water and knead until a smooth, non-sticky dough forms, adding a little extra boiled water if too stiff. 3. Shape the dough into ping-pong-sized balls and let rest for 15 minutes. 4. Flatten and roll each dough ball into a thin round disc. 5. Heat oil in a wok, slide in one dough disc at a time, and gently splash hot oil over the top so it puffs up. 6. Fry until golden yellow, lift out with a strainer to drain excess oil, and serve warm with curry.

name: Kambing Varuval
ingredients: 500 g mutton (cut small, cleaned, and drained)
Four-spice mix (cinnamon, star anise, cardamom, cloves)
A little sweet soy sauce (kicap manis)
instructions: 1. Toss the mutton in a mixing bowl with the turmeric powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder, and marinate for about 15 minutes. 2. Heat a little oil in a wok or frying pan and sauté the blended ginger, blended garlic, curry leaves, four-spice mix, and sliced onion until fragrant. 3. Stir in the chili paste and meat curry powder and cook until slightly crisp. 4. Add the marinated mutton and a little water, cooking until it simmers. 5. Stir in the sweet soy sauce, salt, and sugar to taste. 6. Cook over medium heat until the gravy reduces and thickens, then remove from the stove and serve.

name: Simple Chicken Masala
ingredients: 2 sprigs curry leaves (leaves stripped from stems)
A little sweet soy sauce (for darker color)
instructions: 1. Wash the chicken thoroughly and marinate in a mixing bowl for 10 minutes with a little salt. 2. Fry the chicken in a wok or frying pan until cooked through, then set aside. 3. Sauté the blended shallots and garlic in the pan until fragrant and oil separates. 4. Stir in the chili powder and curry powder. 5. Season with salt and sugar to taste, then add a little sweet soy sauce. 6. Stir until the gravy thickens. 7. Add the fried chicken back into the pan and toss until well coated. 8. Finally, stir in the curry leaves and quartered tomato, toss briefly, and serve.

name: Boiled Egg Kurma with Green Chilies
ingredients: 400 g kurma spice powder (mixed with a little water)
4 inches ginger (roughly bruised or finely sliced)
Three-spice mix (cinnamon, star anise, cardamom), as needed
Sliced red and green chilies, as needed
instructions: 1. Heat cooking oil in a large pot and sauté the finely sliced large onions until fragrant, then add the garlic, ginger, and three-spice mix. 2. Stir in the kurma spice paste and blended green chilies, cooking until the oil separates. 3. Add the knotted pandan leaves, dried tamarind slices, potatoes, and quartered onions, mixing evenly. 4. Pour in the water followed by coconut milk and stir well; once boiling and the potatoes are tender, add the boiled eggs and season with salt to taste. 5. Garnish with sliced red and green chilies and serve hot.

name: Coconut Chutney
instructions: 1. Dry-fry the chana dhal in a small frying pan for 3 to 4 minutes. 2. Combine the cooked chana dhal, grated coconut, jalapeno pepper, ginger, salt, and water in a blender, blend until smooth, and transfer to a small bowl. 3. Heat vegetable oil in a small saucepan, add the dried chilies, curry leaves, urad dhal, mustard seeds, and cumin seeds followed by the asafoetida, and turn off the stove when the chilies and curry leaves turn crisp and the mustard seeds begin to pop. 4. Immediately pour the tempered spice mixture over the coconut mixture and stir with a spoon to combine. 5. Serve with flatbreads or vadai.

name: Cucur Udang Mamak (Prawn Fritters)
instructions: 1. Add the sugar and yeast into a small bowl of lukewarm water and set aside for 5 minutes until bubbly. 2. Blend the dried shrimp finely in a blender, then add them with the salt, baking powder, turmeric powder, and yeast mixture to the flour in a mixing bowl; mix well and rest for 30 minutes. 3. Julienne the carrot, slice the shallot, chop the scallions, and gently fold them along with the bean sprouts into the batter. 4. Heat the oil in a wok or frying pan over medium heat, dip a flat stainless steel ladle into the hot oil for 3 minutes, scoop batter onto the ladle with a prawn on top, and fry for about 30 seconds. 5. Use a spoon to gently slide the fritter off the ladle and fry both sides until golden brown.

name: Cucumber, Tomato, and Boondi Raita
instructions: 1. Partially peel the cucumber leaving strips of skin, slice lengthwise into quarters, remove the seeds, halve each strip lengthwise, and cut crosswise into cubes. 2. Toss the cucumber with 1/2 teaspoon salt, set aside for 30 minutes, and drain through a strainer. 3. Quarter the cherry tomatoes lengthwise and crosswise and set aside. 4. Toast the cumin and mustard seeds in a dry frying pan for about 2 minutes, then remove and allow to cool. 5. In a mixing bowl, combine the drained cucumber, tomatoes, toasted spices, boondi, plain yogurt, and sliced mint leaves, mixing well with a spoon. 6. Serve immediately.

name: Home-Style Spiced Squid Masala (Sotong Masala)
ingredients: 500 g large squid (cleaned and cut small)
3 sprigs curry leaves (leaves stripped from stems)
instructions: 1. Place the squid in a frying pan with the marinade salt, 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder, and white pepper powder, mixing evenly. 2. Heat on the stove and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes, then remove and set aside. 3. In another frying pan, heat 2 tablespoons of cooking oil and sauté the minced garlic, diced onion, julienned ginger, and curry leaves until fragrant. 4. Add the 1/2 tablespoon turmeric powder, black pepper powder, and masala spice powder, stirring for 1 to 2 minutes. 5. Add the squid, tamarind juice, sliced green chilies, and diced tomato, stirring briefly. 6. Lower the heat and season with salt and sugar to taste. 7. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes more, sprinkle with chopped coriander leaves, turn off the stove, and serve warm.

name: Crispy Masala Vadai
ingredients: Salt, sugar, and seasoning to taste
instructions: 1. Wash the chana dhal and soak in water for 3 hours. 2. Reserve a small handful of soaked dhal aside and blend the remainder in a blender with a little water until coarsely crushed. 3. Drain excess water with a strainer, then combine in a mixing bowl with the diced shallot, fennel seeds, cut dried chilies, chopped curry leaves, and reserved whole dhal. 4. Season with salt, sugar, and seasoning to taste, and let the mixture rest for 1 hour. 5. Shape into flat patties, heat oil in a wok or frying pan, and fry until crisp and golden yellow. 6. Lift out, drain, and serve warm.

name: Indian-Style Chicken Curry
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (tossed with a little salt and turmeric)
2 large green and red chilies (halved lengthwise)
instructions: 1. Heat oil in a pot and sauté the cinnamon stick, star anise, sliced onions, garlic, ginger, and curry leaves until fragrant. 2. Add the potatoes, large green chilies, dried chilies, and tomatoes, stirring well. 3. Add the chicken and stir until it changes color. 4. Add the Babas curry powder and stir evenly. 5. Pour in enough water to submerge the chicken. 6. Season with seasoning powder or salt and add the large red chilies last. 7. Simmer until the chicken and potatoes are tender and the gravy thickens, then serve hot.

name: Traditional Thairu Vadai (Yogurt Lentil Fritters)
instructions: 1. Blend the soaked urad dhal in a blender without water, sprinkling in only a little cold water if needed until thick and smooth. 2. Mix all the ingredients together in a bowl, shape into patties, and fry in hot oil until golden brown. 3. Soak the fried vadai in warm water for 2 to 3 minutes, then gently squeeze out the excess water. 4. In a mixing bowl, stir plain yogurt with sugar, salt, and cumin powder to taste using a spoon. 5. In a small frying pan, sauté dried chilies, mustard seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, and asafoetida in a little oil, then pour into the yogurt. 6. Soak the vadai in the spiced yogurt and garnish with sliced coriander leaves or grated carrot.

name: Prawn and Drumstick Dhal Curry (Kari Dhal Murungai)
instructions: 1. Soak the dhal in water for several hours so it softens faster during cooking. 2. Blend the 5 shallots, 2 cloves garlic, and ginger with a little water in a blender until smooth. 3. Combine the blended paste, prawn curry powder, and soaked dhal in a pot, stir evenly, and cook over medium heat until the dhal is completely soft, stirring so it does not stick and adding 1 cup of water if needed. 4. Once the dhal is tender, pour in the thin coconut milk and let the curry simmer gently. 5. Add the drumstick pods, anchovy stock cube, and prawns, cooking until the prawns are tender and the gravy thickens, then season with salt to taste. 6. In a separate frying pan, heat a little oil and sauté the remaining 5 shallots, 5 cloves garlic, mixed fenugreek spices, dried chilies, and curry leaves until crisp and fragrant. 7. Pour the hot tempered aromatics into the pot of curry, cover briefly to trap the aroma, and serve warm.

name: Mamak Squid Curry (Kari Sotong Mamak)
instructions: 1. Blend the garlic and large onion in a blender until smooth. 2. Heat a little oil in a pot and briefly sauté the mixed fenugreek spices. 3. Add the curry leaves and sauté until fragrant. 4. Add the blended onion-garlic paste and sauté briefly. 5. Stir in chili paste or chili powder along with the fish curry powder until well combined. 6. Pour in a splash of water and sauté until the oil separates. 7. Season with salt, seasoning powder, and a little sugar, mixing evenly. 8. Stir in the tamarind juice and mix well. 9. Once the spiced gravy simmers, add the squid and stir to coat. 10. Cover briefly just until the squid is cooked through so it stays tender. 11. Add finely sliced large chilies, simmer briefly, and serve hot.

name: Traditional Indian Payasam (Sweet Milk Pudding)
ingredients: 1 tbsp cardamom pods (shelled and seeds finely pounded)
instructions: 1. Soak the chana dhal for 1 to 2 hours, then boil in a pot of water with a pinch of salt until tender and remove from the stove. 2. Heat ghee in a frying pan, fry the cashew nuts until golden, and transfer to a plate. 3. Fry the raisins in the same pan until plump and transfer to the plate. 4. Fry the vermicelli in the ghee until lightly browned. 5. Transfer the browned vermicelli and ghee into the pot of cooked chana dhal. 6. Place the pot back on the stove and cook for 1 minute. 7. Add the sago pearls and stir well over medium heat. 8. Pour in the sweetened condensed milk (plus sugar if sweeter is desired) and hot water, stirring every 2 minutes. 9. Add the fried cashews, raisins, and yellow food coloring, cooking until the vermicelli is soft and the sago turns translucent, adding more hot water if needed. 10. Finally, stir in the finely pounded cardamom seeds, turn off the stove, cover the pot, and let rest for 10 to 20 minutes before serving.

name: Aromatic Chicken Varuval (Ayam Varuval)
instructions: 1. Pound garlic and ginger with a mortar and pestle, then marinate half a chicken in a mixing bowl with the garlic-ginger paste, turmeric powder, curry powder, and salt for 1 hour. 2. Deep-fry the marinated chicken in hot oil until cooked and set aside. 3. Fry the fennel seeds in oil briefly and set aside on a plate. 4. Fry the dried chilies, 15 cloves garlic, and curry leaves until crisp and set aside. 5. In a wok or frying pan, sauté the sliced large onions, remaining garlic-ginger paste, and chopped tomato until the onions change color. 6. Add dried chili powder or blended dried chilies to taste. 7. Cook in the oil without adding water, using the moisture released by the onions. 8. Season with salt and sugar and cook until crisp and oil separates. 9. Stir in the fried fennel seeds, dried chilies, garlic, and curry leaves evenly. 10. Finally, add the fried chicken, toss until coated, adjust seasoning if needed, and garnish with mint and coriander leaves before serving.

name: Spiced Chicken Masala (Ayam Masala)
ingredients: Four-spice mix (cloves, star anise, cinnamon, cardamom)
instructions: 1. Combine the chicken in a mixing bowl with the yogurt, crispy fried shallots, blended ginger, and blended garlic, and marinate for 1 hour. 2. Meanwhile, dry-toast the coriander seeds, fennel seeds, and cumin seeds in a frying pan, then pound finely using a mortar and pestle. 3. Heat cooking oil in a wok or pan and sauté the sliced large onions, bay leaves, and four-spice mix until fragrant. 4. Add the chili powder, turmeric powder, and pounded spices, cooking until crisp and oil separates. 5. Add the marinated chicken and 1 cup of water, then let simmer until cooked through. 6. Season with salt and a little brown sugar, garnish with fresh coriander leaves, and serve warm.

name: 15-Minute Maggi Goreng Mamak
ingredients: 1 packet curry or tom yum seasoning
instructions: 1. Boil the 2 packets of Maggi noodles in a pot of water for 2 minutes until just tender, turn off the heat, drain with a strainer, and set aside. 2. Heat a little oil in a wok or frying pan and sauté the sliced shallot, garlic, and bird's eye chilies until fragrant. 3. Stir in the chili paste, chili sauce, oyster sauce, and 1 packet of curry or tom yum seasoning. 4. Crack in 1 to 2 eggs, let them set for about a minute, then stir gently until combined. 5. Add the fish balls, sliced fish cake, and boiled noodles. 6. Drizzle in a little soy sauce for color and toss evenly until hot, then serve immediately.

name: Odisha-Style Indian Fish Curry
ingredients: Cinnamon stick, star anise, and cumin seeds
2 tbsp garam masala or fish curry powder
instructions: 1. Toss the fish in a bowl with salt and turmeric powder, then pan-fry until three-quarters cooked and set aside. 2. Blend the ginger, 1 large onion, garlic, and 1/2 tablespoon cumin seeds in a blender and set aside. 3. Blend the mustard seeds with 1 dried chili and a splash of water into a paste, and separately blend the tomatoes until smooth. 4. Heat oil in a wok or frying pan, add the remaining whole dried chili, and fry until dark and crisp. 5. Add the star anise, cinnamon stick, fenugreek seeds, and remaining cumin seeds, sautéing until slightly crisp. 6. Add the remaining finely chopped large onion and the blended ginger-garlic-onion paste. 7. Once browned, stir in the blended tomato and mustard seed paste, stirring slowly until the oil separates. 8. Add the bay leaf, salt, garam masala, fish curry powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and coconut milk. 9. Gently fold in the fried fish until evenly coated in the gravy, garnish with coriander leaves, and serve.

name: Crispy Urad Dhal Vadai
instructions: 1. Wash the urad dhal thoroughly, soak in water for 4 hours, and drain with a strainer. 2. Blend the urad dhal in stages in a blender with a little water until a thick, slightly coarse batter forms. 3. Transfer to a mixing bowl and stir in the chopped onion, ginger, bird's eye chilies, curry leaves, fennel seeds, baking soda, salt, and rice flour until well combined. 4. Wet your hands lightly with water to prevent sticking and shape the batter into small ring-shaped patties. 5. Deep-fry in hot oil in a wok or frying pan until crisp and golden brown. 6. Lift out, drain excess oil, and serve warm.

name: Crispy Butter Murukku
instructions: 1. Warm the thick coconut milk with the salt in a saucepan until just warm, then set aside. 2. Place the dry-toasted rice flour, urad dhal flour, carom seeds, cumin seeds, and white sesame seeds in a mixing bowl. 3. Add the butter and mix evenly with a spoon until combined with the dry ingredients. 4. Gradually pour in the warm coconut milk while kneading until a soft dough forms, stopping if the dough reaches the right consistency before using all the milk. 5. Press the dough into spiral coils using a murukku mold. 6. Heat oil or melted butter in a wok or frying pan and fry the murukku until crisp and golden brown. 7. Lift out, drain excess oil, and let cool completely before storing in an airtight container.

name: Rich Mamak Fish Curry
ingredients: Pomfret, fish head, or preferred fish
2 tbsp chili paste (adjust to desired spiciness)
Tamarind paste (rubbed onto the fish to remove fishiness)
instructions: 1. Rub the fish lightly with tamarind paste in a bowl, rinse, and set aside. 2. Heat oil in a pot and sauté the sliced large onion, shallots, garlic, and ginger with the cinnamon stick, star anise, and curry leaves until fragrant. 3. Stir in the chili paste and curry powder with a splash of water and cook until the oil separates. 4. Add the dried tamarind slice followed by the fish, avoiding excessive stirring so the fish stays intact. 5. Add water gradually if the gravy is too thick, noting it will thicken further once cooked. 6. Season with salt to taste. 7. Add the okra and tomato wedges and simmer for 5 to 7 minutes until the okra is tender, then serve hot.

name: Fluffy Cheese Naan
instructions: 1. Combine the dry ingredients in a mixing bowl and stir with a spoon. 2. Add the sweetened condensed milk, cooking oil, and water, then knead until a soft, non-sticky dough forms. 3. Cover and let rise for 45 minutes or until doubled in size. 4. Knead the dough briefly and divide into 6 equal portions. 5. Roll each portion into a ball, flatten it, place about 1/2 cup of shredded mozzarella cheese in the center, seal into a ball again, and rest for 8 to 10 minutes. 6. Flatten each cheese-stuffed dough ball and cook on a dry flat frying pan over medium-low heat until golden brown on both sides. 7. Remove from the pan and brush lightly with butter before serving.

name: Crispy Mamak-Style Spiced Fried Chicken
instructions: 1. Blend the large onions, garlic, ginger, coriander seeds, and fennel seeds with 1/2 cup of water in a blender until smooth. 2. Combine the blended paste in a mixing bowl with the chicken pieces, chili powder, sugar, salt, curry leaves, rice flour, wheat flour, and tamarind juice. 3. Toss well until the chicken is evenly coated. 4. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. 5. Heat plenty of cooking oil in a wok or deep frying pan until hot and deep-fry the chicken in small batches until crisp and golden brown. 6. Lift out with a strainer, drain excess oil, and serve hot.

name: Sarawak Laksa Authentic
ingredients: 2 eggs, made into thin omelette strips
instructions: 1. Blend shallots and garlic with a splash of water. 2. Simmer prawn shells and chicken bones in a pot with bruised lemongrass for 20 minutes to build stock, then strain. 3. Stir-fry the Sarawak laksa paste with the blended aromatics in a pot until fragrant. 4. Pour in the strained stock and bring to a gentle simmer. 5. Stir in coconut milk and season with salt to taste. 6. Place blanched bihun and bean sprouts in bowls, top with shredded chicken, prawns and omelette strips, ladle over hot broth, and serve with coriander and calamansi.

name: Kek Lapis Red Velvet Sarawak (Red Velvet Layered Cheese Cake)
ingredients: 235 g wheat flour, sifted with cocoa powder (for red batter)
150 g sweetened condensed milk (for red batter)
135 g plain or mixed berries yogurt (for red batter)
1 tsp ovalette (cake emulsifier, for red batter)
1 1/2 tbsp red food coloring (for red batter)
A splash of vanilla essence (for cheese batter)
instructions: 1. For the red batter, whisk the butter and caster sugar until pale and fluffy. Add the ovalette and eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. 2. Mix in the sweetened condensed milk until smooth, then fold in the sifted wheat flour and cocoa powder gradually at low speed. 3. Stir the red food coloring into the yogurt, add to the batter, and mix gently until evenly red. 4. For the cheese batter, beat the cream cheese until smooth, add caster sugar, eggs, and vanilla essence, mix until combined, and divide into three equal portions. 5. Preheat the oven to 170-190°C and grease and line a baking tin with parchment paper. 6. Bake 3 thin layers of the red batter sequentially (about 5 tbsp per layer) until each layer sets without over-browning, then spread one portion of the cheese batter and bake until set. Repeat the pattern of 3 red layers to 1 cheese layer until finished.

name: Rendang Sarawak (Spiced Coconut Chicken or Beef Stew)
ingredients: 1 whole chicken or 1 kg beef, cut into pieces
Kerisik (toasted grated coconut paste) from 1/2 coconut
Salt and seasoning powder to taste
instructions: 1. Wash the chicken or beef thoroughly and drain well. 2. Blend or pound the ginger, shallots, garlic, lemongrass, and bird's eye chilies, then mix with turmeric powder, ground cumin, ground fennel, and coat the meat evenly. 3. Cook the seasoned meat in a wok or frying pan over medium heat until its natural juices release. 4. Pour in the coconut milk gradually while stirring. 5. Add the kerisik (toasted grated coconut paste) and finely sliced turmeric leaves. 6. Simmer until the meat is tender and cooked through. 7. Season with salt and seasoning powder to taste. 8. Continue cooking until the gravy thickens and dries to your liking, then turn off the heat and serve hot.

name: Kek Lapis Oreo Cheddar Cream Cheese
ingredients: 350 g Hong Kong flour or pau flour (superfine flour)
instructions: 1. Whisk the butter, fine sugar, and ovalette at high speed until pale and fluffy. 2. Add the cream cheese and beat until smooth, then add the eggs one at a time while mixing well. 3. Stir in the vanilla essence, sweetened condensed milk, and vanilla ice cream flour until completely smooth with no lumps. 4. Gradually fold in the Hong Kong flour a little at a time, then mix in the white food coloring evenly. 5. Preheat the oven to 180°C for 10 minutes. Line a baking tin, spread 180 g of batter for the first layer, sprinkle with grated cheddar cheese and crushed Oreos, and bake on the middle rack using top and bottom heat for 10 minutes. 6. For the second and remaining layers, switch to top grill heat only at 150°C on the lowest rack for 8 minutes per layer, pressing each cooked layer gently before adding the next batter, cheese, and Oreos until used up.

name: Pinasakan Sada (Sabah Braised Basung Fish)
ingredients: 3-5 basung fish (ikan sambong) or Indian mackerel (ikan kembung), gutted and cleaned
1/4 buah bambangan (wild Borneo mango) or 5 belimbing buluh (bilimbi)
instructions: 1. Place the sliced garlic, shallots, fresh turmeric, dried chilies, buah bambangan (or bilimbi), salt, tamarind paste, asam keping, and water into a pot and bring to a boil. 2. Add the MSG if using and simmer for 30 minutes to build the sour-savory broth. 3. Add the cleaned fish and simmer gently for another 15 minutes until the fish is cooked through and infused with the broth.

name: Hinava (Sabah Limed Raw Fish Salad)
ingredients: 1/2 bitter gourd, seeded and thinly sliced
2-3 sachets sweetener or sugar to taste
instructions: 1. Briefly scald a pot of water on the stove to sanitize utensils or blanch aromatics if desired, then combine the lime juice and calamansi juice in a small bowl. 2. Cut the fresh fish fillet into fairly thick bite-sized slices and place them in a mixing bowl. 3. Pour the lime and calamansi juice over the fish, toss evenly, and set aside for 10-15 minutes until the fish turns opaque and is cured by the citrus. 4. Rub the sliced bitter gourd with a pinch of salt, leave for 10 minutes, then rinse cleanly and squeeze out excess liquid. 5. Add the ginger, shallots, red and yellow onions, green mango, bitter gourd, and bird's eye chilies to the cured fish and toss to combine. 6. Mix the white pepper, black pepper, sweetener, and salt in a small bowl, sprinkle over the salad, and toss well. 7. Garnish with red chili slices, coriander leaves, and spring onion before serving.

name: Mee Kolok Sarawak (Sarawak Dry Noodles with Beef Soup and Roasted Chicken)
ingredients: 5 portions mee kolok (Sarawak egg noodles), blanched
1/2 inch fresh ginger, blended (for chicken marinade)
1 tsp black pepper powder (for chicken marinade)
2 tsp red food coloring (for chicken marinade)
2 inches fresh ginger, blended (for beef soup)
1 stalk spring onion, sliced (for beef soup)
Fried shallots and fried garlic, for garnish
instructions: 1. For the aromatic oil, heat 150 ml cooking oil in a wok or frying pan and fry the chopped garlic and shallots until golden. Strain the oil and set the crispy fried garlic and shallots aside for garnish. 2. Marinate the boneless chicken thighs with oyster sauce, sugar, blended ginger, blended garlic, black pepper powder, and red food coloring for 30 minutes, then roast in an oven at 180°C for 20 minutes until cooked through. Cool slightly and slice thinly. 3. For the beef soup, heat 2 tbsp cooking oil in a pot and sauté the blended shallots, garlic, and ginger with lemongrass, cinnamon stick, star anise, and cloves until browned and fragrant. 4. Add the beef and water, bring to a boil, and simmer until the beef is tender. Remove the beef, slice thinly, and season the soup with spring onion, MSG if using, and salt. 5. In a mixing bowl, toss the blanched mee kolok with the garlic-shallot oil, sweet soy sauce, dark soy sauce, white pepper powder, MSG if using, and salt until evenly coated. 6. Plate the noodles with sliced beef, roasted chicken, blanched bok choy, fried shallots and garlic, and spring onion, and serve with the hot beef soup on the side.

name: Dabai Fried Rice (Nasi Goreng Dabai)
ingredients: 3 cups cooked rice, day-old and chilled
2 tbsp buah dabai (Sarawak black olive) paste
1 stalk bunga kantan (torch ginger flower), finely sliced (optional)
Salt or light soy sauce to taste
instructions: 1. Heat the cooking oil in a wok or frying pan over medium-high heat, fry the ikan bilis (anchovies) until crisp, and set aside. 2. Sauté the sliced shallots and minced garlic in the same pan until fragrant. 3. Add the buah dabai paste and stir-fry for about 1 minute until aromatic. 4. Turn the heat to high, add the chilled rice, and toss well until every grain is coated and heated through. 5. Season with salt or light soy sauce to taste, then toss in the chopped bird's eye chilies, sliced bunga kantan, and crispy anchovies. 6. Garnish with spring onion and serve hot.

name: Kuih Lidah Buaya (Crispy Layered Kuih Tiram)
ingredients: 4 tbsp tapioca flour (tepung ubi kayu, about 31 g)
4 tbsp cooking oil (about 55 g, for layering paste)
150 g granulated sugar, blended fine for coating
instructions: 1. Mix the tapioca flour and 4 tbsp cooking oil in a small bowl until it forms a smooth, thick paste with no lumps, then set aside. 2. Combine the wheat flour and salt in a mixing bowl, pour in the melted margarine, and rub with your fingertips until crumbly. Add the egg and mix briefly. 3. Gradually pour in the cold water while kneading until a smooth, non-sticky dough forms, kneading for about 10 minutes. Shape into a ball and rest covered for 10-30 minutes. 4. Divide the dough into portions, roll each thinly, and spread a thin even layer of the tapioca paste over the surface, leaving one edge bare. 5. Roll up tightly into a log, moisten the bare edge with a little water to seal, and slice into 1 cm pieces, trimming the ends. 6. Press each piece flat with your fingers to expose the spiral layers and roll out thinly in a single pass so the layers stay distinct. 7. Heat cooking oil in a wok or frying pan over medium heat and deep-fry piece by piece until golden and puffed, gently separating the layers with a fork or skewer, then drain well. 8. Blend the granulated sugar into a fine powder and toss the cooled, oil-drained pastries in the sugar until evenly coated.

name: Manok Kacangma (Sarawak Ginger Herb Chicken)
ingredients: 1 free-range chicken (700 g), cut into small pieces
150-250 ml langkau (Sarawak rice spirit, to taste)
100 g old ginger, peeled and sliced (for ginger paste)
instructions: 1. Clean and cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and place them in a mixing bowl. 2. Dry-toast the dried daun kacangma in a wok or frying pan over medium heat without oil for 5 minutes until crisp and dry. 3. Immediately transfer the warm toasted leaves to a mortar and pestle and pound into a fine powder, then set aside. 4. Blend the old ginger with 60 ml water until smooth, strain the ginger juice directly over the chicken pieces, and reserve the strained ginger pulp. 5. Heat sesame oil in the wok over medium heat and sauté the reserved ginger pulp for about 2 minutes until fragrant. 6. Add the chicken along with the ginger juice and stir to coat evenly. Cover and cook over high heat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. 7. Pour in 450 ml water, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes. 8. Stir in the pounded kacangma powder, cover, and simmer for another 10 minutes. 9. Pour in 150 ml langkau (adding up to 100 ml more to taste), cover, and bring to a boil for 5 minutes. 10. Season with salt, stir well, and serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Mi Tuaran with Chicken Char Siu
ingredients: 1 tbsp light soy sauce (for char siu marinade)
1 tbsp hoisin sauce (for char siu marinade)
1/2 tsp five-spice powder (for char siu marinade)
1/2 tsp chicken stock seasoning powder (for char siu marinade)
2 tbsp caster sugar or to taste (for char siu marinade)
Red food coloring, optional (for char siu marinade)
22 small balls fresh wonton noodles (Tuaran noodles)
1 tbsp light soy sauce (for noodle seasoning)
1 1/2 tsp chicken stock seasoning powder (for noodle seasoning)
instructions: 1. Mix the light soy sauce, hoisin sauce, five-spice powder, 1/2 tsp chicken stock seasoning, caster sugar, honey, and optional red food coloring in a mixing bowl. Add the chicken thigh and marinate for a few hours. 2. Heat a little oil in a frying pan and pan-fry the marinated chicken until cooked through and caramelized. Rest for 5-10 minutes, then slice thinly. 3. Heat 3 tbsp cooking oil in a wok, loosen the fresh noodles, and pan-fry them evenly on both sides until lightly crisp and aromatic, then remove. 4. Bring a pot of water to a rolling boil, briefly blanch the fried noodles in small batches, and drain immediately. 5. Heat 2 tbsp cooking oil and 1 tbsp sesame oil in the wok, pour in the beaten eggs, and once half-set add the choy sum, blanched noodles, and the noodle seasoning mixture (light soy sauce, pepper, chicken stock seasoning, salt, sugar, 1 tsp sesame oil, and water). Toss quickly over high heat. 6. Plate the noodles and top with sliced chicken char siu, chopped spring onion, and red chili slices.

name: Mee Kampua Sarawak with Roasted Chicken
ingredients: 2 tbsp soy sauce (plus extra for tossing noodles)
1 tbsp vegetable oil or shallot oil (for tossing noodles)
instructions: 1. Marinate the chicken with oyster sauce, soy sauce, honey, ground black pepper, and garlic powder for at least 30 minutes. 2. Place the chicken on an oven tray, pour the remaining marinade over it, and bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes until cooked through and browned. 3. Meanwhile, boil water in a pot and blanch the mee kampua noodles for 2-3 minutes, then lift and drain well. 4. In a mixing bowl, toss the hot drained noodles with soy sauce, vegetable or shallot oil, and a pinch of black pepper until evenly coated. 5. Slice the roasted chicken, arrange alongside the seasoned mee kampua on a plate, and serve.

name: Kek Lapis Anyaman Batik Sarawak (Batik Weave Layered Cake)
ingredients: 240 g Hong Kong flour (or pau flour)
instructions: 1. Whisk the butter, caster sugar, and ovalette at high speed until pale and fluffy. 2. Lower the speed and gradually beat in the eggs and sweetened condensed milk until smooth. 3. At the lowest speed, fold in the Hong Kong flour and malt powder little by little until evenly combined. 4. Preheat the oven to 180°C using the top grill function with the fan turned off. 5. Pour 140-160 g of batter into a lined baking tin for the first layer, smooth it out, and bake until set. 6. Continue baking layer by layer using top heat only until all batter is finished, assembling woven strips if making the batik pattern.

name: Kek Lapis Tampung Seribu Sarawak (Layered Kaya and Chocolate Malt Cake)
ingredients: 1 medium can seri kaya (coconut egg jam)
500 g leftover cake crumbs or cubes
instructions: 1. Whisk the butter, fine sugar, and ovalette in a mixing bowl until pale and fluffy, then add the eggs one by one and beat until combined. 2. Mix in the sweetened condensed milk and seri kaya until smooth. 3. Fold in the pau flour, Horlicks, food whitener, and vanilla essence until well blended, incorporating the leftover cake pieces and optional grated cheese as desired. 4. Line a 9x9-inch baking tin. Pour in the first layer and bake at 150°C using top and bottom heat for 15-20 minutes until set. 5. Switch to top heat only for subsequent layers, baking each layer until golden and cooked before adding the next until all batter is used.

name: Umai Ayam (Sabah-Style Shredded Chicken Salad)
ingredients: Assorted vegetables of choice (such as cucumber, cabbage, or long beans)
instructions: 1. Bring a pot of water to a boil and poach the chicken breast until fully cooked, then remove and cool slightly. 2. Blanch the vegetables briefly in the chicken poaching water, then drain and place in a mixing bowl. 3. Pound the bird's eye chilies and garlic in a mortar and pestle until crushed. 4. Shred the cooked chicken breast finely and mix it with the pounded chili-garlic paste, lemon juice, lime juice, sliced shallots, kaffir lime leaves, blanched vegetables, and salt to taste. Toss thoroughly and serve.

name: Kek Lapis Pelangi (Rainbow Layered Cheese Cake)
ingredients: 310 g Hong Kong flour or pau flour, sifted
Fruit jam or filling of choice, as needed
instructions: 1. Beat the cream cheese, butter, sweetened condensed milk, and fine sugar in a mixing bowl until fluffy. 2. Add the ovalette and beat well, then add the eggs one at a time, mixing thoroughly. Stir in the lemon oil and lemon juice. 3. Gradually fold in the sifted Hong Kong flour until completely smooth and lump-free. 4. Divide the batter into two parts: keep part A plain white and divide part B into 7 portions tinted with rainbow colors. 5. Spread and bake each layer in a lined baking tin at 170-180°C using top heat for 7-9 minutes per layer, pressing each baked layer gently and spreading jam on selected colored layers before adding the next.

name: Kek Belacan Kukus Sarawak (Steamed Dark Caramel Chocolate Cake)
ingredients: 1 1/2 small cans seri kaya (coconut egg jam)
1 1/4 cups granulated sugar (for homemade browning sugar)
2/3 cup hot water (for homemade browning sugar)
instructions: 1. To make browning sugar, heat the granulated sugar in a saucepan over low heat until melted and dark amber, carefully stir in the hot water until smooth, and let cool completely. 2. In a mixing bowl, beat the butter, ovalette, and fine sugar until pale and fluffy. 3. Add the eggs one by one, beating well after each addition. 4. Stir in the sweetened condensed milk, seri kaya, Horlicks, cocoa powder, vanilla essence, Nestle cream, and 1/2 cup cooled browning sugar until smooth. 5. Fold in the Hong Kong flour until evenly mixed. 6. Pour into a greased baking tin, cover loosely with foil, and steam in a covered pot over simmering water for 4 hours until cooked through.

name: Kek Lapis Masam Manis Sarawak (Steamed Haw Flake Layer Cake)
ingredients: Haw flakes (asam haw flakes), as needed
instructions: 1. Whisk the chilled eggs, fine sugar, ovalette, and baking powder in a mixing bowl until thick and pale. 2. Add the vanilla essence and beat briefly, then stir in the cooking oil until combined. 3. Fold in the cake flour alternately with the evaporated milk until smooth. 4. Divide the batter into 2 or 3 bowls and tint each with food coloring. 5. Bring water to a boil in a large pot set up for steaming and grease a cake tin. 6. Spread 5 tbsp of one colored batter into the tin, arrange haw flakes on top, cover, and steam for 5-7 minutes until set. 7. Repeat layering alternating colors and haw flakes, steaming the final layer longer until completely cooked. Cool completely before slicing.

name: Kuih Cempiang Sabah (Five-Spice Fried Buns)
ingredients: 1 tbsp ground spice mix (cinnamon, star anise, and cloves)
instructions: 1. Mix the instant yeast, sweetened condensed milk, and 2 tbsp sugar into 1 cup warm water in a small bowl and let stand for 10 minutes until frothy. 2. Combine the wheat flour, 1/2 tsp salt, margarine, and milk powder in a mixing bowl, pour in the frothy yeast mixture, and knead briefly until combined. Rest the dough for 1 hour. 3. Mix the sweet soy sauce, 1 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, ground five-spice mix, and 1 tbsp warm water in a small bowl to form the filling paste. 4. Knead and roll out the rested dough into a thin rectangle, spread the spiced soy paste evenly over the surface leaving the outer edges bare, and roll up tightly into a log. 5. Slice the log into 1.5-2 cm thick rounds. 6. Deep-fry in plenty of oil in a wok or frying pan over low heat until puffed and golden brown, then drain.

name: Tempoyak Goreng Ikan Bilis Sarawak (Fried Fermented Durian with Anchovies)
ingredients: 2 stalks tepus (Borneo wild torch ginger stem), sliced
instructions: 1. Heat cooking oil in a wok or frying pan over medium heat and fry the pusuk (dried anchovies) until crisp, then remove and set aside. 2. In the same pan, sauté the sliced shallots, garlic, red chilies, and tepus until fragrant and softened. 3. Add the tempoyak and stir continuously over medium-low heat until thickened and aromatic. 4. Season with sugar and salt to taste, fold the fried anchovies back in, and serve warm.

name: Bunga Durian Goreng (Stir-Fried Durian Blossoms with Dried Shrimp)
ingredients: 300 g bunga durian (durian blossoms), tips trimmed and washed
instructions: 1. Trim the tips from the durian blossoms, wash thoroughly, and drain in a strainer. 2. Pound the shallots, garlic, dried shrimp, bird's eye chilies, and optional belacan in a mortar and pestle until coarse. 3. Heat cooking oil in a wok or frying pan and sauté the pounded paste until fragrant and the oil separates. 4. Add the drained durian blossoms and stir-fry evenly. 5. Season with salt and seasoning powder, add a splash of water for light gravy if desired, and stir-fry until tender and cooked through.

name: Kuih Celorot Sarawak (Steamed Palm Sugar Rice Cakes in Nipah Cones)
ingredients: 130 g gula Melaka (or gula apong / palm sugar)
Nipah palm leaves and coconut skewers, shaped into upright cones
instructions: 1. Bring water to a boil in a large pot for steaming and arrange the nipah leaf cones upright in a heatproof dish or tray. 2. In a saucepan, simmer the coconut milk, 50 ml water, palm sugar, and salt while stirring until the sugar dissolves completely. 3. Place the sifted rice flour in a mixing bowl and pour in the warm palm sugar coconut milk mixture, whisking until smooth and lump-free. 4. Pour the batter into the upright nipah leaf cones and steam in the covered pot for about 30-45 minutes until firm and cooked through.

name: Kuih Bongkol Sarawak (Steamed Coconut Pandan Rice Pudding)
ingredients: A splash of vanilla essence (for topping)
Gula apong (nipah palm sugar), as filling
Banana leaves, softened over low flame and cut into squares
Toothpicks or bamboo skewers, for securing
instructions: 1. Whisk the rice flour, 3 cups water, and pandan paste together in a mixing bowl until smooth and set aside. 2. In a pot, heat 1-1.5 liters water with 250 ml thick coconut milk, pandan leaves, and salt until boiling. 3. Reduce to low heat, pour in the rice flour slurry, and stir continuously until thickened into a soft custard-like paste; remove from heat and cool slightly. 4. In a separate bowl or blender, mix the eggs, 1 cup thick coconut milk, sugar, and vanilla essence until smooth. 5. Soften the banana leaves over a low stove flame, fold into neat cups or parcels, place 1 tbsp gula apong at the base, top with 2-3 tbsp of the thickened rice paste, pour over the egg-coconut mixture, and fold shut, securing with a toothpick. 6. Steam in a covered pot over boiling water for 15-20 minutes until set.

name: Kuih Penyaram (Sarawak Gula Apong Fritters)
instructions: 1. Combine the wheat flour, rice flour, gula apong, water, and optional white sugar in a mixing bowl and stir with a spoon until mixed. 2. Transfer to a blender and blend until completely smooth, then chill in the refrigerator overnight. 3. Heat oil in a small wok or frying pan over medium-high heat, ladle in a portion of batter, and fry until the edges are crisp and lacy and the center puffs and cooks through, then drain.

name: Kek Kota Sabah (No-Bake Milo Peanut Biscuit Cake)
ingredients: 1 packet Marie biscuits, broken into pieces
instructions: 1. Dry-roast the peanuts in a wok or frying pan over medium-low heat without oil until fragrant and cooked, then cool and crush coarsely with a mortar and pestle. 2. Combine the sweetened condensed milk, broken Marie biscuits, Milo powder, and crushed peanuts in a mixing bowl and mix thoroughly. 3. Press the mixture evenly into a plastic-lined tray and smooth the surface with a spoon. 4. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour until firm before slicing.

name: Umai Udang Sarawak (Limed Raw Prawn Salad)
ingredients: 500 g medium fresh prawns, peeled, deveined, and cut into small pieces
Turmeric leaves, celery leaves, coriander leaves, and sliced lemongrass, for garnish (optional)
instructions: 1. Briefly scald a pot of water on the stove to rinse tools or blanch aromatics if preferred, then marinate the cut prawns with calamansi lime juice and salt in a mixing bowl. 2. Pound the shallots, garlic, ginger, belacan, and red chili in a mortar and pestle until smooth. 3. Add the pounded spice paste, sliced onion, bird's eye chilies, ground peanuts, vinegar, and sugar to taste into the prawn bowl and mix well. 4. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour until the prawns turn opaque and cure in the lime juice. 5. Garnish with herbs and lemongrass if using and serve with hot rice.

name: Kek Lapis Kukus Merdeka (Steamed Layered Jam Cake)
ingredients: 150 ml corn oil or cooking oil
Blue, red, and yellow food colorings
Mixed fruit jam (or jam of choice)
instructions: 1. Whisk the eggs, caster sugar, ovalette, vanilla essence, and salt in a mixing bowl until pale, thick, and fluffy. 2. Beat in the wheat flour gradually at low speed until incorporated. 3. Mix in the coconut milk at low speed, then fold in the oil gently with a spatula until smooth. 4. Set aside 2 small ladles of batter tinted yellow for decorative cutouts, and divide the rest into 4 portions (white, blue, red, and yellow). 5. Bring water to a boil in a large pot for steaming and line an 8x8-inch tin with parchment paper. 6. Steam the 2 ladles of yellow batter for 10 minutes first, then steam each main colored layer for 10 minutes (15 minutes for the final layer) until cooked through. 7. Cool completely, slice into strips, spread fruit jam between slices to assemble patterned layers, and top with the yellow cutouts.

name: Biskut Makmur Sabah (Peanut Melt-in-Mouth Cookies)
