instructions: 1. Dry-toast the wheat flour in a wok or frying pan over low heat while stirring constantly until light and aromatic, then cool and sift. 2. Melt the margarine and ghee in a small pan and let cool. 3. In a mixing bowl, combine the toasted flour, blended peanuts, icing sugar, and milk powder, then mix in the melted margarine and ghee until a pliable dough forms. 4. Shape into small balls and arrange on a baking tray. 5. Bake in the oven at 150°C for 20 minutes until lightly browned underneath. 6. Allow the cookies to cool completely, then dust or toss in a mix of milk powder and icing sugar.

name: Kek Lapis Dilwale Sarawak (Layered Chocolate Strawberry Cheesecake)
ingredients: 1 small can seri kaya (coconut egg jam)
instructions: 1. Beat the butter and 130 g caster sugar in a mixing bowl until pale and fluffy, then add the 10 eggs one by one and whisk until smooth. 2. Mix in the seri kaya, sweetened condensed milk, 150 g wheat flour, Horlicks, milk powder, and vanilla essence at low speed until combined. 3. Divide the batter in half: stir strawberry jam and red food coloring into one half, and chocolate spread and browning sugar into the other. 4. Bake the dark chocolate batter layer by layer under the oven's top grill at 190°C, followed by the red strawberry batter layer by layer until both halves are used. 5. Whisk the cream cheese, 100 g caster sugar, 3 eggs, cold water, and 3 tbsp wheat flour until smooth, pour over the baked layers, cover with foil, and steam in a pot or water bath until the cheese layer is set.

name: Mee Udang Ala Sarawak (Sarawak-Style Prawn Noodles)
ingredients: 2 packets curry instant noodles with seasoning
instructions: 1. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pot and fry the prawn heads and cleaned prawns until aromatic and cooked, then set the prawns aside and discard the heads after extracting flavor. 2. Blend the shallot, ginger, garlic, fresh chilies, and soaked dried shrimp until smooth. Heat 3 tbsp oil in the pot and sauté the blended paste until fragrant. 3. Stir in the curry noodle seasoning packets, pour in water, and bring to a simmer. 4. Add the fishballs, mashed sweet potato, fried prawns, and palm sugar, simmering until the broth thickens slightly. 5. Cook the instant noodles for 2 minutes until just tender, place in a serving bowl, ladle over the hot prawn broth, and garnish with mustard greens, spring onion, boiled egg, lime, and green chili.

name: Lada Sabah (Sabah Pickled Bird's Eye Chili Sauce)
ingredients: 100 g lada putih Sabah (white/Sabah bird's eye chilies), stemmed
1 cup white vinegar (enough to cover chilies)
instructions: 1. Place the stemmed Sabah chilies, peeled garlic, young ginger slice, vinegar, salt, sugar, and optional MSG into a blender. 2. Blend until completely smooth and transfer to a clean airtight bottle. 3. Before serving, spoon a portion into a small bowl and finish with freshly squeezed calamansi or lime juice, and optional soy sauce to taste.

name: Ambuyat with Sambal Belacan (Borneo Sago Paste)
ingredients: 1 kg (6 cups) tepung sagu rumbia (sago palm flour)
1 liter (4 cups) room-temperature water (for soaking sago)
Boiling water, freshly boiled (for setting ambuyat)
1 block toasted belacan (fermented shrimp paste, for sambal)
Bird's eye chilies or red chilies, to taste (for sambal)
Seasoning powder and a pinch of sugar (for sambal)
instructions: 1. Stir the sago flour with 4 cups water in a mixing bowl and let settle for 10 minutes, then pour off the excess water and transfer the damp sago sediment into a heatproof mixing bowl. 2. Boil water in a pot on the stove, then slowly pour the freshly boiling water into the sago while stirring vigorously until the mixture turns translucent and forms a thick, glossy glue-like paste. 3. For the sambal belacan, pound the toasted belacan, chilies, seasoning powder, sugar, and lime juice in a mortar and pestle until smooth. Serve the hot ambuyat alongside the sambal belacan.

name: Kek Lapis Cempedak Sarawak (Jackfruit Layered Cake)
ingredients: 600 g cempedak (chempedak jackfruit) flesh, seeded (for puree)
instructions: 1. To prepare the cempedak puree, blend the seeded cempedak flesh, 220 g caster sugar, and water until smooth, then cook in a saucepan over low heat while stirring until thick. Measure out 150 g for the batter and reserve the rest for layering. 2. Beat the butter, condensed milk, cempedak essence, and vanilla essence at high speed until pale and fluffy. 3. In a separate mixing bowl, whisk the egg yolks, egg whites, 270 g caster sugar, and ovalette at high speed until thick and voluminous, then fold into the butter mixture. 4. Gradually fold in the Hong Kong flour, milk powder, and 150 g cempedak puree until smooth. 5. Line a 10x7-inch or 8x8-inch tin. Bake the first layer at 170-180°C using top and bottom heat for 5 minutes, then switch to top heat until golden. 6. Bake the second layer using top heat, spread 2-3 tbsp of cempedak puree over it, and bake until dry. Repeat every 2 layers, lowering the oven to 130-140°C with top and bottom heat for 10-15 minutes on the final layer.

name: Kek Buah Kukus Sarawak (Steamed Fruit Cake)
ingredients: 1/2 can fine sugar or caster sugar (measured using 399 g milk tin)
3 1/2 cans wheat flour (measured using 399 g milk tin)
instructions: 1. Whisk the butter and caster sugar in a mixing bowl until pale and fluffy. 2. Add the eggs one at a time along with the vanilla essence, beating well after each addition. 3. Stir in the sweetened condensed milk until smooth. 4. Fold in the wheat flour and baking powder using a spoon until evenly combined, then stir in the red dates, green and red cherries, and mixed and black raisins. 5. Rest the batter covered at room temperature overnight. 6. Transfer into a greased 9x9-inch tin, cover loosely with foil, and steam in a covered pot over boiling water for 4 hours until fully cooked. Cool completely before slicing.

name: Lempeng Sagu Sarawak (Crispy Sago Coconut Pancakes)
ingredients: A little cooking oil, for greasing the pan
Sugar or sambal ikan bilis (anchovy sambal), for serving
instructions: 1. Combine the sago flour, grated coconut, and salt in a mixing bowl. 2. Gradually sprinkle in water while mixing until the mixture is damp and crumbly enough to press together lightly. 3. Lightly grease a wok or frying pan with cooking oil and heat over low heat. 4. Scoop a portion of the sago mixture directly into the pan and press it out thinly and evenly. 5. Cook slowly over low heat until the underside turns crisp and lightly golden, flip carefully, and cook the other side until crisp. 6. Serve warm with sugar or anchovy sambal.

name: Kuih Pisang Hijau Sabah (Green Pandan Banana Rolls in Coconut Sauce)
ingredients: 4 pandan leaves, blended with water and strained (for green wrapper)
A few drops green food coloring (for green wrapper)
Red rose syrup, sweetened to taste (for serving)
4-5 pisang raja (ripe raja bananas), steamed or boiled until tender
instructions: 1. Blend the pandan leaves with water and strain the juice. Combine the wheat flour, egg, salt, green food coloring, and pandan juice in a mixing bowl or blender until smooth and lump-free. 2. Heat a lightly greased frying pan over low heat, ladle in a thin layer of green batter like a crepe, cook until set, and remove to a plate. 3. Place a boiled or steamed pisang raja onto each green crepe and roll up neatly. 4. For the coconut sauce, heat the coconut milk in a saucepan until simmering, gradually stir in the rice flour dissolved in a little water and sugar until thickened into a smooth, glossy sauce. 5. Slice the banana rolls, ladle the coconut sauce over them, drizzle with sweet rose syrup, and serve chilled or over ice.

name: Kek Lapis Milo Horlicks Sarawak
ingredients: 1/2 cup cream crackers, finely blended and sifted
instructions: 1. Sift together the wheat flour, baking powder, and finely blended cream crackers into a bowl. 2. Whisk the butter and caster sugar in a mixing bowl until pale and fluffy, then beat in the eggs one by one. 3. Mix in the vanilla essence and sweetened condensed milk until smooth. 4. Fold in the sifted dry ingredients alternately with the evaporated milk until smooth, then divide the batter into two bowls: stir Horlicks into one half and Milo into the other. 5. Bring water to a boil in a large pot for steaming. Pour a thin layer of one batter into a lined cake tin and steam for 7 minutes until set, then alternate with the other flavor until all batter is used. 6. Steam the final layer for 45 minutes until cooked through, then cool before slicing.

name: Kapurung Sabah (Sago Pearls in Sardine and Vegetable Soup)
ingredients: 1 ear sweet corn, kernels sliced off
100 g long beans, cut into short lengths
Salt and seasoning powder to taste
Prepared ambuyat (sago paste balls), for serving
instructions: 1. Bring water to a boil in a pot, add the corn kernels, long beans, water spinach, and banana blossom, and simmer until the vegetables are tender. 2. Pour in the canned sardines along with their sauce and stir gently. 3. In a wok or frying pan, fry the dried anchovies and peanuts separately until crisp, drain, and pound or coarsely grind them with a mortar and pestle. 4. Stir the crushed anchovies and peanuts into the vegetable soup, season with salt and seasoning powder to taste, and simmer briefly. 5. Serve hot with spoonfuls of ambuyat, blended bird's eye chilies, and freshly squeezed lime juice.

name: Kuih Cincin Sabah (Crispy Palm Sugar Ring Fritters)
ingredients: 1-2 blocks gula Melaka or palm sugar (gula kabung)
1 cup rice flour, whisked with water into a thin dipping batter
instructions: 1. Chop the gula Melaka and combine with the dark brown sugar and 1 1/2 cups water in a saucepan. Simmer until melted, then remove from heat and let cool slightly. 2. Mix the white sugar, 2 tbsp cooking oil, and salt in a mixing bowl, pour in the warm palm sugar syrup, and stir well. 3. Add the wheat flour and knead into a soft, smooth dough. 4. Roll the dough out thinly on a lightly floured surface and cut out large rounds with smaller holes punched inside to form rings. 5. Dip each ring briefly in water and deep-fry in hot oil in a wok or frying pan until crisp, then lift out and drain. 6. Dip the fried rings into the rice flour batter and deep-fry a second time until golden and extra crunchy.

name: Umai Ikan Tenggiri Sarawak (Limed Mackerel Salad)
ingredients: 500 g fresh Spanish mackerel (ikan tenggiri) fillet, deboned and thinly sliced
instructions: 1. Briefly boil a pot of water to sanitize your cutting board or knife if desired, then place the sliced mackerel fillet in a mixing bowl, pour in the calamansi lime juice, and toss gently. Let cure for about 20 minutes until the fish turns opaque white. 2. Blend or pound the bird's eye chilies, shallots, and belacan until smooth. 3. Add the chili-belacan paste, salt, seasoning powder, sliced yellow onion, and julienned calamansi peel to the cured fish. 4. Toss gently so the fish slices stay intact and serve immediately.

name: Kelupis Sarawak (Steamed Glutinous Rice Rolls)
ingredients: 500 g glutinous rice (beras pulut), washed and drained
600 ml thick coconut milk (enough to cover the rice)
Palas palm leaves (daun palas), for wrapping
instructions: 1. Place the glutinous rice in a wok or pot, pour in thick coconut milk until it sits just above the rice level, season with salt, and cook over medium heat while stirring continuously so the bottom does not scorch until the coconut milk is absorbed. 2. Transfer the partially cooked glutinous rice to a covered pot on the stove pot and steam until tender. 3. Spread the steamed rice onto a tray, cut into equal portions, and shape each into neat logs. 4. Wrap each rice log tightly in a palas leaf, bundle 4-5 wrapped logs together, and tie securely with twine. 5. Return the wrapped bundles to the pot and steam for another 40-60 minutes before serving with rendang or curry.

name: Coto Makassar (Spiced Beef and Peanut Soup)
ingredients: 500 g beef or chicken, cut into small pieces
Salt and seasoning powder to taste
Fried shallots and chopped celery leaves, for garnish
Pounded chili paste, sweet dark soy sauce, and lime wedges, for serving
instructions: 1. Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, and large onion with a splash of water until smooth. 2. Heat a little oil in a wok or frying pan and sauté the blended paste until dry and fragrant, then set aside. 3. Dry-fry or lightly fry the raw peanuts until half-cooked, then blend until finely ground. 4. Place the beef (or chicken) into a pot of water with salt, cloves, star anise, and cinnamon stick, and boil until tender. Slice or shred the cooked meat and keep it in the broth. 5. Stir the sautéed spice paste and ground peanuts into the pot, season with salt and seasoning powder, and simmer until rich and aromatic. 6. Garnish with fried shallots and celery leaves and serve with chili paste, dark soy sauce, and lime.

name: Ikan Terubuk Masin Goreng Bawang (Sarawak Crispy Salted Toli Shad with Onions)
ingredients: 1 salted terubuk fish (ikan terubuk masin / salted toli shad), cut into pieces
2 red or bird's eye chilies, sliced
instructions: 1. Heat the cooking oil in a wok or frying pan over medium heat and fry the salted terubuk fish pieces (keeping the scales on for crispness) until golden brown and crunchy, then transfer to a plate. 2. In the same oil, quickly sauté the sliced onion and chilies until fragrant and just softened, keeping some crispness. 3. Spoon the sautéed onions and chilies over the crispy fried fish, squeeze fresh calamansi lime juice on top, and serve immediately with steamed rice.

name: Burasak Sabah (Bugis Coconut Milk Rice Cakes)
ingredients: Young banana leaves, cut into A4-sized sheets
Large banana leaves, for outer wrapping
instructions: 1. Combine the washed rice, coconut milk, water, and salt in a rice cooker or pot and cook until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is nearly tender. 2. Wrap portions of the coconut rice tightly in the A4-sized banana leaf sheets, pressing each parcel flat and compact without making it too thick or thin. 3. Stack 6 flattened parcels together, wrap them tightly inside a large banana leaf, and tie securely with kitchen twine. 4. Submerge the tied bundles in a large pot of water and boil for 8 hours, topping up hot water as needed, then drain and cool before slicing.

name: Ikan Terubuk Masin Masak Sambal Cili Api (Sarawak Salted Fish in Bird's Eye Chili Sambal)
ingredients: 1 salted terubuk fish (ikan terubuk masin), cut into pieces
Sugar and seasoning powder to taste
1/2 tsp belacan (fermented shrimp paste, for pounding)
6 red or green bird's eye chilies (for pounding)
Cooking oil, for frying and sautéing
instructions: 1. Soak the cut salted terubuk fish pieces in a bowl of water for 30 minutes to reduce excess saltiness, then drain well. 2. Coarsely pound the large onion, shallots, garlic, belacan, large red chilies, and bird's eye chilies in a mortar and pestle. 3. Heat cooking oil in a wok or frying pan and fry the salted fish until golden and cooked, then set aside. 4. In the same pan with a little oil, sauté the coarsely pounded chili paste until fragrant and the oil separates. 5. Stir in the tamarind juice, sugar, and seasoning powder (omit extra salt since the fish is salty). 6. Add the sliced onion, sliced red chilies, and quartered tomato, cooking until slightly softened, then toss the fried salted fish back in until coated.

name: Mee Belacan Sarawak (Fermented Shrimp Paste Noodles)
ingredients: 1 packet rice vermicelli (bihun), soaked and blanched
1 tbsp belacan (preferably Bintulu fermented shrimp paste)
2 tbsp gula apong (nipah palm sugar) or gula Melaka
2 tbsp otak udang (hae ko / fermented prawn paste)
1 tsp cornstarch, mixed with a little water
Sweet soy sauce and salty soy sauce, to taste
Century egg (telur padi), halved or quartered (for serving)
Rehydrated cuttlefish (sotong kembang), blanched and sliced (for serving)
Dried chilies and toasted belacan, blended with seasoning (for chili sambal)
instructions: 1. Blend the shallots, garlic, large onion, dried chilies, belacan, and dried shrimp until smooth. 2. Heat cooking oil in a pot and sauté the blended paste until fragrant and the oil separates. 3. Pour in the water and add the asam keping, sweet and salty soy sauces, oyster sauce, otak udang, gula apong, and chicken stock cube, simmering and adjusting sweet, salty, and tangy flavors. 4. Stir in the cornstarch slurry to lightly thicken the gravy. 5. For the chili sambal, blend extra dried chilies with toasted belacan, sauté until the oil separates, and season to taste. 6. Serve the blanched rice vermicelli topped with the warm gravy, bean sprouts, cucumber, century egg, cuttlefish, crushed peanuts, calamansi lime, and chili sambal.

name: Kek Lapis Neopolitan Sarawak
instructions: 1. Whisk the egg yolks, egg whites, ovalette, and caster sugar in a mixing bowl until pale and fluffy. 2. In another mixing bowl, beat the butter and vanilla essence until light and creamy, then combine both mixtures smoothly. 3. Sift together the vanilla ice cream flour, milk powder, Hong Kong flour, and baking powder, and fold into the batter gradually until smooth. 4. Divide the batter into three portions: flavor one with strawberry emulco, one with chocolate and mocha emulco, and leave the third plain. 5. Grease and line an 8-inch baking tin, spread 4 tbsp of batter per layer, and bake layer by layer under the oven's top grill at 200°C for 4-5 minutes each, pricking air bubbles and pressing each baked layer gently before adding the next.

name: Acar Timun Sarawak (Sarawak Spiced Pickled Cucumber)
ingredients: 300 g cucumber, seeded and cut into 3 cm strips
150 g carrot, peeled and cut into 3 cm strips
2 red chilies, seeded and cut into 3 cm strips
2 green chilies, seeded and cut into 3 cm strips
2 tbsp dried shrimp (udang kering), soaked until soft (plus 1 tbsp for spice paste)
instructions: 1. Toss the cucumber and carrot strips with vinegar in a mixing bowl and marinate for 4 hours, then drain in a strainer and sun-dry until thoroughly dry (up to 1 day). 2. Blend the garlic, shallots, 1 tbsp soaked dried shrimp, red chili, bird's eye chilies, ginger, and candlenuts into a smooth paste. 3. Heat cooking oil in a wok or frying pan and sauté the spice paste until fragrant and the oil separates. 4. Add the dried cucumber and carrot strips, sliced red and green chilies, remaining soaked dried shrimp, and turmeric powder, tossing well. 5. Season with salt and sugar, transfer to a serving dish, sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds, and serve with crispy keropok.

name: Bubur Pedas and Kuih Bongkol Sarawak (Spiced Porridge and Steamed Pudding)
ingredients: 4 tbsp rempah bumbu (Sarawak spiced toasted-rice bubur pedas paste)
250 ml thick coconut milk (for bubur pedas)
50 g dried beancurd skin (fuchuk), soaked and sliced
50 g dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and sliced
50 g wood ear mushrooms, soaked and sliced
Vietnamese coriander leaves (daun kesum), finely sliced
Salt, sugar, cooking oil, and water, as needed
6 shallots and 2 cloves garlic, blended (for bubur pedas)
150 g rice flour and 70 g tapioca flour (for kuih bongkol)
650 ml thin coconut milk and 200 ml thick coconut milk (for kuih bongkol)
3 tbsp granulated sugar and 1/2 tsp salt (for kuih bongkol)
2 pandan leaves, knotted, banana leaves, toothpicks, and 150 g diced gula Melaka or gula apong (for kuih bongkol)
instructions: 1. For the bubur pedas, heat oil in a pot and sauté the blended shallots and garlic, chili paste, and dried shrimp until fragrant. 2. Add the diced potatoes, sweet potato, carrot, rempah bumbu, water, and 250 ml thick coconut milk, simmering 1-2 minutes until tender. 3. Stir in the turmeric leaf, shiitake mushrooms, wood ear mushrooms, lily buds, fuchuk, and daun kesum, then add the long beans, baby corn, prawns, tamarind juice, salt, and sugar, simmering until boiling and cooked through. 4. For the kuih bongkol, mix the rice flour, tapioca flour, 650 ml thin coconut milk, 3 tbsp sugar, and salt in a saucepan over low heat until thick and smooth. 5. Spoon onto softened banana leaves lined with pandan leaf, top with diced gula Melaka or gula apong and 200 ml thick coconut milk, fold into neat parcels secured with toothpicks, and steam in a pot for 25-30 minutes.

name: Mee Goreng Udang and Pastel (Sabah Prawn Fried Noodles and Noodle Curry Puffs)
ingredients: 500 g yellow egg noodles (mee kuning, for mee goreng udang)
1 kg fresh prawns, peeled (shells used for prawn stock)
125 ml cooking oil plus 4 tbsp cooking oil
3 tbsp chili sauce (plus extra for pastel)
3 tbsp oyster sauce (plus extra for pastel)
1 egg (for mee goreng udang) and boiled eggs (for garnish)
4 cloves garlic, blended (plus extra for pastel)
Fried shallots, sliced spring onion, and calamansi limes, for garnish
1 kg wheat flour, 2 tbsp margarine, and salted water (for pastel pastry)
200 g rice vermicelli (bihun), yellow onion, red chilies, vinegar, salt, and MSG (for pastel filling)
instructions: 1. Simmer the prawn shells in 2 liters of water to make prawn stock. Heat oil in a wok, sauté the blended shallots, garlic, and soaked chilies until cooked, then stir in chili sauce, tomato sauce, oyster sauce, and soy sauce. 2. Pour in the prawn stock and yellow noodles, adding water as needed until tender, then add the prawns, white pepper, sugar, and beaten egg, tossing well before garnishing with fried shallots, spring onion, boiled egg, and calamansi lime. 3. For the Sabah pastel (noodle curry puffs), pound red chilies and garlic in a mortar and pestle, sauté with sliced yellow onion until crisp, add chili sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, and pre-soaked bihun, toss evenly, and cool. 4. Knead wheat flour, margarine, and salted water into a smooth pastry dough, flatten into circles, fill with the seasoned bihun, fold and crimp into half-moon puffs, and deep-fry in hot oil until golden and crisp.

name: Oven-Roasted Herb Chicken & Potato Wedges
instructions: 1. Preheat oven to 200°C. 2. Optionally par-cook potato wedges in the microwave for 3 minutes to cut roasting time in half. 3. Toss chicken, potato wedges, onion, carrot and garlic with oil, paprika, black pepper and salt on a baking tray. 4. Roast for 25-30 minutes until the chicken is golden and potatoes are crispy outside and fluffy inside. 5. Serve warm.

name: Kuih Bingka Ubi (Baked Tapioca Cake)
instructions: 1. Preheat the oven to 170°C and line a 23x5 cm square cake tin with banana leaf (oiled on the shiny side). 2. Peel yellow tapioca tubers and grate finely to yield 1 kg, then place in a strainer over a mixing bowl for 30 minutes to drain. 3. Slowly pour off the liquid from the bowl, leaving the tapioca starch settled at the bottom, then return the strained tapioca to the bowl and mix with the starch. 4. Add the sugar, beaten eggs, and salt, and stir until the sugar dissolves. 5. Crush and twist the pandan leaves into the mixture to extract their aroma, then stir in the coconut milk and water before discarding the pandan leaves. 6. Pour the batter into the prepared tin, smooth the top with a spatula, and bake for 1 hour 15 minutes until golden brown. 7. Let the cake cool in the tin for 30 minutes, then unmold and cool completely for 1 hour before slicing with an oiled knife and serving at room temperature.

name: Crispy Apam Balik (Crispy Crepes)
instructions: 1. Whisk the rice flour, cornstarch, all-purpose flour, sugar, salt, and baking soda in a mixing bowl. 2. Add the egg, milk, and vanilla extract, whisk until smooth, and strain the batter to remove any lumps. 3. Rest the batter for at least 30 minutes at room temperature or chill overnight. 4. Stir the batter, heat a non-stick pan over low heat, and lightly grease with cooking oil. 5. Pour 35 to 40 ml of batter into the center and swirl to coat the pan thinly, then increase heat to medium-low. 6. Drizzle with melted butter and sprinkle crushed peanuts, chocolate sprinkles, and sugar while the top is still wet. 7. Cook until the bottom is golden brown, loosen the edges with a spatula, fold into quarters, and cool until crisp before serving.

name: Steamed Kaya Butter Bread
instructions: 1. Chop the pandan leaves, blend with 180 ml lukewarm milk, strain to collect the pandan milk, and stir in pandan essence if using. 2. Mix the yeast, 1/2 tsp sugar, and 15 ml lukewarm milk, then let stand for 10 minutes until foamy. 3. Whisk both flours, 60 g sugar, and salt in a mixing bowl, add the yeast mixture and oil, and gradually add the pandan milk while kneading for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. 4. Cover and rest the dough for 15 minutes, then roll it out to the length of a greased, parchment-lined loaf pan, roll up tightly like a Swiss roll, and place in the pan. 5. Cover and proof in a warm place for about 1 hour until doubled in size. 6. Place the pan on a rack inside a large pot of cold water, cover with a cloth-wrapped lid, bring to a gentle boil over medium heat, and cook for 40 minutes. 7. Turn off the heat and wait 5 minutes before uncovering, then unmold and cool the loaf slightly. 8. Slice thick, warm gently if needed, spread with kaya jam, add a slice of cold butter, sandwich together, and serve.

name: Hainanese Pork Chop
ingredients: 1 tsp freshly ground white or black pepper
1 tbsp cornstarch + 2 tbsp water (plus extra cornstarch for coating)
instructions: 1. Cover the pork chops with plastic wrap and gently pound with a pestle to about 1/2-inch thickness, then season with salt and pepper. 2. Marinate the pork chops with oyster sauce and cooking wine for at least 1 hour or overnight. 3. Coat each pork chop in dry cornstarch, dip into beaten eggs, press into cream cracker crumbs, and fry in hot oil over medium heat for about 2 minutes per side until golden brown; keep warm in the oven. 4. Pat the quartered potatoes dry, toss lightly with cooking oil, and cook in an air fryer at 200°C (400°F) for 10 to 15 minutes until golden and tender. 5. Mix ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, brown sugar, water, and salt in a mixing bowl. 6. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a saucepan, sauté the onion for 3 minutes, add green peas for 1 minute, then pour in the sauce mixture and tomatoes. 7. Bring to a boil, stir in the cornstarch slurry, and cook until thickened. 8. Slice the pork chops into strips on a serving plate, spoon the hot gravy over them, and serve with the air-fried potatoes.

name: Kaya Jam Thumbprint Cookies
ingredients: Kaya jam (chilled, about 1 tsp per cookie)
instructions: 1. Place the softened butter, sugar, vanilla extract, egg yolks, baking powder, and salt in a mixing bowl and beat vigorously with a sturdy spatula until creamy and pale. 2. Fold in the all-purpose flour until a soft dough forms. 3. Scoop about 25 g of dough per cookie, roll into balls, place 2 inches apart on a parchment-lined baking tray, and press a well into each center with the back of a spoon. 4. Chill the shaped dough in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours. 5. Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), then fill each well with about 1 teaspoon of chilled kaya jam. 6. Bake one tray at a time on the middle rack for 15 to 16 minutes until the edges turn lightly golden. 7. Cool on the tray for 5 minutes before transferring to cool completely.

name: Kuih Talam Gula Melaka (Steamed Palm Sugar Cake)
ingredients: 35 g mung bean starch (hunkwe flour, for bottom layer)
400 ml coconut milk (for cooked top layer option)
100 ml water (for cooked top layer option)
40 g mung bean starch (for cooked top layer option)
10 g tapioca starch (for cooked top layer option)
1 tsp salt (for cooked top layer option)
50 g rice flour (for no-cook top layer option)
25 g tapioca starch (for no-cook top layer option)
250 ml thick coconut milk (for no-cook top layer option)
1 tsp salt (for no-cook top layer option)
250 g boiling water (for no-cook top layer option)
instructions: 1. Grease a cake pan, line the bottom with parchment paper, and bring water to a boil in a large pot fitted with a steaming rack and a cloth-wrapped lid. 2. Simmer the gula Melaka and 750 ml water in a saucepan until dissolved, strain, and cool until lukewarm. 3. Whisk the bottom-layer mung bean starch, rice flour, and tapioca starch in a mixing bowl, stir in the warm gula Melaka syrup and alkaline water until smooth, and strain if needed. 4. Cook the mixture over low heat until it thickens slightly and coats the back of a spatula while remaining pourable. 5. Pour into the prepared pan and cook over medium-high heat in the covered pot for 20 minutes until the surface sets. 6. For the top coconut layer, either whisk the cooked-option ingredients and simmer over low heat until slightly thickened, or whisk the no-cook-option flours, salt, coconut milk, and boiling water until smooth and lump-free. 7. Strain and gently pour the coconut layer over the set gula Melaka layer, then cook covered over medium heat for 15 to 17 minutes until set. 8. Cool completely for about 2 hours before slicing with an oiled knife.

name: Hainanese Bread Loaf (Roti Benggali)
instructions: 1. Combine the bread flour, milk powder, sugar, instant yeast, salt, and cold water in a mixing bowl and knead for 5 minutes until a rough dough forms. 2. Add the softened butter and knead for 10 to 15 minutes until smooth, elastic, and able to stretch thinly without tearing. 3. Shape into a round ball, place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover, and proof in a warm place for about 1 hour until doubled in size. 4. Grease or line a loaf pan with parchment paper, punch down the dough, divide into 3 or 4 equal balls, cover, and rest for 10 minutes. 5. Roll each ball into a rectangle, fold in the sides, roll up like a Swiss roll, and place side by side in the loaf pan. 6. Cover loosely and proof for 45 to 60 minutes until the dough reaches near the top rim of the pan; preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) during the last 10 minutes. 7. Bake on the middle rack for 50 minutes (tenting with foil if browning too quickly) until the internal temperature reaches 88°C. 8. Remove from the pan immediately and cool completely on a rack before slicing.

name: Spiral Curry Puffs (Karipap Pusing)
ingredients: 3 tbsp meat curry powder (mixed with water into a paste)
300 g orange sweet potatoes (cut into small cubes)
400 g all-purpose flour (sifted, for water dough)
200 g all-purpose flour (sifted, for oil dough)
instructions: 1. Heat 3 tbsp oil in a wok or frying pan over medium heat, sauté the onion and garlic until fragrant, then stir-fry the curry paste until aromatic. 2. Add the chicken cubes and coat well, pour in 2 cups warm water, bring to a boil, and add both potatoes, 1 tbsp salt, and 2 tbsp sugar. 3. Cover and cook until the potatoes are tender and the filling is dry, stir in the minced curry leaves, and set aside to cool. 4. For the water dough, mix 400 g flour, 1/4 tsp salt, 2 lightly beaten eggs, and 100 ml warm water, knead until smooth, and rest covered for 30 minutes. 5. For the oil dough, combine 200 g flour and melted margarine until soft, then divide into 22 portions of 15 g each and divide the water dough into 22 portions of 25 g each. 6. Flatten each water dough ball, wrap around an oil dough ball, roll into a rectangle, roll up like a Swiss roll, turn upright, flatten again, roll up a second time, and cut in half crosswise. 7. Press each half cut-side down into a round disc, place 1 tbsp filling and an egg wedge in the center of the uncut side, fold into a half-moon, and pleat the edges to seal. 8. Deep-fry in hot oil (infused briefly with curry leaves) over medium heat until golden brown, drain with a strainer, and serve warm.

name: Kuih Pie Tee Shells (Nyonya Top Hats)
instructions: 1. Whisk the sifted all-purpose flour, rice flour, salt, eggs, and water gradually in a mixing bowl until smooth, then pass through a strainer. 2. Heat enough cooking oil in a wok or deep frying pan over medium heat to submerge a pie tee mold. 3. Dip the pie tee mold into the hot oil until heated, shake off excess oil, and dip it into the batter to coat about 95% up the sides. 4. Lift the mold, let excess batter drip off, then submerge into the hot oil and jiggle gently until the shell releases. 5. Deep-fry the released shell until light golden brown, transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate to drain, and repeat with the remaining batter. 6. Cool completely and store in an airtight container, or fill with savory turnip filling before serving.

name: Malaysian Popiah (Fresh Spring Rolls)
ingredients: Fresh lettuce leaves (washed and drained dry)
2 pieces firm tofu (fried and sliced into strips)
200 g bean sprouts (blanched and drained dry)
2 eggs (beaten with a pinch of salt, fried into thin omelettes and sliced into strips)
50 g shallots (thinly sliced and fried crispy)
1 cup water (or dried prawn soaking water)
instructions: 1. Shallow-fry the firm tofu in oil until light golden, drain, and slice into thin strips. 2. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a hot wok, fry the chopped dried prawns until lightly golden, then add the minced garlic and fry until golden brown. 3. Add the julienned jicama, French beans, and carrot, stir-fry until heated through, and season with salt and sugar. 4. Pour in the water, reduce heat, and simmer for about 30 minutes until the jicama is tender yet crisp, then stir in white pepper and drain off excess sauce in a bowl. 5. Lay a popiah wrapper flat on a chopping board, spread lightly with sweet sauce and chili sauce, and place a lettuce leaf on top. 6. Spoon 2 tbsp of drained filling onto the lettuce, top with tofu strips, omelette strips, bean sprouts, fried shallots, and crushed peanuts, then fold in the sides and roll up tightly to serve.

name: Vegetarian Chicken Pongteh
ingredients: 250 g vegetarian chicken meat (cut into pieces)
1 1/2 cups mushroom soaking water (or plain water)
instructions: 1. Soak the dried shiitake mushrooms until soft, reserve the soaking liquid, and slice the mushrooms. 2. Heat oil in a wok and sauté the minced ginger until fragrant, then add the fermented bean paste and stir-fry for 2 minutes until aromatic. 3. Add the sliced mushrooms and potato chunks and stir-fry briefly. 4. Stir in the palm sugar, reserved mushroom water, light soy sauce, and dark soy sauce until the sugar dissolves, then cook over low heat until the potatoes are tender. 5. Add the vegetarian chicken pieces, bring to a boil, and simmer covered over low heat for 5 minutes until the gravy thickens before serving hot with steamed rice.

name: Kuih Seri Muka (Purple Sweet Potato)
ingredients: 150 ml thick coconut milk (for rice layer)
150 g purple sweet potato (cooked and mashed)
200 ml thick coconut milk (for custard layer)
instructions: 1. Boil the blue pea flowers in water, steep for 10 minutes, and strain to obtain indigo blue coloring. 2. Wash the glutinous rice, soak 100 g in the blue coloring and 200 g in plain water for at least 4 hours or overnight, then drain both. 3. Combine 150 ml coconut milk, 50 ml water, 1 tsp salt, and 1 tbsp sugar, pour over the drained rice in a tray topped with knotted pandan leaves, and cook over a rack in a covered pot for 30 minutes (fluffing after 20 minutes). 4. Mix the white and blue rice gently for a marbled effect, press firmly into an oiled 7-inch square pan lined with banana leaf, and keep warm. 5. Combine the mashed purple sweet potato, 70 ml water, and 200 ml thick coconut milk, whisk in the all-purpose flour, rice flour, and cornstarch, and strain into a saucepan. 6. Whisk the eggs with 110 g sugar, stir into the batter, and cook over low heat while stirring continuously until the custard thickens slightly. 7. Pour the custard over the warm rice layer, tap gently to remove air bubbles, and cook covered over medium-low heat for 30 minutes until set. 8. Cool completely before slicing and serving at room temperature.

name: Pulut Tai Tai (Blue Pea Glutinous Rice Cake)
ingredients: 250 g thick coconut milk (divided into 180 ml and 70 ml)
instructions: 1. Wash and soak the glutinous rice for at least 2 hours, then drain; steep the blue pea flowers in 150 ml hot water until dark blue and strain. 2. Place an oiled banana leaf on a tray, add the drained glutinous rice, stir in 180 ml coconut milk with salt, and top with knotted pandan leaves. 3. Cook over a rack in a covered pot of boiling water over medium heat for 20 minutes. 4. Remove the pandan leaves, stir in the remaining 70 ml coconut milk and the 150 ml blue coloring to create a marbled effect, and cook covered for another 20 minutes. 5. Remove from the pot, press the rice firmly and evenly to compact it, and cool completely to room temperature. 6. Cut into diamond or square pieces and serve topped with a scoop of kaya jam.

name: Pan-Fried Nian Gao (Kuih Bakul)
instructions: 1. Remove any banana leaves from the nian gao and slice thinly using an oiled knife. 2. Stir the rice flour, cornstarch, baking powder, and salt in a mixing bowl, then whisk in the egg and ice-cold water to form a thick batter. 3. Heat 2 tbsp cooking oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat. 4. Dip the nian gao slices into the batter to coat evenly and pan-fry over medium heat until golden brown on both sides. 5. Drain on a paper-towel-lined plate and serve immediately while crisp.

name: Nyonya Chap Chye
ingredients: 500 g Napa cabbage (cut into large chunks)
100 g boneless skinless chicken thighs (diced or thinly sliced)
instructions: 1. Mix the fermented bean paste, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and sesame oil in a small bowl. 2. Soak the shiitake mushrooms in 500 ml hot water for 30 minutes until plump (reserve the soaking liquid), soak the wood ear mushrooms and dried beancurd sheets until soft and slice into bite-size pieces, soak the dried shrimp in warm water and chop finely, and soak the mung bean thread noodles in cold water until soft. 3. Heat cooking oil in a large wok over high heat, sauté the garlic briefly, add the dried shrimp for 1 minute, and stir-fry the chicken until no longer pink. 4. Add the mushrooms, beancurd sheets, Napa cabbage, and seasoning mixture, stir well, pour in the reserved mushroom soaking liquid, and bring to a boil. 5. Cover, reduce heat to low, and braise for 30 to 40 minutes until tender. 6. Adjust seasoning to taste, stir in the drained noodles and black moss until softened, and transfer to a serving plate.

name: Mee Siam Kuah
ingredients: 300 g dried rice vermicelli (or 500 g fresh rice noodles)
150 g fried tofu puffs (tau pok, cubed)
80 g dried shrimp (soaked in warm water until soft)
instructions: 1. Soak the dried chilies and dried shrimp in warm water for 20 minutes, drain, and blend with onion and garlic (adding a little water if needed) into a smooth spice paste. 2. Boil the shell-on shrimp in a small pot of water for 1 to 3 minutes until pink and firm, cool on a plate, and peel. 3. Soak the rice vermicelli in water for 1 hour until soft, then drain. 4. Bring 6 cups chicken broth to a boil in a large pot, stir in the fermented bean paste, sugar, tomato paste, tamarind paste, and salt, and simmer for 10 minutes until balanced in savory, sour, and sweet flavors. 5. Heat cooking oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the spice paste for 5 minutes until fragrant. 6. Add the drained rice vermicelli to the wok and stir-fry until soft, then toss briefly with Chinese chives, cubed tofu puffs, and bean sprouts. 7. Divide the noodles into bowls, ladle hot gravy generously on top, and garnish with sliced hard-boiled eggs, shrimp, chives, and lime wedges.

name: Kuih Kosui (Pandan & Gula Melaka)
ingredients: 100 ml boiling water (cooled 15 minutes, for pandan version)
45 g rice flour (for gula Melaka version)
45 g tapioca flour (for gula Melaka version)
100 g gula Melaka (chopped, for gula Melaka version)
1/2 tsp alkaline water (for gula Melaka version)
instructions: 1. Mix the grated coconut with 1/4 tsp salt, heat over a rack in a covered pot over high heat for 10 minutes, and set aside. 2. Lightly grease small cups and preheat them inside a covered pot with boiling water for 5 minutes. 3. For the pandan batter, dissolve 80 g sugar in 100 ml boiling water, cool for 15 minutes until lukewarm, then whisk into 60 g rice flour, 30 g tapioca flour, 1/8 tsp salt, pandan juice, and 1/2 tsp alkaline water until smooth. 4. For the gula Melaka batter, simmer 100 g gula Melaka and 200 ml water in a saucepan until melted, strain, cool until lukewarm, and whisk into 45 g rice flour, 45 g tapioca flour, 1/8 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp alkaline water until smooth. 5. Stir the batter well, pour into the preheated cups about 3/4 full, and cook covered over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes (or 18 to 20 minutes for larger cups). 6. Cool for 5 minutes, unmold with a small spatula, and serve topped with salted grated coconut.

name: Cendol Agar-Agar Cake
ingredients: 125 ml water (to mix with agar-agar for cendol layer)
4 g agar-agar powder (2 tsp, for cendol layer)
5 pieces sweet jackfruit (cut into small cubes)
250 ml water (to mix with agar-agar for gula Melaka layer)
6 g agar-agar powder (1 tbsp, for gula Melaka layer)
instructions: 1. Stir 100 ml coconut milk with cornstarch and salt in a mixing bowl. 2. Mix 125 ml water with 4 g agar-agar powder; bring 250 ml water and 100 g sugar to a boil in a saucepan, stir in the agar-agar mixture, simmer for 3 to 5 minutes until dissolved, then stir in the coconut milk mixture and keep warm on lowest heat. 3. Mix 250 ml water with 6 g agar-agar powder; boil 500 ml water, gula Melaka, and pandan leaves in a second pot until melted, stir in the agar-agar mixture, and simmer for 3 to 5 minutes until dissolved. 4. Strain half of the gula Melaka mixture into a cake pan and let cool until a soft film forms on top, keeping the other half warm on low heat. 5. Stir the cendol and jackfruit into the warm coconut layer, gently pour it over the partially set gula Melaka layer, and let cool until a soft film forms. 6. Gently pour the remaining warm gula Melaka mixture on top, cool until slightly set, then chill in the refrigerator for 2 to 4 hours before unmolding onto a plate and slicing.

name: Steamed Ondeh-Ondeh Mini Sponge Cake
instructions: 1. Grease mini muffin or cupcake cups and bring water to a boil in a pot fitted with a steaming rack, then reduce to medium heat. 2. Whisk the eggs and sugar in a mixing bowl until dissolved, then whisk in the pandan essence, whole milk, and cooking oil. 3. Sift in the cake flour, baking powder, and 1/8 tsp salt and whisk until smooth. 4. Spoon the batter into the cups about 3/4 full and cook covered over medium heat for about 10 minutes until a toothpick inserted comes out clean, then cool and unmold. 5. Whisk the cold heavy cream, coconut sugar, and a pinch of salt vigorously in a chilled bowl until stiff peaks form. 6. Core a small well into the center of each sponge cake without piercing the bottom, pipe or spoon in the cream filling, and sprinkle with desiccated coconut before serving.

name: Nyonya Acar Awak (Pickled Vegetables)
ingredients: 200 g cucumber (seeded and cut into 2-inch strips)
1 inch fresh turmeric (or 1 tsp turmeric powder)
instructions: 1. Soak the dried chilies in warm water for 15 minutes and coarsely crush the roasted peanuts with a mortar and pestle. 2. Toss the cucumber strips with 1 tsp salt, let sit for 30 minutes, then rinse, squeeze dry, and pat thoroughly dry. 3. Bring a pot of water to a boil, blanch the long beans, cabbage, and carrots for 3 minutes, refresh in cold water, drain, and pat completely dry. 4. Blend the soaked chilies, lemongrass, shallots, garlic, galangal, turmeric, and cooking oil into a smooth paste. 5. Sauté the spice paste in a large wok for 10 minutes until fragrant, add the vinegar and sugar, and stir until dissolved. 6. Turn off the heat, toss in all the prepared vegetables, pineapple, toasted sesame seeds, and crushed peanuts until evenly coated, cool completely, and chill in an airtight jar for 24 hours before serving.

name: Pandan Cendol Layer Cake
ingredients: 1 7-inch square or 8-inch round pandan sponge cake
instructions: 1. Slice the prepared pandan sponge cake horizontally into 2 or 3 even layers. 2. Whisk the mung bean starch with the coconut milk and 80 g water in a mixing bowl. 3. Combine 660 g water, sugar, salt, and agar-agar powder in a heavy saucepan and let soak for 20 minutes. 4. Place over low heat, add butter, and cook until the agar-agar dissolves completely. 5. Remove from heat, whisk in the coconut milk mixture, return to low heat, and cook while stirring until slightly thickened yet pourable, then fold in the cendol and sweetened red beans. 6. Rinse the cake pan with water, pour in a layer of custard, place a sponge layer on top, and repeat alternating custard and cake layers, finishing with custard. 7. Cool to room temperature, refrigerate for 5 to 6 hours or overnight, and invert onto a serving plate to slice.

name: Kuih Talam Pandan (Steamed Pandan Coconut Cake)
instructions: 1. Grease a cake pan, line with parchment paper, and bring water to a boil in a large pot fitted with a steaming rack and a cloth-wrapped lid. 2. Blend the pandan leaves with 300 ml water until smooth and strain to yield 300 ml pandan juice. 3. Whisk the mung bean starch, 40 g tapioca starch, 120 g rice flour, sugar, pandan juice, 320 ml water, and alkaline water in a saucepan until smooth, straining if necessary. 4. Cook over low heat while stirring until slightly thickened and pourable, pour into the prepared pan, and cook covered over medium-high heat for 20 minutes until set. 5. Whisk 50 g rice flour, 25 g tapioca starch, salt, coconut milk, and boiling water in a mixing bowl until smooth, then strain over the pandan layer. 6. Cook covered over medium heat for 15 to 17 minutes until the white layer sets, then cool completely for about 2 hours before slicing with an oiled knife.

name: Cheese Kuih Bangkit
ingredients: 3 cups tapioca flour (dry-toasted until light and sifted)
instructions: 1. Dry-toast the tapioca flour in a dry wok or pan over low heat until light, cool, and sift with the cornstarch and baking powder. 2. Whisk the softened butter and caster sugar in a mixing bowl until pale and fluffy. 3. Add the cream cheese, vanilla essence, and egg yolks and whisk until smooth and well combined. 4. Gradually fold in the sifted flours and knead gently until a soft, non-sticky dough forms (adding a little extra tapioca flour if needed). 5. Fold in the grated cheddar cheese evenly, rest the dough for a few minutes, and press into cookie molds or cut into shapes. 6. Bake in a preheated oven at 170°C for about 30 minutes until lightly golden and cool before storing.

name: Otak-Otak Johor (Spiced Fish Parcels)
instructions: 1. Roughly chop the fish fillet and pound the shallots, belacan, turmeric, red chilies, and lemongrass into a fine paste. 2. In a large mixing bowl, combine the fish, coconut milk, eggs, kaffir lime leaves, anchovy seasoning, MSG, fish sauce, and spice paste until thoroughly blended. 3. Spread 1 tablespoon of fish paste onto a piece of coconut leaf, cover with a second leaf strip, and secure both ends; repeat until all paste is used. 4. Bake in the oven or pan-sear in a frying pan until cooked through and fragrant before serving.

name: Kuih Bangkit (Sago & Tapioca Cookies)
ingredients: 6 pandan leaves (rinsed, dried, and cut into 3-inch lengths)
180 ml thick coconut cream (3/4 cup, scooped from 400 ml can)
Red food coloring (a few drops, optional)
instructions: 1. Combine the sago and tapioca flours on a baking tray, bury the pandan leaves in the flour, and bake at 93°C (200°F) for 1 hour, then cool and sift, reserving 1/4 cup for dusting molds. 2. Beat the caster sugar and egg yolks in a mixing bowl until light and fluffy. 3. Mix in the cooked flours and coconut cream alternately in three additions with a spatula, then knead gently into a soft, non-sticky dough (adding 1 to 2 tbsp extra coconut cream if dry). 4. Dust cookie molds with the reserved flour, press dough into the cavities, trim excess with a knife, and tap onto a parchment-lined baking tray (or roll to 1/4-inch thickness and cut with cookie cutters). 5. Bake at 163°C (325°F) for 20 to 25 minutes until the bottoms are lightly browned, cool completely, and dot with red food coloring if desired.

name: Nasi Ulam (Nyonya Herb Rice)
ingredients: 300 g long-grain rice (2 rice cooker cups)
50 g grated coconut (1/2 cup, for kerisik)
1 stalk lemongrass (white part only, thinly sliced)
10 g Vietnamese mint / daun kesum (1 cup, thinly sliced)
10 g mint leaves (1 cup, thinly sliced)
instructions: 1. Wash and drain the rice 3 to 4 times in the rice cooker pot, add 480 ml water, and cook in the rice cooker. 2. Dry-toast the grated coconut in a wok until golden brown and pound into toasted coconut paste (kerisik). 3. Pan-fry the snapper fillet in a non-stick pan with 1/4 tsp pepper and 1/2 tsp salt for about 10 minutes until flaky, then break into flakes with a spatula. 4. Transfer the cooked rice to a large mixing bowl and toss thoroughly with the fish flakes, kerisik, shallots, lemongrass, turmeric leaves, kaffir lime leaves, daun kesum, mint leaves, remaining pepper, remaining salt, and sugar before serving warm.

name: Rice Cooker Hainanese Chicken Rice
ingredients: 150 g long-grain rice (3/4 cup, rinsed and drained)
instructions: 1. Bring 540 ml water to a boil in the rice cooker. 2. Debone the chicken thighs (reserving the bones) and season the meat with salt and pepper. 3. Arrange half the green onions and ginger on the rice cooker rack, top with the chicken skin-side up and the remaining green onions and ginger, and cook over the boiling water for 7 minutes. 4. Meanwhile, heat vegetable oil in a small saucepan, sauté the garlic for 30 seconds, and transfer half of the garlic oil to a small bowl. 5. Stir the drained rice into the saucepan with the remaining garlic oil to coat, then remove 360 ml chicken broth from the rice cooker (leaving 180 ml), stir the rice and salt into the rice cooker pot, and place the chicken back on top until the rice finishes cooking. 6. Mix soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sesame oil into the bowl of garlic oil. 7. Simmer the reserved 360 ml broth with the chicken bones in the saucepan for 10 minutes, discard bones, season, and boil the Napa cabbage for 2 minutes for soup. 8. Slice the chicken over cucumber slices on a plate, drizzle with garlic oyster sauce, and serve with the rice, soup, and garlic chili sauce.

name: Sugee Cake
ingredients: 100 g granulated white sugar (plus 30 g for meringue)
Slivered almonds and honey (optional, for topping)
instructions: 1. Cream the softened butter and 100 g sugar together in a mixing bowl for 2 to 3 minutes until light and fluffy. 2. Beat in the egg yolks one at a time until fully incorporated, then stir in the vanilla extract and orange juice. 3. Whisk in the plain flour, semolina, and ground almonds until just combined, then cover and rest for 2 hours to soften the semolina. 4. Near the end of resting, whisk the egg whites in a clean bowl until stiff peaks form, gradually adding the remaining 30 g sugar during the foamy stage. 5. Whisk one-third of the meringue into the batter to lighten it, then gently fold in the remaining meringue in two batches with a spatula. 6. Transfer to a 7-inch round cake pan and bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for 53 to 56 minutes until golden brown (tent with foil if browning too quickly). 7. Cool completely before glazing with honey and topping with slivered almonds if desired.

name: Penang Acar (Spicy Pickled Vegetables)
ingredients: 500 g cucumber (seeded and cut into 1 1/2-inch strips)
200 g carrots (peeled and cut into 1 1/2-inch strips)
5 dried chilies (soaked in hot water until soft)
instructions: 1. Toss the cucumber and carrot strips with 1 tbsp salt in a mixing bowl, rest for 30 minutes, then rinse thoroughly and squeeze out excess liquid. 2. Bring a large pot half-filled with water, 250 ml white vinegar, and a pinch of salt to a boil, blanch the vegetables in batches for 2 to 3 minutes, drain, and air-dry for 1 hour. 3. Blend the fresh chilies, soaked dried chilies, shallots, garlic, turmeric, galangal, candlenuts, coriander seeds, and belacan into a smooth spice paste. 4. Heat 6 tbsp oil in a large wok and fry the spice paste for about 10 minutes until aromatic and the oil separates. 5. Stir in the remaining 200 ml vinegar, sugar, and 1 tsp salt until dissolved, then mix in the ground peanuts. 6. Toss in the dried vegetables until evenly coated, garnish with toasted sesame seeds, and chill overnight before serving.

name: Nyonya Chicken Rice Dumplings (Bak Chang)
ingredients: 1 kg glutinous rice (divided into 2 equal portions)
30 g blue pea flowers (boiled in 200 ml water)
2 tbsp salt (1 tbsp each for white and blue rice)
2 tbsp ground white pepper (1 tbsp each for white and blue rice)
2 tbsp fried garlic oil (1 tbsp each for white and blue rice)
100 g dried chestnuts (boiled, peeled, and cubed)
50 g dried shiitake mushrooms (soaked and cubed)
instructions: 1. Boil the bamboo leaves for 15 minutes until soft, wipe clean, and soak in cold water with grass strands until needed. 2. Fry the minced garlic in 2 tbsp oil until golden brown and reserve both garlic and oil. 3. Boil the blue pea flowers in 200 ml water, steep for 20 minutes, strain, and cool; soak half the washed glutinous rice in the blue water with vinegar (plus extra water to cover) and the other half in plain water for 1 hour, then drain and season each with 1 tbsp salt, 1 tbsp white pepper, and 1 tbsp fried garlic oil. 4. Boil the dried chestnuts for 20 minutes until soft, peel, and chop coarsely. 5. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok, sauté the ground shallots and garlic until fragrant, add the chicken cubes, and stir-fry until cooked. 6. Add the chestnuts, mushrooms, coriander powder, fermented bean paste, oyster sauce, sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp white pepper, stir-fry until combined, and cool. 7. Overlap two bamboo leaves into a cone, layer with white rice, blue rice, chicken filling, salted egg yolk, candied winter melon, more rice, and a pandan piece, then fold and tie firmly with a grass strand. 8. Submerge the dumplings in a large pot of boiling water with knotted pandan leaves and boil over medium heat for 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours until tender, then hang to drip dry before serving.

name: Nyonya Rice Dumplings (Zong Zi)
ingredients: 128 bamboo leaves (boiled, washed, and soaked overnight)
8 pandan leaves (5 cut into 2-inch pieces, 3 knotted)
100 g dried shiitake mushrooms (soaked and cubed)
instructions: 1. Render the diced pork fat in a wok over low-medium heat until golden brown, strain to separate the crispy lardons from the lard oil, and chop the lardons finely. 2. Sauté the garlic and shallots in lard oil in the wok until fragrant, add the mushrooms and cubed pork belly, season with 2 tbsp salt, sugar, and 2 tbsp white pepper, and stir-fry until opaque. 3. Stir in the chopped lardons, dark soy sauce, 200 ml water, and candied winter melon, simmer covered over medium-low heat for 10 minutes, mix in coriander powder, and chill until next day. 4. Boil the blue pea flowers in 300 ml water, cool, strain, and soak the 500 g rice in the blue water overnight while soaking the 1.5 kg rice in plain water overnight; boil and clean the bamboo leaves and soak with bamboo strings overnight. 5. Drain both portions of rice and season each separately with salt, white pepper, MSG if using, and lard oil. 6. Overlap two bamboo leaves into a cone, layer with blue rice, pork filling (and salted egg yolk if using), white rice, and a piece of pandan leaf, then fold tightly and tie with bamboo strings. 7. Boil the dumplings submerged in salted water with knotted pandan leaves over medium heat for about 2 hours until cooked through, then hang to drain and cool slightly before serving.

name: Steamed Radish Cake (Loh Bak Gou)
ingredients: 15 g dried shiitake mushrooms (soaked and finely diced, liquid retained)
30 g dried shrimp (soaked and minced, liquid retained)
25 g dried scallops (soaked and shredded, liquid retained)
1 cup radish and soaking liquid (or water)
1/4 cup toasted white sesame seeds (for garnish)
instructions: 1. Soak the dried shrimp, shiitake mushrooms, and dried scallops in water for about 2 hours, reserving the soaking liquid, then mince the shrimp, dice the mushrooms, shred the scallops, and dice the Chinese sausage. 2. Toss the shredded daikon in a hot wok until slightly wilted, pour in the soaking liquid, and simmer covered for 10 minutes until soft. 3. Drain the cooked radish through a strainer, pressing out the juice into a bowl, and measure 1 cup of cooled radish juice. 4. Whisk the rice flour, tapioca flour, and 1 cup radish juice in a mixing bowl until smooth. 5. Heat a little oil in a wok, sauté the garlic until fragrant, fry the Chinese sausage over low heat to release its fat, then sauté the mushrooms, dried shrimp, and scallops until aromatic. 6. Stir in the drained radish and seasonings, reduce heat to low, pour in the flour batter, and stir quickly until it thickens into a paste. 7. Transfer to a lightly oiled tray, smooth the top with a spatula, and cook over a rack in a covered pot or wok of boiling water for 40 to 50 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. 8. Cool completely, garnish with toasted sesame seeds, fried shallots, spring onions, and red chili, and slice to serve.

name: Kuih Ketayap (Pandan Coconut Crepes)
instructions: 1. For the coconut filling, boil the palm sugar, granulated sugar, water, and pandan leaves in a saucepan until dissolved, then strain. 2. Stir the grated coconut and salt into the syrup and cook over medium heat until the liquid dries up, then stir in 1 tbsp flour until well combined and set aside to cool. 3. For the crepes, blend the 2 cups flour, cooking oil, salt, pandan juice, and green food coloring if using until smooth, then strain into a mixing bowl. 4. Heat a non-stick frying pan (wiping lightly with oil before the first crepe only), ladle in a small amount of batter, and swirl thinly until set. 5. Remove the cooked crepe, spoon coconut filling onto one edge, fold in the sides, and roll neatly into a cylinder before serving.

name: Acar Ikan Cencaru (Pickled Fried Hardtail Scad)
ingredients: Whole spices (cinnamon stick, star anise, cloves, cardamom)
Salt and sugar (to taste, with more sugar than salt)
Toasted coconut paste (kerisik, a small amount)
Hardtail scad fish (ikan cencaru, rubbed with turmeric and salt, fried and halved)
instructions: 1. Heat oil in a wok and sauté the whole spices, shallots, garlic, and ginger until fragrant, then add fenugreek seeds and stir briefly. 2. Add the chili paste, turmeric powder, curry powder, and belacan, stir-frying until thickened, then add a splash of water. 3. Once simmering, add vinegar, salt, sugar, and kerisik and stir well. 4. Add the carrot, cucumber, and quartered onion, adding a little water if needed, and cook until the vegetables soften slightly. 5. Fold in the fried fish and sliced red and green chilies, cook briefly to coat in the sauce, and transfer to a serving plate.

name: Northern Style Nasi Ulam (Nasi Ulam Utara)
ingredients: Assorted fresh ulam herbs (finely sliced, such as water dropwort and pennywort leaves)
Salted talang fish fillets (fried and finely pounded)
instructions: 1. Fry the salted talang fish fillets in a frying pan until crisp, cool slightly, and pound finely in a mortar and pestle. 2. Pound the lemongrass, galangal with belacan, and black peppercorns separately in the mortar and pestle. 3. In a large mixing bowl, mix the cooked white rice thoroughly with the kerisik and pounded salted fish, tasting before adding salt. 4. Stir in the pounded lemongrass, galangal-belacan paste, black pepper, sliced shallots, and diced ginger. 5. Toss in the finely sliced ulam herbs until evenly distributed and serve.

name: Hainanese Mixed Vegetables
ingredients: 40 g dried lily buds (soaked and knotted)
20 g fried tofu skin (fu zuk, cut into medium squares)
instructions: 1. Heat the cooking oil in a wok and fry the sliced ginger until fragrant. 2. Add the soaked black fungus, dried lily buds, and carrots and stir-fry briefly. 3. Add the Napa cabbage, fried tofu skin, leek, and red dates, stir-frying until half-cooked. 4. Season with MSG, salt, light soy sauce, and oyster sauce, then pour in 500 ml water and simmer until the vegetables soften. 5. Stir in the black and white shimeji mushrooms and soaked glass noodles, cook until heated through, and serve.

name: Pulut Inti (Glutinous Rice with Sweet Coconut)
ingredients: 50 g gula Melaka (1/4 cup palm sugar)
100 g grated coconut (1 cup, white part only)
instructions: 1. Wash and drain the glutinous rice 4 to 5 times until clear, then soak in water for at least 4 hours or overnight. 2. Line a steaming rack inside a pot with the large banana leaf and top with 1 pandan leaf. 3. Drain the rice, stir in salt, transfer to the rack, pour over 3/4 cup coconut milk, and cook covered over medium heat for 20 minutes. 4. Fluff the rice with a fork, sprinkle the remaining 2 tbsp coconut milk on top, and cook covered for 5 more minutes. 5. Meanwhile, simmer the water, gula Melaka, and remaining pandan leaf in a saucepan until melted, stir in the grated coconut and butter for 4 to 5 minutes, thicken with the cornstarch slurry for 1 minute, discard the pandan leaf, and cool. 6. Portion 1/4 cup cooked rice onto each banana leaf square, top with 1 tbsp sweet coconut, and fold neatly into a pyramid parcel to serve.

name: Asam Laksa Instant Noodles
ingredients: 1 packet asam laksa instant noodles (78 g)
1/2 red chili (seeded and cut into strips)
instructions: 1. Bring 360 ml water to a boil in a small saucepan and stir in the instant noodle seasoning packet. 2. Add the instant noodles and sardines, boiling for 2 minutes until the noodles are just tender. 3. Transfer to a serving bowl, top with cucumber, red onion, red chili, pineapple, and mint leaves, and squeeze fresh lime juice over before serving.

name: Lobak (Five-Spice Pork Rolls)
ingredients: 450 g pork tenderloin (1 lb, cut into 1-inch strips)
2 large fresh beancurd sheets (cut into eight 7x7-inch squares)
instructions: 1. Mix the pork strips, five-spice powder, salt, pepper, sweet dark soy sauce, sesame oil, green onions, and egg in a mixing bowl and marinate for 30 minutes. 2. Wipe each beancurd sheet square with a damp cloth to soften, spoon a strip of marinated pork along one edge, and roll tightly into a cylinder, placing seam-side down on a plate. 3. Heat vegetable oil in a wok or frying pan to 165°C (325°F) and deep-fry the rolls for 4 to 5 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown. 4. Drain on paper towels, slice diagonally, and serve hot with sweet chili sauce.

name: Nyonya Acar Fish (Acar Hu)
ingredients: 1 red chili (seeded and cut into thin strips)
1 green chili or jalapeño (seeded and cut into thin strips)
2 tbsp vegetable oil (plus extra for frying fish)
instructions: 1. Season the fish evenly with 1/4 tsp salt and ground pepper. 2. Heat frying oil in a wok or frying pan and pan-fry the fish in two batches for 6 to 7 minutes until golden brown, then arrange on a serving plate. 3. Scatter the julienned ginger, sliced garlic, red chili, and green chili over the fried fish. 4. Blend the fresh turmeric until fine, adding 2 tbsp water if needed. 5. Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a small saucepan, stir-fry the blended turmeric for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant, add vinegar, sugar, and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt, and bring to a boil until dissolved. 6. Pour the hot pickling sauce over the fish and aromatics and let soak for at least 30 minutes before serving.

name: Youtiao (Chinese Crullers / Cakoi)
ingredients: 1/2 tbsp cooking oil (plus extra for deep-frying)
instructions: 1. Mix the all-purpose flour, baking powder, and salt in a mixing bowl. 2. Add 120 ml water and 1/2 tbsp oil, knead for 4 to 5 minutes until smooth and shiny, then cover and rest for 2 hours. 3. On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough to 3 to 4 mm thickness and cut into strips about 2.5 cm wide and 15 cm long. 4. Dab a wet skewer down the center of one strip, lay a second strip on top, and press the center gently with the skewer to fuse them together. 5. Deep-fry in hot oil at 180°C in a wok or deep frying pan, turning constantly so the crullers puff evenly, until golden brown, then drain with a strainer and serve.

name: Hainanese Spring Rolls with Homemade Chili Sauce
ingredients: 3 dried Chinese mushrooms (soaked and finely sliced)
6 tbsp cooking oil (plus extra for deep-frying)
2 tbsp all-purpose flour (mixed with 3 tbsp water for sealing)
1 tbsp chicken stock seasoning (for chili sauce)
instructions: 1. Heat 6 tbsp oil in a wok, sauté the garlic, and stir-fry the sliced mushrooms, chopped chicken, and prawns for a couple of minutes. 2. Add the surimi, shredded jicama, and carrot, stir-fry until fairly dry, season with 1 tbsp chicken stock seasoning, MSG, and soy sauce, then transfer to a bowl to cool. 3. Place 2 tbsp cooled filling onto each spring roll wrapper, fold and roll into a tight cylinder, and seal the edge with the flour-and-water paste. 4. Deep-fry in hot oil until crisp and golden brown, then drain with a strainer. 5. Whisk the hot water, 1 tbsp chicken stock seasoning, chili sauce, tomato ketchup, plum sauce, and toasted sesame seeds in a small bowl and serve alongside the hot spring rolls.

name: Homemade Fruit Rojak Sauce (Kuah Rojak Buah)
ingredients: Dark sweet soy sauce and chili sauce (as needed)
Toasted sesame seeds and crushed roasted peanuts (as needed)
instructions: 1. Blend the chilies and belacan with 1 cup water until smooth and transfer to a wok. 2. Dissolve the palm sugar in 1 cup water, strain into the wok, and add the granulated sugar, soy sauce, and chili sauce. 3. Bring to a boil while stirring continuously so it does not boil over, then season with salt to balance the flavor. 4. Reduce heat to low, stir in the cornstarch slurry while stirring constantly until thickened, then fold in the toasted sesame seeds and most of the crushed peanuts (reserving some for garnish). 5. Cook until glossy, dark, and thick, cool, and serve with fresh cut fruits topped with the remaining crushed peanuts.

name: Terengganu Fruit Rojak Sauce (Kuah Rojak Buah)
ingredients: 1 tbsp cornstarch (mixed with water, for thickening)
Assorted fresh fruits (jicama, cucumber, pineapple, young mango, starfruit)
instructions: 1. Blend the dried chilies, bird's eye chilies, and toasted belacan until smooth, then place in a wok with the palm sugar disc and bring to a boil until the sugar melts. 2. Stir in the sweet soy sauce, chili sauce, tomato ketchup, vinegar, and shrimp paste until combined. 3. Add the toasted sesame seeds and crushed peanuts, then season with sugar, salt, and seasoning powder. 4. Stir in the cornstarch slurry gradually until the sauce reaches a thick, sweet-spicy-tangy consistency, then cool. 5. Cut the jicama, cucumber, pineapple, young mango, and starfruit into bite-size pieces, drizzle with the rojak sauce, and sprinkle with extra crushed peanuts to serve.

name: Kapitan Style Spicy Coconut Fish (Ikan Masak Lemak Cili)
ingredients: Whole or filleted fish (tilapia, sea bass, pomfret, or mackerel, lightly fried)
25 red and green chilies (for spice paste)
10 red chilies (cut into pieces, for garnish)
Salt, sugar, and chicken seasoning powder (to taste)
instructions: 1. Lightly fry the fish in a frying pan until cooked without making it overly crisp, then place on a serving plate. 2. Coarsely blend the onions, garlic, ginger, turmeric, 25 red and green chilies, 3 red chilies, and belacan. 3. Heat cooking oil in a wok and sauté the blended paste until fragrant without browning. 4. Add the bruised lemongrass and asam keping, then season with salt, sugar, and chicken seasoning powder. 5. Pour in the coconut milk and a little water to adjust consistency, and simmer until boiling and thickened. 6. Reduce heat to low, stir in most of the shredded turmeric leaves, balance the savory, sweet, and sour flavors, then pour the hot gravy over the fried fish and garnish with the remaining turmeric leaves and cut red chilies.

name: Hainanese Chicken Chop
ingredients: Boneless chicken leg fillets (for chicken chop)
1 tbsp cornstarch (mixed with a little water, for thickening)
instructions: 1. Marinate the chicken leg fillets with ground white pepper, Worcestershire sauce, 2 tbsp sugar, and a pinch of salt. 2. Coat the marinated chicken evenly in cornstarch, pan-fry or shallow-fry in hot oil until crisp and cooked through, then drain onto a serving plate. 3. In the same pan, sauté the sliced yellow onion until fragrant, then add tomato ketchup, chili sauce, 1 tsp white pepper, liquid seasoning, 4 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 2 tbsp sugar, salt, and 2 1/2 cups water. 4. Bring to a boil, stir in the cornstarch slurry until the gravy thickens, and pour over the crispy chicken to serve.

name: Kuih Talam Cendol
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups thick coconut milk (for top layer)
instructions: 1. Simmer the palm sugar, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, pandan leaves, and 1 cup water in a saucepan until dissolved, then strain and cool. 2. For the bottom layer, whisk 3/4 cup sugar, rice flour, 2 tbsp cornstarch, 1 tsp salt, and 2 3/4 cups thick coconut milk in a mixing bowl, strain into a pot, and cook over medium heat until slightly thickened. 3. Remove from heat, gently fold in the cendol, pour into an 8x8-inch pan, and cook over a rack in a covered pot of boiling water for 25 minutes. 4. For the top layer, whisk the eggs, all-purpose flour, 2 tbsp cornstarch, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 1/2 cups coconut milk, and 1 cup cooled palm sugar syrup, strain into a saucepan, and heat gently until steaming. 5. Pour the top mixture over the set cendol layer, cover the pot with a cloth-wrapped lid, and cook for 25 to 30 minutes (uncovering for the final 5 minutes to dry the surface), then cool for at least 2 hours before slicing.

name: Lepat Cendol (Coconut Cendol Pudding Parcels)
ingredients: 5 cups diluted coconut milk (1 small box coconut milk mixed with 4 cups water)
Banana leaves (softened over low heat, for wrapping)
instructions: 1. Whisk the cornstarch, diluted coconut milk, sugar, and salt together in a saucepan until smooth. 2. Cook over medium heat while stirring continuously until thick and bubbling. 3. Turn off the heat, let the mixture cool slightly until warm, and gently fold in the cendol until evenly distributed. 4. Spoon the mixture onto softened banana leaves (resting on a plate) and fold into neat parcels, or transfer into small molds. 5. Chill in the refrigerator until completely firm before serving.

name: Gula Melaka Cendol Pudding (Puding Cendol)
ingredients: 15 g agar-agar strips (half of a 30 g pack, for cendol layer)
1 1/4 small boxes coconut milk (about 250 ml, for cendol layer)
15 g agar-agar strips (remaining half of 30 g pack, for gula Melaka layer)
1 block gula Melaka (boiled with 300 ml water)
3/4 small box coconut milk (about 150 ml, for gula Melaka layer)
Pinch of salt (for gula Melaka layer)
instructions: 1. Boil 15 g agar-agar strips in 1 liter water in a pot until completely dissolved, then stir in sugar until dissolved. 2. Add 1 1/4 boxes coconut milk and 1 knotted pandan leaf, stir well, then mix in the cendol and a pinch of salt briefly without letting it boil. 3. Discard the pandan leaf, pour into a lightly wetted mold, and let cool until partially set. 4. Boil the remaining 15 g agar-agar strips in 1 liter water until dissolved, then stir in the melted gula Melaka syrup, 3/4 box coconut milk, remaining pandan leaf, and a pinch of salt and bring to a boil. 5. Lightly score the surface of the partially set cendol layer, gently pour the gula Melaka mixture on top, and chill in the refrigerator for several hours until firm before slicing.
